fact: Highest point of Belgium. Signal de Botrange is the highest point in Wallonia and Belgium, located in the High Fens, at 694 metres (2,277 feet). It is the top of a broad plateau and a road crosses the summit, passing an adjacent café.

title: Zla Kolata
fact: Highest point of Montenegro: 2,534 m above sea level. Zla Kolata or Kollata e Keqe is one of the highest peaks of the Accursed Mountains, on the border of Albania and Montenegro.

title: Beqaa Valley
fact: The Beqaa Valley is a fertile valley in eastern Lebanon and its most important farming region. Industry, especially the country's agricultural industry, also flourishes in Beqaa. The region broadly corresponds to the Coele-Syria of classical antiquity.

title: Białowieża Forest
fact: Białowieża Forest is a large forest complex and World Heritage Area straddling the border between Poland and Belarus. It is one of the last and the largest remaining parts of the immense primeval forest that once stretched across the European Plain.

title: Lake Zurich
fact: Lake Zurich is a lake in Switzerland, that extends southeast of the city of Zurich. Depending on the context, Lake Zurich or Zürichsee may refer to the entire lake or specifically to the section downstream of the Hurden peninsula and Seedamm causeway.

title: Tonle Sap
fact: Tonle Sap is a lake in central Cambodia. Belonging to the Mekong river system, Tonle Sap is the largest freshwater lake in Southeast Asia and one of the most diverse and productive ecosystems in the world.

title: Grand Canyon National Park
fact: National park since 1919, 4,863 km². Grand Canyon National Park is a national park of the United States located in northwestern Arizona, the 15th site to have been named as a national park.

title: Lake Manasarovar
fact: Lake Manasarovar also called Mapam Yumtso, is a high altitude freshwater lake near Mount Kailash in Burang County, Ngari Prefecture, Tibet Autonomous Region, China. It is located at an elevation of 4,600 m (15,100 ft), near the western trijunction between China, India and Nepal.

title: Gjeravica
fact: Highest point of Kosovo: 2,656 m above sea level. Gjeravica is a mountain peak in Kosovo. It also is the second-highest mountain peak in the Accursed Mountains range and the Dinaric Alps range, after Jezercë. It has an elevation of 2,656 m (8,714 ft) above sea level.

title: Maglić (mountain)
fact: Highest point of Bosnia and Herzegovina: 2,386 m above sea level. Maglić is a transboundary mountain in the Dinaric Alps, on the border of Bosnia and Herzegovina and Montenegro. Its highest peak has an elevation of 2,388 m (7,835 ft) and is located in Montenegro.

title: Lake Inari
fact: Lake Inari is the largest lake in Sápmi and the third-largest lake in Finland. It is located in the northern part of Lapland, north of the Arctic Circle. The lake is 117–119 metres (384–390 ft) above sea level, and is regulated at the Kaitakoski power plant in Russia.

title: Los Glaciares National Park
fact: National park since 1937, 4,459 km². Los Glaciares National Park is a federal protected area in Santa Cruz Province, Argentina. The park covers an area of 726,927 ha (7,269.27 km2; 2,806.68 sq mi), making it the largest national park in the country.

title: Northeast Greenland National Park
fact: National park since 1974, 972,000 km². Northeast Greenland National Park is the world's largest national park and the 10th largest protected area (the only larger protected areas consist mostly of sea).

title: Mount Saint Elias
fact: 5,500 m above sea level. Mount Saint Elias (Was'eitushaa, also designated Boundary Peak 186) is an 18,008 foot (5,489 m) mountain located approximately 11 miles (18 km) northeast of the Pacific Ocean on the Yukon-Alaska border.

title: Chogolisa
fact: 7,668 m above sea level. Chogolisa is a trapezoidal mountain located in the Karakoram range within the Gilgit-Baltistan region of Pakistan. It is situated near the Baltoro Glacier in the Concordia region, which is renowned for hosting some of the world's tallest peaks.

title: Maromokotro
fact: Highest point of Madagascar: 2,876 m above sea level. Maromokotro or Maromokotra is a volcano in Madagascar. At 2,876 meters (9,436 ft), it is the highest peak on the island.

title: Muztagh Tower
fact: 7,273 m above sea level. Muztagh Tower, also Mustagh Tower; Muztagh: icy mountain, is a mountain situated in Baltoro Muztagh, which is a segment of the Karakoram range.

title: Peak Ozodi
fact: 7,105 m above sea level. Ozodi Peak or until 2020 Korzhenevskoi Peak, is the third highest peak in the Pamir Mountains of Tajikistan. It is one of the five "Snow Leopard Peaks" in the territory of the former Soviet Union.

title: Saser Kangri
fact: 7,672 m above sea level. Saser Kangri (or Sasir Kangri) is a mountain in India. It is the highest peak in the Saser Muztagh, the easternmost subrange of the Karakoram range. Sasir Kangri is located within Ladakh.

title: Volcán Tajumulco
fact: Highest point of Guatemala: 4,220 m above sea level. Volcán Tajumulco is a large stratovolcano in the department of San Marcos in western Guatemala. It is the highest mountain in Central America at 4,203 metres (13,789 ft).

title: Chitwan National Park
fact: National park since 1973, 932 km². Chitwan National Park is the first national park of Nepal and was established in 1973 as Royal Chitwan National Park. It was granted the status of a World Heritage Site in 1984.

title: Lake Lucerne
fact: Lake Lucerne is a lake in central Switzerland and the fourth largest in the country.

title: Comoé National Park
fact: National park since 1968, 11,492 km². The Comoé National Park is a Biosphere Reserve and UNESCO World Heritage Site in the Zanzan and Savanes districts of north-eastern Ivory Coast.

title: Garamba National Park
fact: National park since 1938, 4,920 km². Garamba National Park is a national park in the north-eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo covering nearly 5,200 km2 (2,000 sq mi).

title: Lake Prespa
fact: The Lake Prespa is located on the tripoint of North Macedonia, Albania and Greece. It is a system of two lakes separated by an isthmus: the Great Prespa Lake, divided among the three countries, and the Little Prespa Lake, mostly within Greece.

title: Lake Trasimeno
fact: Lake Trasimene, is a lake in the province of Perugia, in the Umbria region of Italy on the border with Tuscany. The lake has a surface area of 128 km2 (49.4 sq mi), making it the fourth largest in Italy, slightly smaller than Lake Como.

title: Monument Valley
fact: Monument Valley is a region of the Colorado Plateau characterized by a cluster of sandstone buttes, with the largest reaching 1,000 ft (300 m) above the valley floor. The most famous butte formations are located in northeastern Arizona along the Utah–Arizona state line.

title: Sagarmatha National Park
fact: National park since 1976, 1,148 km². Sagarmāthā National Park is a national park in the Himalayas of eastern Nepal that was established in 1976 and encompasses an area of 1,148 km2 (443 sq mi) in the Solukhumbu District.

title: West Lake
fact: West Lake, also known as Xihu and by other names, is a freshwater lake in Hangzhou, China.

title: Mount Richard-Molard
fact: Highest point of Ivory Coast: 1,752 m above sea level. Mount Richard-Molard is a mountain along the border of Guinea, Ivory Coast and Liberia in West Africa. The summit is on the border of Guinea and Ivory Coast and is the highest peak for both countries at 1,752 m (5,748 ft).

title: Niulakita
fact: Highest point of Tuvalu: 5 m above sea level. Niulakita is the southernmost island of Tuvalu, and also the name of the only village on this island. Niulakita has a population of 36 (2022 Census). The residents of Niulakita have moved to the island from Niutao.

title: Batura Sar
fact: 7,795 m above sea level. Batura Sar, also referred to as Batura I, is the 25th-highest mountain on Earth. Located in Passu (Gojal Valley) in the Hunza District of Gilgit-Baltistan region in northern Pakistan, it is the highest peak of the Batura Muztagh…

title: Changtse
fact: 7,543 m above sea level. Changtse is a mountain situated between the Main Rongbuk and East Rongbuk Glaciers in Tibet Autonomous Region, China, immediately north of Mount Everest.

title: Kunyang Chhish
fact: 7,852 m above sea level. Kunyang Chhish is the second-highest mountain in the Hispar Muztagh, a subrange in the Karakoram mountains in Pakistan. Alternative variations of the name are Kunyang Kish and Khinyang Chhish.

title: Lake Khanka
fact: Lake Khanka or Lake Xingkai, is a freshwater lake on the border between Primorsky Krai, Russia and Heilongjiang province, Northeast China.

title: Salonga National Park
fact: National park since 1970, 36,000 km². Salonga National Park is a national park in the Democratic Republic of the Congo located in the Congo River basin. It is Africa's largest tropical rainforest reserve covering about 36,000 km2 or 3,600,000 hectares (8,900,000 acres).

title: Cerro Chirripó
fact: Highest point of Costa Rica: 3,820 m above sea level. Cerro Chirripó is the highest mountain in Costa Rica, with an elevation of 3,821 meters (12,536 feet). It is part of the Cordillera de Talamanca, and the mountain range's highest point.

title: Mount Catherine
fact: Highest point of Egypt: 2,629 m above sea level. Mount Saint Catherine is the highest mountain in Egypt. It is located near the town of Saint Catherine in the South Sinai Governorate.

title: Areopagus
fact: The Areopagus was a principal council of ancient Athens, later serving mainly as a judicial body responsible for cases of homicide, wounding, and certain religious offenses.

title: Canaima National Park
fact: National park since 1962, 28,645 km². Canaima National Park is a 30,000 km2 (12,000 sq mi) park in south-eastern Venezuela that roughly occupies the same area as the Gran Sabana region. It is located in Bolívar State, reaching the borders with Brazil and Guyana.

title: Chiemsee
fact: Chiemsee is a freshwater lake in Bavaria, Germany, near Rosenheim. It is often called "the Bavarian Sea". The rivers Tiroler Achen and Prien flow into the lake from the south, and the river Alz flows out towards the north.

title: Glacier National Park (U.S.)
fact: National park since 1910, 4,100 km². Glacier National Park is a national park of the United States located in northwestern Montana, on the Canada–United States border.

title: Kinabalu Park
fact: Kinabalu Park, established as one of the first national parks of Malaysia in 1964, is Malaysia's first World Heritage Site designated by UNESCO in December 2000 for its "outstanding universal values" and the role as one of the most important biological sites in the world with…

title: Lake Athabasca
fact: Lake Athabasca is in the north-west corner of Saskatchewan and the north-east corner of Alberta between 58° and 60° N in Canada. The lake is about 26% in Alberta and 74% in Saskatchewan.

title: Wachau
fact: The Wachau is an Austrian valley formed by the Danube River. It is one of the most prominent tourist destinations of Lower Austria, located between the towns of Melk and Krems that attracts epicureans for its high-quality wines.

title: Chomo Lonzo
fact: 7,804 m above sea level. Chomo Lonzo is a mountain in Tibet, 5 km northeast of Makalu in the Mahalungur (Mohalingor) or Khumbu Himalayas. Alternate spellings of the same name include Chomolonzo, Chomolönzo, Chomo Lönzo, Jomolönzo, and Lhamalangcho.

title: Kumbhakarna Mountain
fact: 7,711 m above sea level. Mount Kumbhakarna or Jannu is the 32nd-highest mountain in the world. It is an important western outlier of Kangchenjunga, the world's third-highest peak.

title: Langtang Lirung
fact: 7,227 m above sea level. Langtang Lirung is the highest peak of the Langtang Himal, which is a subrange of the Nepalese Himalayas, southwest of the Eight-thousander Shishapangma. It is listed as the 99th highest mountain in the world.

title: Ngadi Chuli
fact: 7,871 m above sea level. Ngadi Chuli is a mountain in the Mansiri Himal (or Manaslu Himal), also known as the Gurkha Massif, in Nepal. With an elevation of 7,871 metres (25,823 ft) above sea level, it is the 20th-highest mountain on Earth.

title: Elephanta Caves
fact: The Elephanta Caves form a collection of cave temples predominantly dedicated to the Hindu god Shiva; UNESCO has designated them as a World Heritage Site.

title: Kahuzi-Biéga National Park
fact: National park since 1970, 6,000 km². The Kahuzi-Biega National Park is a protected area near Bukavu town in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo. It is situated near the western bank of Lake Kivu and the Rwandan border.

title: Keoladeo National Park
fact: National park since 1971, 29 km². Keoladeo National Park, or Keoladeo Ghana National Park, is a national park in Rajasthan, India.

title: Lake Neuchâtel
fact: Lake Neuchâtel lies primarily in Romandy, the French-speaking part of Switzerland. The lake lies mainly in the canton of Neuchâtel, but is also shared by the cantons of Vaud, Fribourg, and Bern.

title: Doi Inthanon
fact: Highest point of Thailand: 2,565 m above sea level. Doi Inthanon is the highest mountain in Thailand. It is in Chom Thong District, Chiang Mai Province.

title: Grauspitz
fact: Highest point of Liechtenstein: 2,599 m above sea level. The Grauspitz (Vorder Grauspitze or Vorder Grauspitz on some maps) is a mountain in the Rätikon range of the Alps, located on the border between Liechtenstein and Switzerland.

title: Jebel Shams
fact: Highest point of Oman: 3,018 m above sea level. Jabal Shams or Jebel Shams is a mountain located in northeastern Oman north of the town of Al-Hamra.

title: Mount Moco
fact: Highest point of Angola: 2,619 m above sea level. Mount Moco, at 2,620 metres (8,600 ft), is the highest mountain in Angola. It is located in Huambo Province in the western part of the country, 70 kilometres (43 mi) west of the city of Huambo.

title: Pidurutalagala
fact: Highest point of Sri Lanka. Pidurutalagala, or previously Mount Pedro in English, is the highest mountain in Sri Lanka, at 2,524 m (8,281 ft). It is situated North-North-East from the town of Nuwara Eliya and is easily visible from most areas of the Central Province.

title: Great Sandy Desert
fact: The Great Sandy Desert is an interim Australian bioregion, located in the northeast of Western Australia straddling the Pilbara and southern Kimberley regions and extending east into the Northern Territory.

title: Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park
fact: National park since 1916, 879 km². Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park is a national park of the United States, located on the island of Hawaiʻi in the state of Hawaii.

title: Kashmir Valley
fact: The Kashmir Valley, also known as the Vale of Kashmir, is an intermontane valley or basin in the northern part of Indian-administered Jammu and Kashmir.

title: Lake Skadar
fact: Lake Skadar or Lake Scutari – also called Lake Shkodra and Lake Shkodër – lies on the border of Albania and Montenegro, and is the largest lake in Southern Europe. A karst lake, it is named after the Albanian city of Shkodër which lies at its southeastern coast.

title: Manovo-Gounda St. Floris National Park
fact: National park since 1979, 17,400 km². Manovo-Gounda St Floris National Park is a national park and UNESCO World Heritage Site located in the Central African Republic prefecture Bamingui-Bangoran, near the Chad border.
story_label: Wikipedia: Manovo-Gounda St. Floris National Park

title: Olympic National Park
fact: National park since 1938, 3,734 km². Olympic National Park is a national park of the United States located in Washington, on the Olympic Peninsula.

title: Simien Mountains National Park
fact: National park since 1969, 136 km². Simien Mountains National Park is the largest national park in Ethiopia. Located in the North Gondar Zone of the Amhara Region, its territory covers the highest parts of the Simien Mountains and includes Ras Dashan…

title: W National Park
fact: National park since 1954, 10,183 km². The W National Park or W Regional Park is a major national park in West Africa around a meander in the Niger River shaped like the letter W. The park includes areas of the three countries Niger, Benin and Burkina Faso…

title: Kanjut Sar
fact: 7,760 m above sea level. Kanjut Sar is a mountain located between Shimshal Valley and Hisper Valley in the Karakoram mountain range. It is the 28th-highest mountain in the world. Kanjut is the native name of the Hunza valley while Sar means mountain peak in Burushaski.

title: Saltoro Kangri
fact: 7,742 m above sea level. Saltoro Kangri, previously known as Peak 36, stands as the highest peak within the Saltoro Mountains subrange, which is part of the larger Karakoram range. This subrange is also referred to as the Saltoro Range and is situated within the Karakoram region.

title: Khüiten Peak
fact: Highest point of Mongolia: 4,374 m above sea level. Khüiten Peak, also known in China as Friendship Peak, is a mountain peak in the Altai Range.

title: Møllehøj
fact: Highest point of Denmark: 171 m above sea level. Møllehøj is the highest natural point in Metropolitan Denmark at 170.86 m (560.6 ft).

title: Pico Turquino
fact: Highest point of Cuba: 1,974 m above sea level. Pico Turquino, sometimes erroneously spelled as Pico Torquino, is the highest point in Cuba.

title: Vatican Hill
fact: Highest point of Vatican City: 75 m above sea level. Vatican Hill is a hill in Rome, located on the right bank (west side) of Tiber river, opposite to the traditional seven hills of Rome. The hill also gave the name to Vatican City. It is the location of St. Peter's Basilica.

title: Loch Lomond
fact: Loch Lomond is a freshwater Scottish loch that spans the Highland Boundary Fault, often considered the boundary between the Lowlands and Highlands of Scotland.

title: Dongting Lake
fact: Dongting Lake is a large, shallow lake in northeastern Hunan Province, China. Also referred to less frequently as the Dongting Plain, it is a flood basin of the Yangtze River, so its volume depends on the season.

title: Garajonay National Park
fact: National park since 1981, 37 km². Garajonay National Park is located in the center and north of the island of La Gomera, one of the Canary Islands (Spain). It was declared a national park in 1981 and a World Heritage Site by UNESCO in 1986.

title: Lake Poopó
fact: Lake Poopó was a large saline lake in a shallow depression in the Altiplano in Oruro Department, Bolivia, at an altitude of approximately 3,700 m (12,100 ft).

title: Wood Buffalo National Park
fact: National park since 1922, 44,792 km². Wood Buffalo National Park is the largest national park of Canada at 44,741 km2 (17,275 sq mi). It is in northeastern Alberta and the southern Northwest Territories.

title: Kinyeti
fact: Highest point of South Sudan: 3,187 m above sea level. Mount Kinyeti is the highest peak in South Sudan. It is located in the Imatong Mountains in Ikotos County of Eastern Equatoria, near the Ugandan border. Kinyeti has an elevation of 3,187 metres (10,456 ft) above sea level.

title: Baintha Brakk
fact: Baintha Brakk or The Ogre is a steep, craggy mountain, 7,285 metres (23,901 ft) high, in the Panmah Muztagh, a subrange of the Karakoram mountain range. It is located in Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan.

title: Gurla Mandhata
fact: 7,694 m above sea level. Gurla Mandhata, also Naimona'nyi or Namu Nani, is the highest peak of the Nalakankar Himal, a small subrange of the Himalaya. It lies in Burang County of the Ngari Prefecture in the Tibet Autonomous Region of China, near the northwest corner of Nepal.

title: K12 (mountain)
fact: 7,428 m above sea level. K12 is the second highest peak in the Saltoro Mountains, a subrange of the Karakoram range in the Siachen region and is administered as a part of Ladakh territory.

title: Sabalan
fact: 4,811 m above sea level. Sabalan or Savalan is an inactive stratovolcano in northwestern Iran located in Ardabil province. At 4,811 metres (15,784 ft) above sea level, it is the third-highest mountain in Iran. A permanent crater lake has formed at its summit.

title: Doñana National Park
fact: National park since 1969, 543 km². Doñana National Park or Parque Nacional y Natural de Doñana is a natural reserve in Andalusia, southern Spain, in the provinces of Huelva (most of its territory within the municipality of Almonte), Cádiz and Seville.

title: Grand Teton National Park
fact: National park since 1929, 1,255 km². Grand Teton National Park is a national park of the United States in northwestern Wyoming.

title: Jaú National Park
fact: National park since 1980, 23,779 km². The Jaú National Park is a national park located in the state of Amazonas, Brazil. It is one of the largest forest reserves in South America, and part of a World Heritage Site.

title: Lake Ilmen
fact: Lake Ilmen is a large lake in Novgorod Oblast, Russia. A historically important lake, it formed a vital part of the medieval trade route from the Varangians to the Greeks.

title: Lough Neagh
fact: Lake, 392 km², 25 m deep. Lough Neagh is a freshwater lake in Northern Ireland and is the largest lake on the island of Ireland and in the British Isles. It has a surface area of 148 square miles (383 square kilometres) and is about 19 miles (31 km) long and 9 miles (14 km) wide.

title: Rocas Atoll
fact: The Rocas Atoll is the only atoll in the South Atlantic Ocean. It belongs to the Brazilian State of Rio Grande do Norte. It is located approximately 260 km (160 mi) northeast of Natal and 145 km (90 mi) west of the Fernando de Noronha archipelago.

title: Taï National Park
fact: National park since 1972, 3,300 km². Taï National Park is a national park in Ivory Coast that contains one of the last areas of primary rainforest in West Africa. It was inscribed as a World Heritage Site in 1982 due to the diversity of its flora and fauna.

title: Aneto
fact: Aneto is the highest mountain in the Pyrenees and in Aragon, Spain's third-highest mountain, reaching a height of 3,404 metres (11,168 feet).

title: Bălănești Hill
fact: Highest point of Moldova. Bălănești Hill is the highest geographical point in Moldova, with an altitude of 430 metres (1,410 ft) (429 metres; 1,407 ft according to some sources). It is located in Bălănești and belongs to the Cornești Hills.

title: Blue Mountain Peak
fact: Highest point of Jamaica. Blue Mountain Peak is Jamaica's highest mountain, rising to 2,256 metres (7,402 ft), and is the tallest peak in the Caribbean outside of Hispaniola. It is the home of Blue Mountain coffee.

title: Tatamailau
fact: Highest point of Timor-Leste. Tatamailau (Tetum: Foho Tatamailau), or Tata Mailau, also Mount Ramelau, is the highest point in Timor-Leste and also of Timor island at 2,963 m (9,721 ft).

title: Aokigahara
fact: Aokigahara, also known as the Sea of Trees (樹海, Jukai), is a forest on the northwestern flank of Mount Fuji on the island of Honshu in Japan, thriving on 30 square kilometres (12 sq mi) of hardened lava laid down by the last major eruption of Mount Fuji in 864 CE.

title: Arches National Park
fact: National park since 1971, 354 km². Arches National Park is a national park of the United States in eastern Utah. The park is adjacent to the Colorado River, 4 mi (6 km) north of Moab, Utah.

title: Great Smoky Mountains National Park
fact: National park since 1934, 2,114 km². Great Smoky Mountains National Park is a national park of the United States in the southeast, with parts in North Carolina and Tennessee.
story_label: Wikipedia: Great Smoky Mountains National Park

title: Jasper National Park
fact: National park since 1907, 10,878 km². Jasper National Park, in Alberta, Canada, is the largest national park within Alberta's Rocky Mountains, spanning 11,000 km2 (4,200 sq mi).

title: Lake Iseo
fact: Lake Iseo or Iseo lake, also known as Sebino, is the fourth largest lake in Lombardy, Italy, fed by the Oglio River. It is in the north of the country in the Val Camonica area, near the cities of Brescia and Bergamo.

title: Lake Tai
fact: Taihu, also known as Lake Tai or Lake Taihu, is a lake in the Yangtze Delta and the third largest freshwater lake in China. The lake is in Jiangsu province and a significant part of its southern shore forms its border with Zhejiang.

title: Manas National Park
fact: National park since 1990, 2,600 km². Manas National Park is a national park, Project Tiger reserve, and an elephant reserve in Assam, India. Located in the Himalayan foothills, it borders the Royal Manas National Park in Bhutan.

title: Nubian Desert
fact: The Nubian Desert is in the eastern region of the Sahara Desert, spanning approximately 400,000 km2 of northeastern Sudan and northern Eritrea, between the Nile and the Red Sea.

title: Chamlang
fact: 7,319 m above sea level. Chamlang is a mountain in the Nepalese Himalayas, near Makalu. It lies in the southern section of the Mahalangur subrange of the Himalayas. Chamlang has an elevation of 7,319 metres (24,012 ft).

title: Istor-o-Nal
fact: 7,389 m above sea level. Istor-o-Nal is the third highest mountain in the Hindu Kush range, in the Chitral District of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province in Pakistan. It is the 68th highest independent peak in the world.

title: Kabru
fact: 7,412 m above sea level. Kabru is a mountain in the Himalayas on the border of eastern Nepal and India. It is part of a ridge that extends south from the third highest mountain in the world, Kangchenjunga, and is the southernmost 7,000 metres (23,000 ft) peak in the world.

title: Saraghrar
fact: 7,338 m above sea level. Saraghrar is the fourth-highest independent peak in the Hindu Kush and located in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan.

title: Banc d'Arguin National Park
fact: National park since 1976, 12,000 km². The Banc d'Arguin National Park of Bay of Arguin lies in Western Africa on the west coast of Mauritania between Nouakchott and Nouadhibou and is the former mouth of the Tamanrasset River.

title: Lake Managua
fact: Lake Managua, also known as Lake Xolotlán, is a freshwater lake in Nicaragua. At 1,042 km², it is approximately 65 kilometres (40 mi) long and 25 kilometres (16 mi) wide.

title: Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park
fact: National park since 1971, 222 km². The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park is a protected area in the Philippines.
story_label: Wikipedia: Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park

title: Quebrada de Humahuaca
fact: The Quebrada de Humahuaca is a narrow mountain valley located in the province of Jujuy in northwest Argentina, 1,649 km (1,025 mi) north of Buenos Aires (23°11′59″S 65°20′56″W).

title: Teutoburg Forest
fact: The Teutoburg Forest is a range of low, forested hills in the German states of Lower Saxony and North Rhine-Westphalia. Until the 17th century, the official name of the hill ridge was Osning.

title: Virgin Komi Forests
fact: The Virgin Komi Forests is a natural UNESCO World Heritage Site in the Northern Ural Mountains of the Komi Republic, Russia. At 32,800 km2 it is the largest virgin forest in Europe.

title: Võrtsjärv
fact: Lake, 269 km², 3 m deep. Võrtsjärv is a lake in southern Estonia with an area of 270 km2 (100 sq mi). It is the second-largest lake in Estonia (after Lake Peipus), and it is the largest lake entirely within Estonia. The shallow lake is 33.7 m (111 ft) above sea level.

title: Aukštojas Hill
fact: Highest point of Lithuania: 294 m above sea level. Aukštojas Hill is the highest point of Lithuania. It is located in the Medininkai Highlands, Migūnai forestry, approximately 24 kilometres (15 mi) southeast of the capital city of Vilnius.

title: Boggy Peak
fact: Highest point of Antigua and Barbuda: 402 m above sea level. Boggy Peak is a mountain located in the southwest of Antigua, a constituent island of the archipelagic country of Antigua and Barbuda.

title: Jabal An-Nabi Shu'ayb
fact: Highest point of Yemen: 3,666 m above sea level. Jabal An-Nabī Shuʿayb, also called Jabal Hadhur, is a mountain in the Harazi subregion of the Sarawat, located in Bani Matar District, Sanaa Governorate, Yemen. It is the highest mountain in the country and the Arabian Peninsula.

title: Kneiff
fact: Highest point of Luxembourg: 560 m above sea level. Kneiff is a hill in the Ardennes, in the commune of Troisvierges, in northern Luxembourg, near the tripoint shared with Belgium and Germany.

title: Qurnat as Sawda'
fact: Highest point of Lebanon. Qurnat as Sawdā is the highest point in Lebanon and the Levant, at 3,088 m (10,131 ft) above sea level. It is the summit of Jabal al Makmel, a mountain range in Bsharri District, North Lebanon.

title: Bois de Boulogne
fact: The Bois de Boulogne is a large public park that is the western half of the 16th arrondissement of Paris, near the suburb of Boulogne-Billancourt and Neuilly-sur-Seine. The land was ceded to the city of Paris by the Emperor Napoleon III to be turned into a public park in 1852.

title: Engadin
fact: The Engadin or Engadine is a long high Alpine valley region in the eastern Swiss Alps in the canton of Graubünden in southeasternmost Switzerland with about 25,000 inhabitants.

title: Gibson Desert
fact: The Gibson Desert is a large desert in Western Australia, mainly in an almost pristine state. It is about 155,000 square kilometres (60,000 sq mi) in size, making it the fifth largest desert in Australia, after the Great Victoria, Great Sandy, Tanami and Simpson deserts.

title: Gunung Mulu National Park
fact: National park since 1974, 52,864 km². The Gunung Mulu National Park, also known simply as the Mulu National Park is a national park in Miri Division, Sarawak, Malaysia.

title: Namtso
fact: Namtso or Lake Nam (30°42′N 90°33′E), also referred to as Tengri Nor, is a mountain lake on the border between Damxung County of Lhasa prefecture-level city and Baingoin County of Nagqu Prefecture in the Tibet Autonomous Region of China…

title: Dykh-Tau
fact: 5,204 m above sea level. Dykh-Tau or Dykhtau, is the second-highest mountain in Russia and Europe with an elevation of 5,205 m (17,077 ft) above sea level. It is located in Kabardino-Balkaria, Russia; its peak standing about 5 km (3 mi) north of the border with Georgia.

title: Annapurna II
fact: 7,937 m above sea level. Annapurna II is the second-highest mountain of the Annapurna range located in Nepal, and the eastern anchor of the range.

title: Chihuahuan Desert
fact: The Chihuahuan Desert is a desert ecoregion designation covering parts of northern Mexico and the southwestern United States.

title: Fort Jesus
fact: National park 0 km². Fort Jesus, is a fort located on Mombasa Island. Designed by the Italian architect Giovanni Battista Cairati, it was built between 1593 and 1596 by order of King Felipe II of Spain, who also reigned as King Filipe I of Portugal and the Algarves…

title: Lake Starnberg
fact: Lake Starnberg or Starnberger See — called Lake Würm or Würmsee is Germany's fifth-largest lake by area; however, because of its great depth, it is the second-largest body of fresh water. It and its surroundings lie in three different Bavarian districts, or Landkreise.

title: Purnululu National Park
fact: National park since 1987, 2,397 km². The Purnululu National Park is a World Heritage Site in the East Kimberley region of Western Australia.

title: Valley of Flowers National Park
fact: Valley of Flowers National Park is an Indian national park which was established in 1982. It is located in Chamoli in the state of Uttarakhand and is known for its meadows of endemic alpine flowers and the variety of flora.
story_label: Wikipedia: Valley of Flowers National Park

title: Chappal Waddi
fact: Highest point of Nigeria. Chappal Waddi is located in Nigeria and, at 2,419 m (7,936 ft), is the country's highest point and the highest in West Africa. This peak, whose original and indigenous name is "Gang Peak" is steeped in enthralling ancient Mambilla mythologies.

title: Thabana Ntlenyana
fact: Highest point of Lesotho: 3,482 m above sea level. Thabana Ntlenyana is the highest mountain in southern Africa. It stands 3,482 metres (11,424 ft) tall within the Maloti Mountains that crest Lesotho.

title: Aralkum Desert
fact: The Aralkum Desert is a desert that has appeared since 1960 on the seabed once occupied by the Aral Sea. It lies to the south and east of what remains of the Eastern Basin Aral Sea in Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan. It is currently the youngest desert in the world.

title: Bois de Vincennes
fact: The Bois de Vincennes, located on the eastern edge of Paris, France, is the largest public park in the city. It was created between 1855 and 1866 by Emperor Napoleon III. The park is next to the Château de Vincennes, a former residence of the Kings of France.

title: Gehenna
fact: Gehenna or Gehinnom is a Biblical toponym that has acquired various theological connotations, including as a place of divine punishment, in Jewish eschatology.

title: Judaean Desert
fact: The Judaean Desert or Judean Desert is a desert in the West Bank and Israel that stretches east of the ridge of the Judaean Mountains and in their rain shadow, so east of Jerusalem, and descends to the Dead Sea.

title: Lake Champlain
fact: Lake Champlain is a large natural freshwater lake in North America. With a length of 107 mi (172 km) and surface area over 500 sq mi (1,295 km2), it lies mostly between the U.S. states of New York and Vermont, but also extends north into the Canadian province of Quebec.

title: Lake Ritsa
fact: Lake Ritsa is a lake in the north-western part of Abkhazia, in the Caucasus Mountains. It is surrounded by mixed mountain forests and subalpine meadows. The road from the Black Sea coast was built in 1936. The resort of Avadhara lies to the north of the lake.

title: Lake Taymyr
fact: Lake Taymyr is a lake of the central regions of the Taymyr Peninsula in Krasnoyarsk Krai, Russian Federation. It is located south of the Byrranga Mountains.

title: Lake Ülemiste
fact: Lake Ülemiste is the largest of the lakes surrounding Tallinn, Estonia. Ülemiste is the main part of the Tallinn water supply system, which supplies the city with most of its drinking water.

title: Lake Zaysan
fact: Lake Zaysan is a freshwater lake in Tarbagatay District, East Kazakhstan Region, Kazakhstan. It is the largest lake in the region. The lake is generally frozen from the beginning of November to the end of April, but still has an abundance of fish.

title: Nahanni National Park Reserve
fact: National park since 1976, 30,000 km². The Nahanni National Park Reserve, sometimes known as "Headless Valley" or "Valley of The Headless Men" (after a series of unsolved historical deaths in the park), in the Dehcho Region of the Northwest Territories…

title: Serra da Capivara National Park
fact: National park since 1979, 1,291 km². Serra da Capivara National Park is a national park in the Northeastern region of Brazil. The area has many prehistoric paintings.
story_label: Wikipedia: Serra da Capivara National Park

title: Tongariro National Park
fact: National park since 1887, 796 km². Tongariro National Park, located in the central North Island, is the oldest national park in New Zealand and the sixth national park established in the world.

title: Val d'Orcia
fact: The Val d'Orcia or Valdorcia is a region of Tuscany, Central Italy, which extends from the hills south of Siena to Monte Amiata, between the provinces of Siena and Grosseto.

title: Api (mountain)
fact: 7,132 m above sea level. Api, also known as Api Himal, is the highest peak in the Yoka Pahar section of the Gurans Himal, a subrange of the western Himalayas.

title: Trisul
fact: 7,120 m above sea level. Trisul or Trishul is a group of three Himalayan mountain peaks situated mainly in the Chamoli district (Garhwal), with its southern ridges extending into the Kumaon region of Uttarakhand, India. with the highest (Trisul I) reaching 7120m.

title: Yangra
fact: 7,422 m above sea level. Yangra (Ganesh I) is the highest peak of the Ganesh Himal, which is a subrange of the Himalayas. Although not an 8,000 metre peak, and little visited, it enjoys great vertical relief over the nearby valleys.

title: Mousa Ali
fact: Highest point of Djibouti: 2,028 m above sea level. Mousa Ali is a 2,021 metres (6,631 ft) stratovolcano located on the tri-point of Ethiopia, Eritrea and Djibouti. The volcano is the highest point in Djibouti.

title: Phnom Aural
fact: Highest point of Cambodia: 1,813 m above sea level. Phnom Aural, also spelled Phnom Aoral, is the tallest peak in Cambodia. It is 1,813 meters tall (other sources give elevations between 1,771 and 1,667 meters). It is in the eastern part of the Cardamom Mountains.

title: Pico de São Tomé
fact: Highest point of São Tomé and Príncipe. Pico de São Tomé is the highest mountain in São Tomé and Príncipe at 2,024 m (6,640 ft) elevation. It lies just west of the centre of São Tomé Island, in the Parque Natural Obô de São Tomé and in the Lembá District.

title: Ta' Dmejrek
fact: Highest point of Malta. Ta' Dmejrek is the highest point of Malta, located on the Dingli Cliffs, with an elevation of 253 metres (830 ft) above sea level.

title: Eastern Desert
fact: The Eastern Desert (known archaically as Arabia or the Arabian Desert) is the part of the Sahara Desert that is located east of the Nile River.

title: Gir National Park
fact: National park since 1965, 259 km². Gir National Park and Wildlife Sanctuary, also known as Sasan Gir, is a national park and wildlife sanctuary in Gujarat, India.

title: Gros Morne National Park
fact: National park since 2005, 1,805 km². Gros Morne National Park is a Canadian national park and World Heritage Site located on the west coast of Newfoundland.

title: Iron Gates
fact: The Iron Gates is a gorge on the river Danube. It forms part of the boundary between Serbia to the south and Romania to the north.

title: Lake Teletskoye
fact: Lake Teletskoye is the largest lake in the Altai Mountains and the Altai Republic, Russia, and has depth up to 325 meters.

title: Mývatn
fact: Mývatn is a shallow lake situated in an area of active volcanism in the north of Iceland, near Krafla volcano. It has a high amount of biological activity. The lake and the surrounding wetlands provide a habitat for a number of waterbirds, especially ducks.

title: Sangay National Park
fact: National park since 1979, 2,719 km². Sangay National Park is a national park located in the Morona-Santiago, Chimborazo, Tungurahua, Cañar, and Azuay provinces of Ecuador. The park contains two active volcanoes (Tungurahua and Sangay), one extinct volcano El Altar (Kapak Urku).

title: Sarygamysh Lake
fact: Sarygamysh Lake, also Sarykamysh or Sary-Kamysh, is the largest lake in Turkmenistan located about midway between the Caspian Sea and the Aral Sea. A quarter of the lake's area is in Uzbekistan.

title: Sequoia National Park
fact: National park since 1890, 1,635 km². Sequoia National Park is a national park of the United States in the southern Sierra Nevada east of Visalia, California.

title: Atafu
fact: Atafu, formerly known as the Duke of York Group, is a group of 52 coral islets within Tokelau in the south Pacific Ocean, 500 kilometres (270 nmi; 310 mi) north of Samoa.

title: Glacier Bay National Park and Preserve
fact: National park since 1980, 13,287 km². Glacier Bay National Park and Preserve is a national park of the United States located in Southeast Alaska west of Juneau.
story_label: Wikipedia: Glacier Bay National Park and Preserve

title: Jabal al-Nour
fact: Jabal al-Nour is a mountain near Mecca in the Hejaz region of Saudi Arabia. The mountain houses the grotto or cave of Hira.

title: Lake Biel
fact: Lake, 39 km², 74 m deep. Lake Biel or Lake Bienne is a lake in western Switzerland. Together with Lake Morat and Lake Neuchâtel, it is one of the three large lakes in the Jura region of Switzerland. It lies on the language boundary between German and French speaking areas.

title: Lake Chaubunagungamaug
fact: Lake Chaubunagungamaug, also known as Webster Lake, is a lake in the New England town of Webster, Massachusetts. The lake is located near the border with Connecticut and has a surface area of 1,442 acres (2.253 mi2).

title: Mana Pools National Park
fact: National park since 1975, 2,196 km². Mana Pools National Park is a 2,196-square-kilometre (848 sq mi) wildlife conservation area and national park in northern Zimbabwe.

title: Mjøsa
fact: Lake, 360 km², 453 m deep. Mjøsa is the largest lake in Norway and the fourth deepest in Norway and Europe. It is located in the southern part of Norway, about 100 kilometres (62 mi) north of the city of Oslo.

title: Vienna Woods
fact: The Vienna Woods are forested highlands that form the northeastern foothills of the Northern Limestone Alps in the states of Lower Austria and Vienna.

title: Beerenberg
fact: 2,277 m above sea level. Beerenberg is a stratovolcano dominating the northeastern end of the Norwegian island of Jan Mayen. It is 2,277 m (7,470 ft) high and is the world's northernmost subaerial active volcano and the only active volcano in Norway.

title: Brandberg Mountain
fact: Highest point of Namibia: 2,573 m above sea level. The Brandberg is Namibia's highest mountain.

title: Bukit Timah Hill
fact: Highest point of Singapore: 164 m above sea level. Bukit Timah Hill is the highest natural peak in Singapore. It is located in Bukit Panjang rather than its namesake district and its altitude is 164 metres (538 feet) above sea level.

title: Jebel ech Chambi
fact: Highest point of Tunisia: 1,544 m above sea level. Jebel ech Chambi is a mountain peak in Tunisia. At an elevation of 1,544 m (5,066 ft), it is the highest mountain in the country. It stands above the city of Kasserine in western central Tunisia.

title: Morne Diablotins
fact: Highest point of Dominica: 1,447 m above sea level. Morne Diablotins is the highest mountain on the Caribbean island of Dominica, and the island's largest and highest volcano. It is the second highest mountain in the Lesser Antilles.

title: Mount Hombori
fact: Highest point of Mali: 1,153 m above sea level. Mount Hombori (Hombori Tondo) is a mountain in Mali's Mopti Region, near the town of Hombori. At 1,155 meters, it is the highest point in Mali.

title: Mount Nyangani
fact: Highest point of Zimbabwe. Mount Nyangani is the highest mountain in Zimbabwe at 2,592 metres or 8,504 feet. The mountain is located within Nyanga National Park in Nyanga District, about 110 km (68 mi) north-northeast of Mutare.

title: Silisili
fact: Highest point of Samoa: 1,858 m above sea level. Mount Silisili is the highest peak in Samoa and the Samoa Islands chain. It is located in the centre of a mountain chain running the length of Savai'i island. Mount Silisili is ranked 24th by topographic isolation.

title: Baltoro Kangri
fact: 7,312 m above sea level. Baltoro Kangri is a mountain of the Karakoram mountain range in Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan. Baltoro Kangri is the 82nd highest mountain in the world with an elevation of 7,312 metres (23,990 ft).

title: Diran
fact: 7,266 m above sea level. Diran is a mountain in the Karakoram range in Bagrot Valley, Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan. This 7,266-metre (23,839 ft), pyramid-shaped mountain lies to the east of Rakaposhi (7,788m).

title: Sia Kangri
fact: Sia Kangri (7,422 m, 24,350 ft) is a mountain in the Baltoro Muztagh in the Karakoram. Its summit lies on the border of Pakistan and China. About a kilometer southeast of the Sia Kangri summit is the tri point where territories controlled by India, Pakistan and China meet.

title: Skil Brum
fact: 7,410 m above sea level. Skil Brum, or Skilbrum, is a mountain in the Karakoram range in Gilgit–Baltistan, Pakistan, approximately 9 km (5 mi) west-southwest of K2. It lies on the western side of the Godwin-Austen Glacier, roughly opposite Broad Peak.

title: Trivor
fact: 7,577 m above sea level. Trivor is one of the high mountain peaks of the Hispar Muztagh, a subrange of the Karakoram range in the Shimshal Valley, Gilgit-Baltistan of Pakistan.

title: Danakil Desert
fact: The Danakil Desert (or Afar Desert) is a desert in northeast Ethiopia, southern Eritrea, and northwestern Djibouti. Situated in the Afar Triangle, it stretches across 136,956 square kilometres (52,879 mi2) of arid terrain. It is inhabited by a few Afar, who engage in salt mining.

title: Noel Kempff Mercado National Park
fact: National park since 1979, 7,500 km². Noel Kempff Mercado National Park is a national park in northeast Santa Cruz Department, Province of José Miguel de Velasco, Bolivia, on the border with Brazil.
story_label: Wikipedia: Noel Kempff Mercado National Park

title: Rocky Mountain National Park
fact: National park since 1915, 1,076 km². Rocky Mountain National Park is a national park of the United States located approximately 55 mi (89 km) northwest of Denver in north-central Colorado, within the Front Range of the Rocky Mountains.

title: Ténéré
fact: The Ténéré is a desert region in south central Sahara. It comprises a vast plain of sand stretching from northeastern Niger to western Chad, occupying an area of over 400,000 square kilometres (150,000 sq mi).

title: Valtellina
fact: Valtellina, or the Valtelline (English, occasionally spelled as Val Telline), is a valley in the Lombardy region of northern Italy, bordering Switzerland.

title: Hoher Dachstein
fact: 2,995 m above sea level. Hoher Dachstein is a strongly karstic mountain in central Austria and the second-highest mountain in the Northern Limestone Alps. It is situated at the border of Upper Austria and Styria, and is the highest point in each of those states.

title: Piton des Neiges
fact: 3,070 m above sea level. The Piton des Neiges (Snow Peak) is a 3,069 m (10,069 ft) complex volcano on Réunion, one of the French volcanic islands in the Mascarene Archipelago in the southwestern Indian Ocean. It is located about 800 kilometres (500 mi) east of Madagascar.

title: Cheekha Dar
fact: Highest point of Iraq: 3,611 m above sea level. Cheekha Dar, which means Black Tent, is the local Kurdish name for the mountain, located in Kurdistan Region of Iraq, currently thought to be the highest in Iraq.

title: Monte Binga
fact: Highest point of Mozambique: 2,436 m above sea level. Monte Binga is the highest mountain in Mozambique and the second-highest in Zimbabwe. It is located in the Chimanimani Mountains, straddling the border of Zimbabwe and Mozambique in the Chimanimani Transfrontier Park in…

title: Mount Agou
fact: Highest point of Togo. Mount Agou is the highest mountain in Togo at 986 metres (3,235 ft). It is situated to the south east of Kpalimé in the Plateaux Region of Togo. The mountain lies close to the border with Ghana; this country can be seen from the summit.

title: Mount Liamuiga
fact: Highest point of Saint Kitts and Nevis. Mount Liamuiga is a 1,156-metre (3,792 ft) stratovolcano which forms the north-western part of the island of Saint Kitts.

title: Pico Duarte
fact: Highest point of Dominican Republic: 3,101 m above sea level. Pico Duarte is the highest peak in the Dominican Republic, on the island of Hispaniola and in all the Caribbean.

title: Alejandro de Humboldt National Park
fact: National park since 2001, 711 km². Alejandro de Humboldt National Park is a national park in the Cuban provinces of Holguín and Guantánamo. It is named after the German scientist Alexander von Humboldt who visited the island in 1800 and 1801.
story_label: Wikipedia: Alejandro de Humboldt National Park

title: Canyonlands National Park
fact: National park since 1964, 1,366 km². Canyonlands National Park is a national park of the United States located in southeastern Utah near the town of Moab.

title: Central Valley (California)
fact: The Central Valley is a broad, elongated, flat valley that dominates the interior of California, United States. It is 40–60 mi (60–100 km) wide and runs approximately 450 mi (720 km) from north-northwest to south-southeast, inland from and parallel to the Pacific coast.

title: Chapada dos Veadeiros National Park
fact: National park since 1961, 2,406 km². Chapada dos Veadeiros National Park is a national park of Brazil located in the state of Goiás, on the top of an ancient plateau with an estimated age of 1.8 billion years.
story_label: Wikipedia: Chapada dos Veadeiros National Park

title: Wrangell–St. Elias National Park and Preserve
fact: National park since 1980, 33,683 km². Wrangell–St. Elias National Park and Preserve is a United States national park and preserve in south central Alaska.
story_label: Wikipedia: Wrangell–St. Elias National Park and Preserve

title: Gran Paradiso
fact: 4,061 m above sea level. The Gran Paradiso or Grand Paradis is a mountain in the Graian Alps in Italy, located between the Aosta Valley and Piedmont regions. It is located in Gran Paradiso National Park.

title: Baruntse
fact: 7,129 m above sea level. Baruntse is a mountain in the Khumbu region of eastern Nepal, crowned by four peaks and bounded on the south by the Hunku Glacier, on the east by the Barun Glacier, and on the northwest by the Imja Glacier.

title: Haramosh Peak
fact: 7,406 m above sea level. Haramosh Peak, also known as Haramosh or Peak 58, is a Karakoram range mountain located in Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan.

title: Mount Fairweather
fact: 4,653 m above sea level. Mount Fairweather is a mountain located 20 km (12 mi) east of the Pacific Ocean on the Canada–United States border.

title: Passu Sar
fact: 7,478 m above sea level. Passu Sar is a mountain peak in the Batura Muztagh, a sub-range of the Karakoram mountain range, in the Hunza District of Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan. It is the high point of the Passu massif, which also includes Passu Diar (or "Passu East", "Pasu II").

title: Amboseli National Park
fact: National park since 1974, 392 km². Amboseli National Park, formerly Maasai Amboseli Game Reserve, is a national park in Loitoktok District in Kajiado County, Kenya.

title: Badlands National Park
fact: National park since 1939, 982 km². Badlands National Park is a national park of the United States in southwestern South Dakota.

title: Band-e Amir National Park
fact: National park since 2009, 590 km². Band-e Amir National Park is located in the central Bamyan Province of Afghanistan. It was established on 22 May 2009 as Afghanistan's first national park to promote and protect the natural beauty of a series of intensely blue lakes created by…

title: Batu Caves
fact: Batu Caves are a series of limestone caves in Gombak, Selangor, Malaysia. It is located on a 325 m (1,066 ft)–tall mogote, about 13 km (8.1 mi) north of the Malaysian capital of Kuala Lumpur.

title: Błędów Desert
fact: Błędów Desert, is an area of sands and gravels located between Błędów and the villages of Chechło and Klucze in Poland. The area lies mainly on the Silesian Highlands in the Lesser Poland Voivodeship.

title: Iguaçu National Park
fact: National park since 1939, 1,654 km². Iguaçu National Park is a national park in Paraná State, Brazil. It comprises a total area of 185,262.5 hectares (457,794 acres) and a length of about 420 kilometers (260 mi)…

title: Jim Corbett National Park
fact: National park since 1936, 1,288 km². Jim Corbett National Park is a national park in the Nainital district of the state of Uttarakhand, India.

title: Kluane National Park and Reserve
fact: National park since 1972, 21,980 km². Kluane National Park and Reserve are two protected areas in the southwest corner of the territory of Yukon. The National Park Reserve was set aside in 1972 to become a national park, pending settlement of First Nations land claims.
story_label: Wikipedia: Kluane National Park and Reserve

title: Los Katíos National Park
fact: National park since 1974, 720 km². Los Katíos National Natural Park is a protected area located in northwest Colombia which covers about 720 km2 (280 sq mi). The elevation ranges between 50 and 600 m (160 and 1,970 ft).

title: Mount Kenya National Park
fact: National park since 1949, 2,023 km². Mount Kenya National Park is a national park in Kenya that was established in 1949 around Mount Kenya to protect its surrounding environment and wildlife. It is also a drainage basin for the region's water supply.

title: Nairobi National Park
fact: National park since 1946, 117 km². Nairobi National Park is a national park in Kenya that was established in 1946 about 7 km (4.3 mi) south of Nairobi.

title: Nanumea
fact: Nanumea is the northwesternmost atoll in the Polynesian nation of Tuvalu, a group of nine coral atolls and islands spread over about 400 miles (640 km) of the Pacific Ocean just south of the equator and west of the International Date Line.

title: San Fernando Valley
fact: The San Fernando Valley, known locally as the Valley, is an urbanized valley in Los Angeles County, California.

title: Tatra National Park, Slovakia
fact: National park since 1949, 738 km². Tatra(s) National Park is one of the nine national parks in Slovakia. It is situated in North Central Slovakia in the Tatra Mountains.

title: Finsteraarhorn
fact: The Finsteraarhorn (4,274 m; 14,022 ft) is a mountain lying on the border between the cantons of Bern and Valais. It is the highest mountain of the Bernese Alps and the most prominent peak of Switzerland.

title: Jezercë
fact: Jezercë (Albanian definite form: Jezerca) is the highest peak in the Dinaric Alps, the second highest in Albania and sixth highest in Southeast Europe, standing at 2,694 m (8,839 ft) above sea level.

title: Piz Bernina
fact: 4,048 m above sea level. Piz Bernina is the highest mountain in the Eastern Alps, the highest point of the Bernina Range, and the highest peak in the Rhaetian Alps.

title: Emlembe
fact: Highest point of Eswatini: 1,862 m above sea level. Emlembe is the highest mountain in the African country of Eswatini. It is located in the east uKhahlamba (or Drakensberg) mountain range, on the border with South Africa.

title: Mount Bintumani
fact: Highest point of Sierra Leone. Mount Bintumani is the highest peak in Sierra Leone and the Loma Mountains, at 1,945 metres (6,381 ft). It lies in the Loma Mountains and its lower slopes are covered in rainforests, home to a wide variety of animals.

title: Mount Gimie
fact: Highest point of Saint Lucia: 952 m above sea level. Mount Gimie is the tallest mountain on the island of Saint Lucia. It is located in the Canaries District on the west side of Saint Lucia. The mountain's peak reaches 950 m (3,120 ft).

title: Mount Tenakourou
fact: Highest point of Burkina Faso: 749 m above sea level. Mount Tenakourou is the highest point in Burkina Faso. It is a hill situated on the border of the Cascades Region of Burkina Faso and the Sikasso Region of the country of Mali, not far from the source of the Black Volta.

title: Białowieża National Park
fact: National park since 1932, 105 km². Białowieża National Park is a national park in Podlaskie Voivodeship, in Eastern Poland adjacent to the border with Belarus. The total area of the park is 105.2 square kilometres (40.6 sq mi).

title: Emas National Park
fact: National park since 1961, 1,328 km². The Emas National Park is a national park and a UNESCO World Heritage Site in the states of Goiás and Mato Grosso do Sul in Brazil.

title: Jog Falls
fact: Jog Falls is a series of large, segmented waterfalls on the Sharavati River in Karnataka state of India, created by the river plunging approximately 253 metres (830 ft) and splitting into four distinct cascades (Raja, Rani, Roarer, and Rocket).

title: Khangchendzonga National Park
fact: National park since 1977, 1,784 km². Khangchendzonga National Park is a national park and part of the Khangchendzonga Biosphere Reserve in Sikkim, India. It was inscribed to the UNESCO World Heritage Sites list in July 2016, becoming the first "Mixed Heritage" site of India.

title: Kuma–Manych Depression
fact: The Kuma–Manych depression is a geological depression in southwestern Russia that separates the Russian Plain to the north from Ciscaucasia to the south. It is named after the Kuma and Manych rivers.

title: Lake Malawi National Park
fact: National park since 1980, 94 km². Lake Malawi National Park is a national park at the southern end of Lake Malawi in Malawi, Southeast Africa. It is the only national park in Malawi that was created with the purpose of protecting fish and aquatic habitats.

title: Seokguram
fact: Seokguram is a hermitage and part of the Bulguksa temple complex in Gyeongju, South Korea. It and Bulguksa are both on the mountain Tohamsan, although the two are separated by distance of around 3 kilometres (1.9 mi).

title: Viñales Valley
fact: Viñales Valley is a karstic depression in Cuba. The valley has an area of 132 km2 (51 sq mi) and is located in the Sierra de los Órganos mountains (part of Guaniguanico range), just north of Viñales in the Pinar del Río Province.

title: Waikīkī
fact: Waikīkī is a Honolulu neighborhood and the eponymous Waikīkī beach on its south shore, on the island of Oʻahu in the U.S. state of Hawaii.

title: Ama Dablam
fact: 6,814 m above sea level. Ama Dablam is a mountain in the Eastern Himalayas range of Koshi Province, Nepal. The main peak is 6,812 metres (22,349 ft), the lower western peak is 6,170 metres (20,243 ft).

title: Mount Ida (Crete)
fact: Mount Ida, known variously as Idha, Ídhi, Idi, and Ita, is the highest mountain on the island of Crete, with an elevation of 2,456 metres (8,058 ft). It has the highest topographic prominence of any mountain in Greece.

title: Kirat Chuli
fact: 7,365 m above sea level. Kirat Chuli or Tent Peak is a mountain in the Himalayas. It lies on the border between Nepal and India.

title: Malubiting
fact: 7,458 m above sea level. Malubiting, also known as Malubiting West, ranks as the second highest peak between the Haramosh and Hispar valleys in the Karakoram range in Pakistan. It is situated between Bilchar Dobani and Haramosh Peak, in the Gilgit-Baltistan region.

title: Momhil Sar
fact: Momhil Sar is, at 7,414 metres (24,324 ft) above sea level, the 64th highest mountain peak in the world.

title: Skyang Kangri
fact: 7,545 m above sea level. Skyang Kangri, or Staircase Peak, is a high mountain peak of the Baltoro Muztagh, a subrange of the Karakoram range. It lies on the Pakistan–China border, about 7 kilometres (4.3 mi) northeast of K2, the world's second-highest mountain.

title: Ultar
fact: 7,388 m above sea level. Ultar is the southeasternmost major peak of the Batura Muztagh, a subrange of the Karakoram range.

title: Chobe National Park
fact: National park since 1967, 11,700 km². Chobe National Park is Botswana's first national park, and also its most biologically diverse. The park contains the wetlands of the Chobe River, which flows into Victoria Falls and the Zambezi to the East.

title: Darién National Park
fact: National park since 1980, 5,790 km². Darién National Park is a World Heritage Site in Panama. It is about 325 kilometers (202 mi) from Panama City, is the most extensive of all national parks of Panama, and is one of the most important World Heritage Sites in Central America.

title: Fiordland National Park
fact: National park since 1952, 12,500 km². Fiordland National Park is a national park in the south-west corner of South Island of New Zealand. It is the largest of the 13 national parks in New Zealand, with an area of 12,607 km2 (4,868 sq mi).

title: Gran Paradiso National Park
fact: National park since 1922, 710 km². Gran Paradiso National Park is an Italian national park in the Graian Alps, between the Aosta Valley and Piedmont regions.

title: Jezreel Valley
fact: The Jezreel Valley, or Marj Ibn Amir is a large fertile plain and inland valley in the Northern District of Israel.

title: Seljalandsfoss
fact: Waterfall, 65 m tall. Seljalandsfoss is a waterfall in Iceland. Seljalandsfoss is located in the South Region in Iceland right by Route 1 and the road that leads to Þórsmörk Road 249.

title: Swiss National Park
fact: National park since 1914, 172 km². The Swiss National Park is located in the Western Rhaetian Alps, in eastern Switzerland. It lies within the canton of Graubünden, between Zernez, S-chanf, Scuol, and the Fuorn Pass in the Engadin valley on the border with Italy.

title: Yoho National Park
fact: National park since 1886, 1,313 km². Yoho National Park ( YOH-hoh) is a national park of Canada. It is located within the Rocky Mountains along the western slope of the Continental Divide of the Americas in southeastern British Columbia…

title: Monte Pissis
fact: 6,795 m above sea level. Monte Pissis is an extinct volcano on the border of the La Rioja and Catamarca provinces in Argentina, 25 km (16 mi) to the east of the Chilean border and about 550 km (340 mi) north of Aconcagua.

title: Betpak-Dala
fact: Betpak-Dala or Betpaqdala is a desert zone in the Ulytau, Karaganda, Turkestan, and Zhambyl regions, Kazakhstan.

title: Jostedal Glacier
fact: Glacier, 550 km². Jostedal Glacier or Jostedalsbreen is the largest glacier in continental Europe. It is in Vestland county in Western Norway.

title: Nukunonu
fact: Nukunonu, formerly known as Duke of Clarence Island, is the largest atoll within Tokelau, a dependency of New Zealand in the south Pacific Ocean.

title: Panjshir Valley
fact: The Panjshir Valley, also spelled Panjsher, is a valley in northeastern Afghanistan, 150 kilometres (93 mi) north of Kabul, near the Hindu Kush mountain range. It is divided by the Panjshir River.

title: Sherwood Forest
fact: Sherwood Forest consists of the remnants of an ancient royal forest in Nottinghamshire, in the East Midlands region of England. It is associated with the legend of Robin Hood. The forest was proclaimed by William the Conqueror and mentioned in the Domesday Book in 1086.

title: Tanami Desert
fact: The Tanami Desert (Warlpiri: Jarnami) is a desert in northern Australia, situated in the Northern Territory and Western Australia. It has a rocky terrain and small hills.

title: Gasherbrum V
fact: 7,147 m above sea level. Gasherbrum V is a mountain in the Gasherbrum massif, located in the Karakoram range in Gilgit–Baltistan, Pakistan.

title: Shispare
fact: 7,619 m above sea level. Shispare is one of the high mountain peaks of the Batura Muztagh, the westernmost subrange of the Karakoram range in the Gilgit-Baltistan region of Pakistan.

title: Spantik
fact: 7,027 m above sea level. Spantik, also known as Golden Peak, is a mountain situated in the Spantik-Sosbun subrange within the Karakoram range. It is located in Shigar District, of the Gilgit-Baltistan region of Pakistan.

title: Teram Kangri
fact: 7,462 m above sea level. The Teram Kangri group is a mountain massif in the remote Siachen Muztagh, a subrange of the Karakoram range.

title: Bukit Pagon
fact: Highest point of Brunei: 1,850 m above sea level. Bukit Pagon (BOO-kit PAH-gon) is the highest point in the country, rising to an elevation of 1,841 metres (6,040 ft) above sea level. It is located in the Temburong District of eastern Brunei, along the border with Sarawak.

title: Cerro El Pital
fact: Highest point of El Salvador: 2,730 m above sea level. Cerro El Pital is a mountain in El Salvador, Central America and near the border with Honduras.

title: Jabal Umm ad Dami
fact: Highest point of Jordan: 1,854 m above sea level. Jabal Umm ad Dami, in historic Wadi Rum, is the highest mountain in Jordan. Its claimed elevation of 1,854 metres is consistent with SRTM data.

title: Jade Dragon Snow Mountain
fact: 5,596 m above sea level. Jade Dragon Snow Mountain is a mountain massif or small mountain range in Yulong Naxi Autonomous County, Lijiang, in Yunnan province, China. Its highest peak is named Shanzidou or Shan-Tzu-tou (扇子陡) and it is 5,596 m (18,360 ft) above sea level.

title: Kediet ej Jill
fact: Highest point of Mauritania: 915 m above sea level. Kediet ej Jill is a mountain in Tiris Zemmour, Mauritania, with the city of Zouérat on its east and Fderick at west.

title: Mont Ngaoui
fact: Highest point of Central African Republic: 1,410 m above sea level. Mont Ngaoui is the highest mountain in the Central African Republic. It is located on the border with Cameroon and has a summit elevation of 1,410 metres (4,626 ft).

title: Mont Sokbaro
fact: Highest point of Benin. Mont Sokbaro is a mountain that is mostly cited as the highest point of Benin, with an elevation of 658 metres (2,159 ft). This designation is contested, as SRTM readings at coordinates 10°17′22″N 1°32′38″E give an elevation of 672 metres (2,205 ft).

title: Mount Afadja
fact: Highest point of Ghana: 885 m above sea level. Mount Afadja, known as Afadjato to the Ewe people of Ghana and Togo, is one of the highest mountains in Ghana.

title: Great Basin Desert
fact: The Great Basin Desert is part of the Great Basin between the Sierra Nevada and the Wasatch Range in the western United States.

title: St. Brandon
fact: Saint Brandon, also known as the Cargados Carajos Shoals, is a southwest Indian Ocean archipelago of sand banks, shoals and islets belonging to the Republic of Mauritius. It lies about 430 km (270 mi) northeast of the island of Mauritius.

title: Val Camonica
fact: Val Camonica or Valcamonica, also Valle Camonica and anglicized as Camonica Valley, is one of the largest valleys of the central Alps, in eastern Lombardy, Italy.

title: Acotango
fact: 6,052 m above sea level. Acotango is the central and highest of a group of stratovolcanoes straddling the border of Bolivia and Chile. It is 6,052 metres (19,856 ft) high.

title: Atlasov Island
fact: 2,339 m above sea level. Atlasov Island, also known as Alaid Island, is the northernmost island of the Kuril Islands, part of the Sakhalin Oblast in Russia. Located on the island is Alaid volcano, the highest volcano of the Kurils and one of the most active.

title: Monte Viso
fact: 3,841 m above sea level. Monte Viso or Monviso is the highest mountain of the Cottian Alps, located in Piedmont, Italy, close to the French border. Monte Viso is well known for its pyramid-like shape.

title: Mount Elbert
fact: 4,401 m above sea level. Mount Elbert is the highest summit of the Rocky Mountains of North America. With an elevation of 14,440 ft (4,400 m), it is also the highest point in the U.S. state of Colorado and the second-highest summit in the contiguous United States after Mount…

title: Tupungato
fact: 6,635 m above sea level. Tupungato, one of the highest mountains in the Americas, is a massive Andean lava dome dating to Pleistocene times.

title: Wildspitze
fact: 3,768 m above sea level. Wildspitze is the highest mountain in the Ötztal Alps and in North Tyrol, as well as the second highest mountain in Austria after Großglockner and in terms of prominence (2261 m) is the fourth summit of the Alps and the fifteenth of Europe.

title: Cedars of God
fact: The Cedars of God is a forest in the Kadisha Valley of Bsharre, Lebanon. It is a vestige of the extensive forests of the Lebanon cedar that thrived across Mount Lebanon in antiquity.

title: Chalbi Desert
fact: The Chalbi Desert is a small desert in northern Kenya near the border with Ethiopia. It is east of Lake Turkana, within the Marsabit County. Marsabit is the closest major urban center.

title: Goðafoss
fact: Waterfall, 12 m tall. Goðafoss is a waterfall in northern Iceland. It is located along the country's main ring road at the junction with the Sprengisandur highland road, about 45 minutes from Akureyri.

title: Gorham's Cave
fact: Gorham's Cave is a sea-level cave in the British overseas territory of Gibraltar. Though not a sea cave, it is often mistaken for one.

title: Krimml Waterfalls
fact: The Krimml Waterfalls, with a total height of 380 metres (1,247 feet), are the highest waterfall in Austria. The falls are on the Krimmler Ache river and are located near the village of Krimml in the High Tauern National Park in Salzburg state.

title: Nui (atoll)
fact: Nui is an atoll and one of nine districts of the Pacific Ocean state of Tuvalu. It has a land area of 3.37 km2 (1.31 sq mile)and a population of 514 (2022 Census).

title: Nukulaelae
fact: Nukulaelae is an atoll that is part of the nation of Tuvalu, and it has a population of 300 (2017 census). The largest settlement is Pepesala on Fangaua islet with a population of 341 people (2022 Census). It has the form of an oval and consists of at least 15 islets.

title: Öræfajökull
fact: Öræfajökull is an ice-covered volcano in south-east Iceland. The largest active volcano and the highest peak in Iceland at 2,110 metres (6,920 ft), it lies within the Vatnajökull National Park and is covered by part of the glacier.

title: Reichenbach Falls
fact: Reichenbach Falls is a waterfall in the Bernese Oberland region of Switzerland, which drop a height of 250 metres (820 ft).

title: Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta
fact: The Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta (English: Snow-Covered Mountain Range of Saint Martha) is an isolated mountain range in northern Colombia, separate from the Andes range that runs through the north of the country.
story_label: Wikipedia: Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta

title: Cerro Las Minas
fact: Highest point of Honduras: 2,849 m above sea level. Cerro Las Minas is the highest mountain in Honduras. Cerro Las Minas is located in the rugged and relatively isolated Lempira Department in the western part of the country.

title: Cerro Tres Kandú
fact: Highest point of Paraguay. Cerro Tres Kandú is the highest point in Paraguay, with an elevation of 842 meters (2,762 ft). It is located in the municipality of General Eugenio Garay, Guairá Department, in a hill range named Ybytyruzú.

title: Jabal as-Sūda
fact: Highest point of Saudi Arabia: 3,133 m above sea level. Jabal Soudah is a peak in the as-Sūda mountains in Saudi Arabia. Jabal as-Sūda is officially recognised by the Saudi authorities as the highest point in Saudi Arabia, with an elevation of 3,015 metres (9,892 ft)…

title: Machapuchare
fact: 6,993 m above sea level. Machapuchare, Machhapuchchhre or Machhapuchhre, is a mountain situated in the Annapurna massif of Gandaki Province, north-central Nepal.

title: Monte San Valentín
fact: 4,058 m above sea level. Monte San Valentin, also known as Monte San Clemente, is the highest mountain in Chilean Patagonia and the highest mountain south of 37°S outside Antarctica. It stands at the north end of the North Patagonian Icefield.

title: Mount Hasan
fact: 3,268 m above sea level. Mount Hasan is a volcano in Anatolia, Turkey. It has two summits, the 3,069 metres (10,069 ft) high eastern Small Hasandağ and the 3,253 metres (10,673 ft) high Big Hasandağ, and rises about 1 kilometre (0.62 mi) above the surrounding terrain.

title: Mount Heha
fact: Highest point of Burundi: 2,684 m above sea level. Mount Heha is the highest mountain in Burundi and the highest point in the Burundi Highlands mountain range.

title: Mountain of Smoke
fact: Highest point of Bahrain: 134 m above sea level. The Mountain of Smoke is a hill in the Southern Governorate of Bahrain. At 134 m (440 ft) above mean sea level, it is the country's highest point.

title: Pic la Selle
fact: Highest point of Haiti: 2,674 m above sea level. Pic la Selle, also called Morne La Selle, is the highest peak in Haiti at 2,574 metres (8,445 ft) above sea level. The mountain is part of the Chaîne de la Selle mountain range and has a pine forest.

title: K6 (mountain)
fact: 7,282 m above sea level. Surveyed as K6, but also known as Baltistan Peak, it is a notable peak of the Masherbrum Mountains, a subrange of the Karakoram mountain range in the Gilgit-Baltistan region of Pakistan.

title: Labuche Kang
fact: 7,367 m above sea level. Labuche Kang (or Lapche Kang, Lobuche Kang I, Choksiam) is a northern outlier of the Himalayas inside Tibet. It rises northwest of Rolwaling Himal and east of Shishapangma.

title: Melungtse
fact: 7,181 m above sea level. Melungtse is the highest mountain of the Rolwaling Himal in the Himalayas. The peak has a long summit ridge capped by the east (main) summit and the west summit, also known as Melungtse II…

title: Tilicho Peak
fact: 7,134 m above sea level. Tilicho Peak is a mountain in the Nepalese Himalayas, near Annapurna. The peak was first seen by Europeans in 1950 by members of the 1950 French Annapurna expedition led by Maurice Herzog who were attempting to find Annapurna I. Lake Tilicho is located…

title: Ad-Dahna Desert
fact: Ad-Dahna Desert is the central division of the Arabian Desert. It is a corridor of sandy terrain forming a bow-like shape that connects an-Nafud desert in the north to Rub' al-Khali desert in the south.

title: Badain Jaran Desert
fact: The Badain Jaran Desert is a desert in China which spans the provinces of Gansu, Ningxia and Inner Mongolia. It covers an area of 49,000 square kilometers (19,000 sq mi; 12,000,000 acres). By size it is the third largest desert in China.

title: Darial Gorge
fact: The Darial Gorge is a river gorge on the border between Russia and Georgia. It is at the east base of Mount Kazbek, south of present-day Vladikavkaz. The gorge was carved by the river Terek, and is approximately 13 kilometres (8.1 mi) long.

title: Gangotri Glacier
fact: Gangotri glacier is located in Uttarkashi District, Uttarakhand, India in a region bordering Tibet. This glacier, one of the primary sources of the Ganges, has a volume of over 27 cubic kilometers.

title: Hunza Valley
fact: The Hunza Valley, also known as the Hunza-Nagar Valley, is a mountainous river valley traversed by the Hunza River in Gilgit-Baltistan region, in Pakistan-administered Kashmir.

title: Jordan Valley
fact: The Jordan Valley forms part of the larger Jordan Rift Valley. Unlike most other river valleys, the term "Jordan Valley" often applies just to the lower course of the Jordan River, from the spot where it exits the Sea of Galilee in the north…

title: Kadisha Valley
fact: Kadisha Valley, also romanized as the Qadisha Valley and also known as the Kadisha Gorge or Wadi Kadisha, is a gorge that lies within the Bsharri and Zgharta Districts of the North Governorate of Lebanon.

title: Kumsusan Palace of the Sun
fact: The Kumsusan Palace of the Sun, formerly the Kumsusan Memorial Palace (금수산기념궁전), is the mausoleum where the preserved bodies of Kim Il Sung and Kim Jong Il, the eternal leaders of North Korea, are displayed.
story_label: Wikipedia: Kumsusan Palace of the Sun

title: Minicoy
fact: Minicoy, locally known as Maliku, is an island in Lakshadweep, India. Along with Viringili, it is on Maliku atoll, the southernmost atoll of Lakshadweep archipelago. Administratively, it is a census town in the Indian union territory of Lakshadweep.

title: Neandertal (valley)
fact: The Neandertal is a small valley of the river Düssel in the German state of North Rhine-Westphalia, located about 12 km (7.5 mi) east of Düsseldorf, the capital city of North Rhine-Westphalia. The valley lies within the limits of the towns of Erkrath and Mettmann.

title: Nukufetau
fact: Nukufetau is an atoll that is part of the nation of Tuvalu. The atoll was claimed by the US under the Guano Islands Act some time in the 19th century and was ceded in a treaty of friendship concluded in 1979 and coming into force in 1983.

title: Orkhon Valley
fact: The Orkhon Valley Cultural Landscape sprawls along the banks of the Orkhon River in Central Mongolia, some 320 km west from the capital Ulaanbaatar.

title: Vaitupu
fact: Vaitupu is the largest atoll of the nation of Tuvalu. It is located at 7.48 degrees south and 178.83 degrees east. There are 1,077 people (2022 Census) living on 5.6 square kilometres (2.2 square miles) with the main village being Asau.

title: Vanch-Yakh Glacier
fact: The Fedchenko Glacier or the Vanch-Yakh Glacier is a large glacier in the Yazgulem Range, Pamir Mountains, of north-central Gorno-Badakhshan province, Tajikistan.

title: Bikku Bitti
fact: Highest point of Libya. Bikku Bitti, also known as Bette Peak, is the highest mountain in Libya at 2,266–2,267 metres (7,434–7,438 ft). It is located on the Dohone spur of the Tibesti Mountains in southern Libya, near the Chadian border.

title: Cerro Catedral (Uruguay)
fact: Highest point of Uruguay: 514 m above sea level. Cerro Catedral ("Cathedral Hill"), also known as Cerro Cordillera, is a peak and the highest point of Uruguay, with an altitude of 513.66 m (1,685.2 ft).

title: Mafadi
fact: Highest point of South Africa: 3,450 m above sea level. Maifadi is a peak on the border of South Africa and Lesotho. At a height of 3,446.1 metres (11,306 ft), it is the highest mountain in the nation of South Africa, but is lower than Thabana Ntlenyana…

title: Mont Idoukal-n-Taghès
fact: Highest point of Niger: 2,022 m above sea level. Mont Idoukal-n-Taghès (also Mont Bagzane, Mont Bagzan) is the highest mountain in Niger. Mont Idoukal-n-Taghès is located in the south central Aïr Mountains, and is at the northern end of the Bagzane plateau.

title: Mount Alvernia
fact: Highest point of The Bahamas. Mount Alvernia is located on Cat Island in The Bahamas and is the highest point in the country at 63 metres (207 ft) above sea level. The mountain shares its name with a school in Montego Bay, Jamaica.

title: Mount Ngerchelchuus
fact: Highest point of Palau: 242 m above sea level. Mount Ngerchelchuus is the Republic of Palau's highest point, located at the border of the states of Ngardmau and Ngaremlengui, on the island of Babeldaob.

title: Mount Saint Catherine (Grenada)
fact: Highest point of Grenada: 840 m above sea level. Mount Saint Catherine is an extensively weathered stratovolcano mountain and tallest peak on the Caribbean island of Grenada.

title: Mount Shimbiris
fact: Highest point of Somalia: 2,460 m above sea level. Mount Shimbiris is the highest peak in Somaliland and Somalia. It has an elevation of 2,460 metres (8,071 ft) above sea level.

title: Hula Valley
fact: The Hula Valley is a topographic depression forming a valley and fertile agricultural region in northern Israel with abundant fresh water that used to be part covered by marshland and Lake Hula.

title: Murchison Falls
fact: Murchison Falls, also known as Kabalega Falls, is a waterfall in Uganda, located at the apex of Lake Albert on the White Nile.

title: Scoresby Sound
fact: Scoresby Sound is a large fjord system of the Greenland Sea on the eastern coast of Greenland. It has a tree-like structure, with a main body approximately 110 km (68 mi) long that branches into a system of fjords covering an area of about 38,000 km2 (14,700 sq mi).

title: Serranilla Bank
fact: Serranilla Bank is a partially submerged reef, with small uninhabited islets, in the western Caribbean Sea. It is situated about 350 kilometres (220 mi) northeast of the Punta Gorda River, Nicaragua, and roughly 280 kilometres (170 mi) southwest of Jamaica.

title: Tabuaeran
fact: Tabuaeran, also known as Fanning Island, is an atoll that is part of the Line Islands of the central Pacific Ocean and part of the island nation of Kiribati. The land area is 33.73 square kilometres (13.02 square miles), and the population in 2015 was 2,315.

title: Wadi El Natrun
fact: Wadi El Natrun is a depression in northern Egypt that is located 23 m (75 ft) below sea level and 38 m (125 ft) below the Nile River level. The valley contains several alkaline lakes, natron-rich salt deposits, salt marshes and freshwater marshes.

title: Ghent Kangri
fact: 7,401 m above sea level. Ghent Kangri (or Mount Ghent, Ghaint I) is a high peak near the north end of the Saltoro Mountains, a subrange of the Karakoram range. It is located west of the Siachen Glacier near the Actual Ground Position Line between India and Pakistan.

title: Molamenqing
fact: 7,661 m above sea level. Molamenqing, also known as Phola Gangchen, is an eastern outlier of Shishapangma, the 14th-highest peak in the world. Both are in the Jugal Himal, a subrange of the Himalayas in Tibet.

title: Bogda Peak
