fact: Sardinero is a popular beach located in the Spanish city of Santander, Cantabria. The beach is divided in two by the gardens of Piquio about one-quarter the way along its length, stretching from the Magdalena Peninsula to Mataleñas…

title: Subi Reef
fact: Subi Reef, also known as Xu Bi Reef, Zamora Reef, or Zhubi Reef, is an atoll in the Spratly Islands of the South China Sea located 26 km (16 mi) southwest of Thitu Island. It is occupied by China, and claimed by the Philippines, Taiwan and Vietnam.

title: Bicaz Gorge
fact: The Bicaz Gorge is a gorge in northeast Romania, in Neamț and Harghita counties. It is in the central part of the Hășmaș Mountains, and is part of the Cheile Bicazului-Hășmaș National Park.

title: Dean's Blue Hole
fact: Dean's Blue Hole is a blue hole located in Long Island, Bahamas in a bay located west of Clarence Town. With a depth of 202 metres (663 ft), it is world's third deepest blue hole after the Taam Ja' Blue Hole in the Chetumal Bay and Dragon Hole in the South China Sea.

title: Deildartunguhver
fact: Deildartunguhver is a hot spring in Reykholtsdalur, Iceland. It is characterized by a very high flow rate for a hot spring (180 liters/second) and water emerges at 97 °C (207 °F). It is the highest-flow hot spring in Europe.

title: Devils Hole
fact: Devils Hole is a geologic formation located in a detached unit of Death Valley National Park and surrounded by the Ash Meadows National Wildlife Refuge, in Nye County, Nevada, in the Southwestern United States.

title: Dunajec River Gorge
fact: The Dunajec River Gorge runs through the Pieniny Mountains in the south of Poland and the north of Slovakia (as Dunajec is the border river between the two countries in the area).

title: Glass Beach (Fort Bragg, California)
fact: Glass Beach is a beach adjacent to MacKerricher State Park near Fort Bragg, California, named from a time when it was abundant with sea glass created from years of dumping garbage into an area of coastline near the northern part of the town.

title: Glen Canyon
fact: Glen Canyon is a natural canyon carved by a 169.6-mile (272.9 km) length of the Colorado River, mostly in southeastern and south-central Utah, in the United States. Glen Canyon starts where Narrow Canyon ends, at the confluence of the Colorado River and the Dirty Devil River.

title: Glover's Reef
fact: Glover's Reef is a partially submerged atoll located off the southern coast of Belize, approximately 45 km (28 mi) from the mainland. It forms part of the outermost boundary of the Belize Barrier Reef, and is one of its three atolls, besides Turneffe Atoll and Lighthouse Reef.

title: Laurel Canyon, Los Angeles
fact: Laurel Canyon is a mountainous neighborhood in the Hollywood Hills region of the Santa Monica Mountains, within the Hollywood Hills West district of Los Angeles, California.

title: Lazurnaya Bay
fact: Lazurnaya Bay is a bay on the east side of the Muravyov-Amursky Peninsula in Russia. It lies to the northeast of Vladivostok and to the southwest from the Three Little Pigs Bay. The Lazurnaya Bay forms part of the Ussuri Bay in the Sea of Japan.

title: Myrtos Beach
fact: Myrtos Beach is in the region of Pylaros, in the north-west of Kefalonia island, in the Ionian Sea of Greece. Myrtos beach lies between the feet of two mountains, Agia Dynati and Kalon Oros (901m).

title: Plages du Prado
fact: The Plages du Prado are the beaches in the south neighborhood of Marseille, France. The seaside park is an artificial coastal development created in the late 1970s by Gaston Defferre. They were built with the fill coming from the construction of the two Marseille metro lines.

title: Roque Cinchado
fact: Roque Cinchado is a volcanic rock formation regarded as emblematic of the island of Tenerife (Canary Islands, Spain). It lies within the Teide National Park (a World Heritage Site) in the municipality of La Orotava, near Teide volcano, in the heart of the island.

title: Steamboat Geyser
fact: Steamboat Geyser, in Yellowstone National Park's Norris Geyser Basin, is the world's tallest active geyser. Steamboat Geyser has two vents, northern and southern, approximately 20 feet (6.1 m) apart.

title: Zwischenahner Meer
fact: is a lake in Ammerland, Lower Saxony, Germany. It is at an elevation of approximately 5 metres (16 ft), and has a surface area of 550 hectares (1,400 acres).

title: Cotahuasi Canyon
fact: Cotahuasi Canyon, near the city of Arequipa in Peru, is one of the deepest canyons in the world.

title: Hammam Maskhoutine
fact: Hammam Maskhoutine is a thermal complex located in Hammam Debagh, of Guelma Province, Algeria. The dramatic, multicolored travertine walls of the spring have attracted attention from locals and tourists alike since the era of the Roman Empire.

title: Ik Kil
fact: Ik Kil is a cenote outside Pisté in the Tinúm Municipality, Yucatán, Mexico. It is located in the northern center of the Yucatán Peninsula and is part of the Ik Kil Archeological Park near Chichen Itza. It is open to the public for swimming.

title: Jacob's Well (Texas)
fact: Jacob's Well is a perennial karstic spring in the Texas Hill Country flowing from the bed of Cypress Creek, located northwest of Wimberley, Texas.

title: Johnson South Reef
fact: Johnson South Reef, also known as Chigua (Chih-kua) Reef, Gạc Ma Reef, or Mabini Reef, is a reef in the southwest portion of the Union Banks in the Spratly Islands of the South China Sea.

title: Kings Canyon (Northern Territory)
fact: Kings Canyon, also known as Watarrka, is a canyon in the Northern Territory of Australia located at the western end of the George Gill Range about 321 kilometres (199 mi) southwest of Alice Springs and about 1,316 kilometres (818 mi) south of Darwin…

title: Ma'ayan Harod
fact: Ma'ayan Harod or Ain Jalut is an all-year spring in the Harod Valley (the easternmost part of the Jezreel Valley) on the northwest corner of Mount Gilboa, that was the location of the 13th-century Battle of Ain Jalut.

title: Second Thomas Shoal
fact: Second Thomas Shoal, also known as Ayungin Shoal, Bãi Cỏ Mây and Rén'ài Jiāo, is a submerged reef in the Spratly Islands of the South China Sea, 105 nautical miles (194 km; 121 mi) west of Palawan, Philippines. It is a disputed territory and claimed by multiple nations.

title: St. Mary's Islands
fact: St. Mary's Islands, also locally known as Thonsepar are a set of four small uninhabited islands in the Arabian Sea off the coast of Malpe in Udupi district of the Indian state of Karnataka.

title: Tsalka Canyon
fact: Tsalka Canyon is part of Khrami (known as Ktsia at its source) gorge near Dashbashi village, 3 km from the small town of Tsalka, in Tsalka Municipality, in Kvemo Kartli region of southeastern Georgia, 1,110-1,448 meters above sea level.

title: Vrelo Bune
fact: Vrelo Bune is a natural and architectural ensemble located at the spring of the Buna River near Blagaj, a village-town, and is part of the wider "Townscape ensemble of the town of Blagaj…

title: Zacatón
fact: Zacatón is a thermal water-filled cenote, or sinkhole, belonging to the Zacatón system – a group of unusual karst features located in Aldama Municipality near the Sierra de Tamaulipas in the northeastern state of Tamaulipas, Mexico.

title: Blenheim Reef
fact: Blenheim Reef is a partly submerged atoll structure in the Chagos Archipelago, Indian Ocean. It includes the coral reef of Baxio Predassa in its southeastern rim, plus another completely submerged part. It is located in the northeastern part of the Chagos Archipelago.

title: Cheshmeh-Ali (Shahr-e-Rey)
fact: Cheshmeh-Ali is an ancient recreational place, located in the south of Tehran and north of Rey or Ray in the country of Iran.

title: Daedalus Reef
fact: Daedalus Reef is an isolated oceanic coral reef in the Egyptian Red Sea, located approximately 90 kilometres (56 mi) east of Marsa Alam and about 100 kilometres (62 mi) south-east of Hurghada…

title: Dune 45
fact: Dune 45 is a star dune in the Sossusvlei area of the Namib Desert in Namibia. Its name comes from the fact that it is at the 45th kilometre of the road that connects the Sesriem gate and Sossusvlei.

title: Horns Rev
fact: Horns Rev is a shallow sandy reef of glacial deposits in the eastern North Sea, about 15 km (9.3 mi) off the westernmost point of Denmark, Blåvands Huk. For many years Horns Rev was marked by a lightship, though that has now been replaced by light buoys.

title: Hveravellir
fact: Hveravellir is a geothermal field (high temperature field) of the Oddnýjarhnjúkur-Langjökull volcanic system - in the north of the Langjökull glacier.

title: Köprülü Canyon
fact: Köprülü Canyon is a canyon and a National Park in the Province of Antalya, Turkey. Covering an area of 366 km2 (141 mi2), it was established as a national park by the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry on December 12, 1973.

title: Lighthouse Reef
fact: Lighthouse Reef is an atoll in the Caribbean Sea, the easternmost part of the Belize Barrier Reef and one of its three atolls, the other two being Turneffe Atoll and Glover's Reef. Lighthouse Reef is located about 80 kilometres (50 mi) southeast of Belize City.

title: Louisa Reef
fact: Louisa Reef is a coral reef in the southern reaches of the Spratly Islands. The reef is oval in shape, approximately 1.5 km (1 mile) east to west and 0.5 km (500 yards) north to south.

title: Mammoth Hot Springs
fact: Mammoth Hot Springs is a large complex of hot springs on a hill of travertine in Yellowstone National Park adjacent to Fort Yellowstone and the Mammoth Hot Springs Historic District.

title: Pink and White Terraces
fact: The Pink and White Terraces were natural wonders of New Zealand. They were reportedly the largest silica sinter deposits on Earth.

title: Qutang Gorge
fact: The Qutang Gorge is the shortest of China's Three Gorges. Immediately downstream of the ancient Baidicheng (白帝城) fortress, the Yangtze River passes between the Chijia Mountain (赤甲山) on the north and the Baiyan Mountain (白鹽山) on the south.

title: Scorpion Reef
fact: Scorpion Reef is an atoll containing a small group of islets in the Gulf of Mexico, about 125 kilometres (78 mi; 67 NM) off the northern coast of the state of Yucatán, Mexico.

title: Acqua Panna
fact: Acqua Panna is an Italian brand of bottled water and one of the world's largest bottled water brands. The brand belongs to Sanpellegrino S.p.A subsidiary of Nestlé Waters.

title: Bagni San Filippo
fact: Bagni San Filippo is an area in the municipality of Castiglione d'Orcia in the Province of Siena, Italy, not far from Monte Amiata. It is a small hot spring containing calcium carbonate deposits, which form white concretions and waterfalls.

title: Caliphal Baths
fact: The Caliphal Baths are an Islamic bathhouse (or Arab baths) complex in Córdoba, Spain. They are situated in the historic centre which was declared a World Heritage Site by UNESCO in 1994.

title: Carondelet Reef
fact: Carondelet Reef is a horseshoe-shaped reef, presumably a submerged atoll formation, of the Phoenix Islands, also known as the Rawaki Islands, in the Republic of Kiribati.

title: Dragon Hole
fact: Dragon Hole, also known as Sansha Yongle Blue Hole after the third Ming emperor, Yongle, was the deepest known blue hole in the world at 300.89 metres (987.2 ft) deep from 2016 until it was discovered that the Taam Ja' surpassed it in 2024.

title: Drijenak
fact: Drijenak is a village in the municipality of Kolašin, Montenegro.

title: Funtensee
fact: Funtensee is a karst lake on the Steinernes Meer plateau in Berchtesgaden National Park, Bavaria, Germany. It is located in the larger of two sinkholes (also referred to as uvala). The area is known for record low temperatures, up to 30 °C (54 °F) lower than the surrounding area.

title: Gunnuhver
fact: Gunnuhver is an active geothermal hot spring and a mud pool with fumaroles on the southwestern tip of the Reykjanes Peninsula in Iceland. It lies within the Reykjanes UNESCO Global Geopark and close to the Reykjanesviti lighthouse.

title: Huaqing Pool
fact: The Huaqing Pool (华清池), also known as the Huaqing Palace (华清宫), is a complex of imperial gardens known for its hot springs at the northern foot of Mount Li, Qinling, approximately 25 kilometers (16 mi) east of Xi'an, Shaanxi, China.

title: Inchcape
fact: Inchcape or the Bell Rock is a reef about 11 miles (18 km) off the east coast of Angus, Scotland, near Dundee and Fife, occupied by the Bell Rock Lighthouse.

title: Isa Bulaghi
fact: Isa Bulaghi is a spring in the city of Shusha, Azerbaijan. The spring is associated with the 19th century. After restoration works completed in the early 2020s, a recreation complex at the site was opened on 5 July 2024.

title: Oyun Musa
fact: Oyun Musa, found 20 km south of the Ahmed Hamdi Tunnel in South Sinai, are a collection of fresh water springs said to be those in the area referred to as Elim in Exodus 15:27.

title: Selja Gorges
fact: Selja Gorges (from the traditional transcription fr. Gorges de Selja) or the Thelja Gorges as more recently transcribed from Arabic are located in southern Tunisia in Gafsa Governorate. The gorges link the Gafsa Valley with the Redeyef plateau.

title: Beveridge Reef
fact: Beveridge Reef (Niuean: Nukutulueatama) is a mostly submerged, unpopulated atoll located in the Exclusive Economic Zone of Niue. It has been the cause of several fishing boats running aground or sinking.

title: Cuarteron Reef
fact: Cuarteron Reef, also known as Calderon Reef, is a reef at the east end of the London Reefs in the Spratly Islands of the South China Sea.

title: Dallas Reef
fact: Dallas Reef (7°38′N 113°48′E), also known as Malay: Terumbu Laya; Vietnamese: đá Suối Cát; Mandarin Chinese: 光星礁; pinyin: Guāngxīng Jiāo; Rajah Matanda Reef, lies on the SW extremity of Dangerous Ground (South China Sea) in the Spratly Islands of the South China Sea.

title: Eden Rocks
fact: The Eden Rocks are two rocks lying 1.5 km off the east coast of Dundee Island, at the northern end of the Antarctic Peninsula. A small island was reported there on 30 December 1842 by Captain James Clark Ross of the Royal Navy, who named it "Eden Island" for Captain Charles Eden.

title: Guanziling Hot Spring
fact: Guanziling Hot Spring is a hot spring in Baihe District, Tainan, Taiwan. The hot spring was discovered by the Japanese troops in the area and it was named Taiwan's No. 1 Hot Spring in 1920. The hot spring is located at an altitude of 270 meters above sea level.

title: Hot Water Beach
fact: Hot Water Beach is a beach on the east coast of the Coromandel Peninsula, New Zealand, just south of Mercury Bay. It is approximately 12 kilometres south east of Whitianga, and approximately 175 kilometres from Auckland by car.

title: Hupao Spring
fact: Hupao or Hupaomeng Spring, also known by a variety of translated names such as Dreaming of Tiger Spring or Tiger's Run Spring, is a spring and park in southwestern Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province, China.

title: "Khan gizi" spring
fact: "Khan gizi" spring is a spring located next to Khan's daughter Natevan's palace in the Çöl Qala neighborhood of Shusha. The spring was built in the 19th century by the order of Khurshidbanu Natavan. After the occupation of Shusha on May 8, 1992, the spring was neglected.

title: Austranten Rock
fact: Austranten Rock (71°24′S 14°2′E) is an isolated rock outcrop lying 2 miles (3 km) southeast of Todt Ridge, at the eastern extremity of the Gruber Mountains and the Wohlthat Mountains, in Queen Maud Land of Antarctica.

title: Ayn al-Zara
fact: Ayn al-Zara, known in ancient times as Callirrhoe, is an archaeological site in Jordan. It includes the remains of a nymphaeum, though it is considered difficult to be interpreted.

title: Bystrov Rock
fact: Bystrov Rock (71°47′S 12°35′E) is a prominent rock lying 1 nautical mile (2 km) south-southeast of Isdalsegga Ridge in the Südliche Petermann Range of the Wohlthat Mountains.

title: Devil's Throat, Iguazu Falls
fact: The Devil's Throat is a waterfall on the Iguazu River at the border of Brazil and Argentina. It is shared by the Argentine Iguazú National Park and the Brazilian Iguaçu National Park and accessible by the Rainforest Ecological Train, whose nearby station is called Garganta.

title: Gambacorta Peak
fact: Gambacorta Peak (84°2′S 56°3′W) is a peak 1,840 metres (6,040 ft) high, standing 4 nautical miles (7.4 km; 4.6 mi) east of Mount Kaschak in the southern Neptune Range, Pensacola Mountains, Antarctica.

title: Guartelá Canyon
fact: The Guartelá Canyon is a canyon in Tibagi and Castro, Paraná, Brazil. The canyon of the Iapó River is protected by the 799 hectares (1,970 acres) Guartelá State Park, created in 1992.

title: Iroquois Plateau
fact: The Iroquois Plateau (83°51′S 54°0′W) is a large, mainly ice-covered plateau situated east of the southern part of the Washington Escarpment in the Pensacola Mountains, Antarctica.

title: Pōhutu Geyser
fact: Pōhutu Geyser is a geyser in the Whakarewarewa Thermal Valley, Rotorua, in the North Island of New Zealand. The geyser is the largest in the southern hemisphere and among the most active in the area, erupting up to twenty times per day at heights of up to 30 m (98 ft).

title: Seeburger See
fact: Seeburger See is a lake in the karst region of the Lower Eichsfeld, Landkreis Göttingen, in southeastern Lower Saxony, Germany.

title: Akhayat sinkhole
fact: Akhayat is a sinkhole in Mersin Province, Turkey. The Akhayat Sinkhole is located in a rural area of the Silifke ilçe (district), to the north of Atayurt town.

title: Annenkov Island
fact: Annenkov Island is an island in South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands, to the west of the main island of South Georgia. The Pickersgill Islands are to its southeast.

title: Aramis Range
fact: On the continent of Antarctica, the Aramis Range is the third range south in the Prince Charles Mountains, situated 11 miles southeast of the Porthos Range and extending for about 30 miles in a southwest–northeast direction.

title: Bimmah Sinkhole
fact: Hawiyyat Najm, known as Bimmah Sinkhole in English, is a water-filled depression, structurally a sinkhole, in the limestone of eastern Muscat Governorate in the Sultanate of Oman, very close to the Al Sharqiyah region just off the highway to Sur, few kilometers before Tiwi.

title: Bleset Rock
fact: Bleset Rock (73°39′S 3°57′W) is a rock lying 5 nautical miles (9 km) east-southeast of Enden Point, surmounting the ice divide between Utrakket Valley and Belgen Valley in the Kirwan Escarpment, Queen Maud Land.

title: Cook Bay (South Georgia)
fact: Cook Bay (54°3′S 37°8′W) is an irregular bay, 1.3 nautical miles (2.4 km) wide at its entrance between Cape Crewe and Black Head, narrowing into two western arms, Lighthouse Bay and Prince Olav Harbour, along the north coast of South Georgia.

title: El Dedo de Dios
fact: El Dedo de Dios (translated: God's finger) is a 30 m (98 ft) high sea stack in the Atlantic Ocean, off the northern part of Gran Canaria, one of the Canary Islands.

title: Envoy Rock
fact: Envoy Rock (67°51′S 68°42′W) is a rock marking the northern limit of the Dion Islands, off the south end of Adelaide Island which is within the Argentine, British and Chilean Antarctic claims.

title: Framnaes Point
fact: Framnaes Point (54°8′S 36°39′W) is a point 1 mile (2 km) southwest of Cape Saunders, on the north side of Stromness Bay, South Georgia. The name was given prior to 1920, probably by Norwegian whalers operating in the area.

title: Gamaleya Rock
fact: Gamaleya Rock (71°44′S 10°43′E) is a rock 2 nautical miles (4 km) southeast of Smirnov Peak, marking the extremity of a line of rocks that extend east from the Shcherbakov Range, in the Orvin Mountains of Queen Maud Land, Antarctic.

title: Gobanme Rock
fact: Gobamme Rock is an exposed rock standing on the coast between Kozō Rock and Byōbu Rock in Queen Maud Land, Antarctica. It was mapped from surveys and air photos by the Japanese Antarctic Research Expedition, 1957–62, and named Gobanme-iwa (checkerboard rock).

title: King Edward Cove
fact: King Edward Cove is a sheltered cove in the west side of Cumberland East Bay, South Georgia.

title: Lientur Rocks
fact: Lientur Rocks is a group of prominent adjacent rocks lying off the north coast of Robert Island in the South Shetland Islands, Antarctica and extending 660 m (722 yd) in east–west direction and 320 m (350 yd) in north–south direction.

title: Ma'in Hot Springs
fact: The Ma'in Hot Springs also known as Hammamat Ma'in are a series of hot mineral springs and waterfalls located between Madaba and the Dead Sea in Madaba Governorate, Jordan.

title: Nashornkalvane Rocks
fact: Nashornkalvane Rocks (72°19′S 1°56′W) is a group of rocks 2 nautical miles (3.7 km) north of Nashornet Mountain, at the south side of the mouth of Viddalen Valley in Queen Maud Land.

title: Nordwestliche Insel Mountains
fact: Nordwestliche Insel Mountains (71°27′S 11°33′E) is a small, detached group of mountains, island-like in appearance, and forming the northern extremity of the Humboldt Mountains, in the Wohlthat Mountains of Queen Maud Land, Antarctica.

title: Östliche Petermann Range
fact: The Östliche Petermann Range is one of the Petermann Ranges. It is trending in a north–south direction for 15 nautical miles (28 km), from Per Spur to the Gornyye Inzhenery Rocks, in the Wohlthat Mountains of Queen Maud Land.

title: Phillips Mountains
fact: The Phillips Mountains (76°16′S 145°0′W) are a range of mountains on the north side of Balchen Glacier and Block Bay in the Ford Ranges, Marie Byrd Land, Antarctica.

title: Pozzo del Merro
fact: Pozzo del Merro is a flooded sinkhole in the countryside northeast of Rome, Italy. Situated at the bottom of an 80 m conical pit, at 392 m (1,286 ft) it is the second deepest underwater vertical cave in the world.

title: Rock formations of Adélie Land
fact: This is a list of rock formations in the French Antarctic territory of Adélie Land.
story_label: Wikipedia: Rock formations of Adélie Land

title: Taam Ja' Blue Hole
fact: Taam Ja' blue hole is an underwater sinkhole located in Chetumal Bay at the southeast corner of the Yucatán Peninsula, Mexico. Its name means deep water in the Mayan language.

title: The Billboard
fact: The Billboard is a massive granite monolith in the Sarnoff Mountains of the Ford Ranges of Marie Byrd Land, West Antarctica, standing just west of Mount Rea between Arthur Glacier and Boyd Glacier.

title: Willis Islands
fact: The Willis Islands are a small archipelago to the west of South Georgia Island in the South Georgia Islands. They are 2 miles (3.2 km) west of Bird Island, separated by the Stewart Strait.

title: Aigualluts
fact: The Forau d'Aigualluts is a karst formation and waterfall in the Province of Huesca, northeastern Spain. It lies along the Ésera River, at 2074 m above sea level on Pico Aneto.

title: Andersson Island
fact: Andersson Island (63°35′S 56°35′W) is an island 7 nautical miles (13 km; 8.1 mi) long and 4 nautical miles (7.4 km; 4.6 mi) wide, lying 0.5 nautical miles (0.93 km; 0.58 mi) south of Jonassen Island at the west side of the south entrance to Antarctic Sound…

title: Aparados da Serra National Park
fact: The Aparados da Serra National Park is a national park located in the Serra Geral range of Rio Grande do Sul and Santa Catarina states in the south of Brazil, between 29º07'—29º15' S and 50º01'—50º10' W. It was created in 1959 as one of Brazil's first national parks…
story_label: Wikipedia: Aparados da Serra National Park

title: Bayou Corne sinkhole
fact: The Bayou Corne sinkhole was created from a collapsed underground salt dome cavern operated by Texas Brine Company and owned by Occidental Petroleum.

title: Chicamocha Canyon
fact: The Chicamocha Canyon is a steep sided canyon carved by the Chicamocha River in Colombia. With a maximum depth of 2,000 metres (6,600 ft), an area of 108,000 hectares (270,000 acres) and a length of 227 kilometres (141 mi), the canyon is the second-largest worldwide.

title: Clerke Rocks
fact: The Clerke Rocks are a group of small rocky islands some 35 miles (56 km) southeast of South Georgia that extend 5 miles (8.0 km) from east to west. The Clerke Rocks include The Office Boys at the northeastern end and Nobby at the southeastern end of the group.

title: Crary Mountains
fact: Crary Mountains (76°48′S 117°40′W) are a group of ice-covered volcanoes in Marie Byrd Land, Antarctica.

title: Dune 7 (Namibia)
fact: Dune 7, located outside of Walvis Bay and became a landmark as it was 7 miles from the town centre. Dune 7 is part of the dune belt that runs from Walvis Bay to Swakopmund.

title: Eddystone Rock, Falkland Islands
fact: Eddystone Rock is a rock and reef located to the north of Falkland Sound in the Falkland Islands. It is 44 m (144 ft) high. There is a lighthouse here, which is named after a more famous light of the same name in England.

title: Fortuna Bay
fact: Fortuna Bay (54°07′S 36°48′W) is a bay 3 miles (5 km) long and 1 mile (1.6 km) wide. Its entrance is defined by Cape Best on the west and Robertson Point to the east, near Atherton Peak on the north coast of South Georgia.

title: Gara Medouar
fact: Gara Medouar, also known as Jebel Mudawwar ("round mountain"), Gara Mdouar or Mdoura, is a horseshoe-shaped geological formation ("erosion cirque") near Sijilmasa, Morocco.

title: Großes Heiliges Meer
fact: Großes Heiliges Meer is a lake in Hopsten, Kreis Steinfurt, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. At an elevation of 42,5 m, its surface area is 11 ha.

title: Hound Bay
fact: Hound Bay is a bay at the base of Barff Peninsula. It is 2.5 miles (4 km) wide at its mouth and recedes 3 miles (5 km), entered between Tijuca Point and Cape Vakop along the north coast of South Georgia.

title: Ikogosi Warm Springs
fact: The Ikogosi Warm Springs is a tourist attraction located at Ikogosi, a town in Ekiti State, southwestern Nigeria. Flowing abreast the warm spring is another cold spring which meets the warm spring at a confluence, each maintaining its thermal properties.

title: Lady Knox Geyser
fact: The Lady Knox Geyser is a geyser in the Waiotapu area of the Taupō Volcanic Zone in New Zealand. It is named after Lady Constance Knox, the second daughter of Uchter Knox, 15th Governor of New Zealand.

title: MacQuarrie Edge
fact: MacQuarrie Edge (80°32′S 30°3′W) is a rock scarp rising to about 760 metres (2,500 ft) in the northern part of the Otter Highlands, in the western Shackleton Range, Antarctica.

title: Morozumi Range
fact: The Morozumi Range (71°39′S 161°55′E) is a mountain range in the Usarp Mountains of North Victoria Land, Antarctica. It extends northwest–southeast for 25 miles (40 km), with its northern elevations overlooking the convergence of Gressitt Glacier and Rennick Glacier.

title: Reserva Provincial Castillos de Pincheira
fact: The Reserva Provincial Castillos de Pincheira is a natural area protected in Argentina. It's located about 27 kilometres (17 mi) to the west of the city of Malargüe in the southern part of the Mendoza Province.
story_label: Wikipedia: Reserva Provincial Castillos de Pincheira

title: Rongé Island
fact: Rongé Island is a high, rugged island 5 nautical miles (9.3 km; 5.8 mi) long, the largest island of the group which forms the west side of Errera Channel, off the west coast of Graham Land in Antarctica.

title: Sewing-Machine Needles
fact: Sewing-Machine Needles, also known as Rocas Ministro Ezcurra (62°58′11.8″S 60°29′39.1″W) is a group of three prominent rock needles, the highest 45 m above water, lying close southeast of Rancho Point, Deception Island, in the South Shetland Islands.

title: Toney Mountain
fact: Toney Mountain (75°48′S 115°49′W) is an elongated snow-covered shield volcano, 38 nautical miles (70 km; 44 mi) long and rising to 3,595 metres (11,795 ft) at Richmond Peak, located 35 nautical miles (65 km; 40 mi) southwest of Kohler Range in Marie Byrd Land, Antarctica.

title: Undine Harbour
fact: Undine Harbour is a small bay at the head of the embayment between Cape Paryadin and Cape Chaplin on the south coast of South Georgia.

title: Wisconsin Range
fact: The Wisconsin Range (85°45′S 125°00′W) is a major mountain range of the Horlick Mountains in Antarctica, comprising the Wisconsin Plateau and numerous glaciers, ridges and peaks bounded by the Reedy Glacier, Shimizu Ice Stream, Horlick Ice Stream and the interior ice plateau.

title: Agua Poca
fact: Agua Poca is a monogenetic volcano in the Puelén Department of Argentina. The volcano has the form of a cinder cone and has been active in the Pleistocene.

title: Nyamyumba Hot Springs
fact: The Nyamyumba Hot Springs, known locally by the Kinyarwanda name Amashyuza, are natural hot springs located on the eastern shore of Lake Kivu in Nyamyumba Sector, Rubavu District, Western Province, Rwanda.

title: Puchuldiza
fact: Puchuldiza is a geothermal field in the Tarapacá Region of Chile. It is part of the Central Volcanic Zone of the Andes, close to the active volcano Isluga and several older volcanoes in the neighbourhood…

title: Puritama Hot Springs
fact: Puritama Hot Springs is a series of eight large pools of geothermal spring water located at the bottom of a canyon in the Atacama Desert, in the Antofagasta Region in the north of Chile.

title: Athens International Airport
fact: 2001 — Athens International Airport Eleftherios Venizelos begins operation.

title: Royal Albert Hall
fact: 1871 — Royal Albert Hall is opened by Queen Victoria.

title: Sack of Berwick (1296)
fact: 1296 — Edward I sacks Berwick-upon-Tweed, during armed conflict between Scotland and England.

title: Cretan State
fact: 1900 — Prince George becomes absolute monarch of the Cretan State.

title: Stand in the Schoolhouse Door
fact: 1986 — Alabama governor George Wallace, a former segregationist, best known for the "Stand in the Schoolhouse Door", announces that he will not seek a fifth four-year term and will retire from public life upon the end of his term in January 1987.
story_label: Wikipedia: Stand in the Schoolhouse Door

title: Hatton Garden
fact: 2015 — Four men steal items worth up to £200 million from an underground safe deposit facility in London's Hatton Garden area in what has been called the "largest burglary in English legal history."

title: Grand National
fact: 1993 — The outcome of the Grand National horse race is declared void for the first (and only) time.

title: Battle of Kassel (1945)
fact: 1945 — World War II: United States Army troops capture Kassel.

title: Riverside Church
fact: 1967 — Martin Luther King Jr. delivers his "Beyond Vietnam: A Time to Break Silence" speech in New York City's Riverside Church.

title: Colonial Building
fact: 1932 — Dominion of Newfoundland: Ten thousand rioters seize the Colonial Building leading to the end of self-government.

title: Casa de la Vall
fact: 1933 — Andorran Revolution: The Young Andorrans occupy the Casa de la Vall and force the government to hold democratic elections with universal male suffrage.

title: Pan Am Flight 103
fact: 1999 — Two Libyans suspected of bringing down Pan Am Flight 103 in 1988 are handed over for eventual trial in the Netherlands.

title: Theater an der Wien
fact: 1805 — German composer Ludwig van Beethoven premieres his Third Symphony, at the Theater an der Wien in Vienna.

title: RAF Fairford
fact: 1969 — The first British-built Concorde 002 makes its maiden flight from Filton to RAF Fairford with Brian Trubshaw as the test pilot.

title: St. Thomas Church, Leipzig
fact: 1727 — Premiere of Johann Sebastian Bach's St Matthew Passion BWV 244b at St. Thomas Church in Leipzig, Electorate of Saxony (now Germany).

title: St Mary Magdalene Church, Sandringham
fact: 1871 — Funeral of Prince Alexander John of Wales at St Mary Magdalene Church, Sandringham.
story_label: Wikipedia: St Mary Magdalene Church, Sandringham

title: Stone of Scone
fact: 1951 — The Stone of Scone, the stone upon which Scottish monarchs were traditionally crowned, is found on the site of the altar of Arbroath Abbey. It had been taken by Scottish nationalist students from its place in Westminster Abbey.

title: Disneyland Park (Paris)
fact: 1992 — The Euro Disney Resort officially opens with its theme park Euro Disneyland; the resort and its park's name are subsequently changed to Disneyland Resort Paris.

title: Stortorvet
fact: 1858 — The 1858 Christiania fire severely destroys several city blocks near Stortorvet in Christiania, Norway, and about 1,000 people lose their homes.

title: Exposition Universelle (1900)
fact: 1900 — The world's fair Exposition Universelle opens in Paris.

title: Hauser Dam
fact: 1908 — Hauser Dam, a steel dam on the Missouri River in Montana, fails, sending a surge of water 25 to 30 feet (7.6 to 9.1 m) high downstream.

title: American School for the Deaf
fact: 1817 — Thomas Hopkins Gallaudet and Laurent Clerc found the American School for the Deaf (then called the Connecticut Asylum for the Education and Instruction of Deaf and Dumb Persons), the first American school for deaf students, in Hartford, Connecticut.
story_label: Wikipedia: American School for the Deaf

title: Notre-Dame de Paris
fact: 2019 — The cathedral of Notre-Dame de Paris in France is seriously damaged by a large fire.

title: Natural Bridges National Monument
fact: 1908 — Natural Bridges National Monument is established in Utah.

title: Siege of Boston
fact: 1775 — American Revolutionary War: Following the Battles of Lexington and Concord, the Siege of Boston begins with American militias blocking land access to the British-held city.

title: Kishinev pogrom
fact: 1903 — The Kishinev pogrom in Kishinev (Bessarabia) begins, forcing tens of thousands of Jews to later seek refuge in Palestine and the Western world.

title: Battle of Marj al-Saffar (1303)
fact: 1303 — The Bahri Mamluks defeat the Ilkhanate in the battle of Marj al-Saffar, marking the end of the Mongol incursions into Syria.

title: Archdiocese of Pisa
fact: 1092 — The Diocese of Pisa is elevated to the rank of metropolitan archdiocese by Pope Urban II.

title: Al-Baqi Cemetery
fact: 1926 — Al-Baqi cemetery, former site of the mausoleum of four Shi'a Imams, is leveled to the ground by Wahhabis.

title: Sachsenhausen concentration camp
fact: 1945 — World War II: Sachsenhausen concentration camp is liberated by soldiers of the Red Army and Polish First Army.

title: San Diego–Coronado Bridge
fact: 1970 — Chicano residents in San Diego, California occupy a site under the Coronado Bridge, leading to the creation of Chicano Park.

title: Elephant Island
fact: 1916 — Ernest Shackleton and five men of the Imperial Trans-Antarctic Expedition launch a lifeboat from uninhabited Elephant Island in the Southern Ocean to organise a rescue for the crew of the sunken Endurance.

title: Tsuruga Nuclear Power Plant
fact: 1981 — More than 100 workers are exposed to radiation during repairs of at the Tsuruga Nuclear Power Plant in Japan.

title: Washington Hilton
fact: 2026 — Shots are fired outside of the White House Correspondents' Dinner in the Washington Hilton where U.S. President Donald Trump and members of his cabinet are attending. One injury is reported and a suspect is taken into custody.

title: Mont Ventoux
fact: 1336 — Francesco Petrarca (Petrarch) ascends Mont Ventoux.

title: Church of Saint Sava
fact: 1595 — The relics of Saint Sava are incinerated in Belgrade on the Vračar plateau by Ottoman Grand Vizier Sinan Pasha; the site of the incineration is now the location of the Church of Saint Sava, one of the largest Orthodox churches in the world

title: Chernobyl disaster
fact: 1986 — The city of Pripyat and surrounding areas are evacuated due to the Chernobyl disaster.

title: Wembley Stadium (1923)
fact: 1923 — Wembley Stadium is opened, named initially as the Empire Stadium.

title: New York City Center
fact: 1948 — Igor Stravinsky conducts the premiere of his American ballet, Orpheus at the New York City Center.

title: Gran Canaria
fact: 1483 — Gran Canaria, the main island of the Canary Islands, is conquered by the Kingdom of Castile.

title: Battle of Camarón
fact: 1863 — A 65-man French Foreign Legion infantry patrol fights a force of nearly 2,000 Mexican soldiers to nearly the last man in Hacienda Camarón, Mexico.

title: Niagara Falls State Park
fact: 1885 — Governor of New York David B. Hill signs legislation creating the Niagara Reservation, New York's first state park, ensuring that Niagara Falls will not be devoted solely to industrial and commercial use.

title: Great Exhibition
fact: 1851 — Queen Victoria opens The Great Exhibition at The Crystal Palace in London.

title: Haymarket affair
fact: 1886 — Rallies are held throughout the United States demanding the eight-hour work day, culminating in the Haymarket affair in Chicago, in commemoration of which May 1 is celebrated as International Workers' Day in many countries.

title: Benty Grange
fact: 1848 — The boar-crested Anglo-Saxon Benty Grange helmet is discovered in a barrow on the Benty Grange farm in Derbyshire.

title: Great Fire of 1901
fact: 1901 — The Great Fire of 1901 begins in Jacksonville, Florida.

title: Royal Albert Bridge
fact: 1859 — The Cornwall Railway opens across the Royal Albert Bridge linking Devon and Cornwall in England.

title: Dominican Monastery (Frankfurt)
fact: 1292 — Election of Count Adolf of Nassau as King of the Romans in the Dominican monastery of Frankfurt.

title: Huntington Avenue Grounds
fact: 1904 — Pitching against the Philadelphia Athletics at the Huntington Avenue Grounds, Cy Young of the Boston Americans throws the first perfect game in the modern era of baseball.

title: St Luke's Hospital for Lunatics
fact: 1757 — English poet Christopher Smart is admitted into St Luke's Hospital for Lunatics in London, beginning his six-year confinement to mental asylums.
story_label: Wikipedia: St Luke's Hospital for Lunatics

title: Tre Kronor (castle)
fact: 1697 — Stockholm's medieval castle Tre Kronor is destroyed by fire. It is replaced in the 18th century by the current Royal Palace.

title: Battle of the Îles Saint-Marcouf
fact: 1798 — French Revolutionary Wars: A French force attempting to dislodge a small British garrison on the Îles Saint-Marcouf is repulsed with heavy losses.
story_label: Wikipedia: Battle of the Îles Saint-Marcouf

title: Newport, Rhode Island
fact: 1639 — William Coddington founds Newport, Rhode Island.

title: Prague uprising
fact: 1945 — End of the Prague uprising, celebrated now as a national holiday in the Czech Republic.

title: Boston Tea Party
fact: 1773 — The Parliament of Great Britain passes the Tea Act, designed to save the British East India Company by reducing taxes on its tea and granting it the right to sell tea directly to North America. The legislation leads to the Boston Tea Party.

title: National Gallery
fact: 1824 — The National Gallery in London opens to the public.

title: Centennial Exposition
fact: 1876 — The Centennial Exposition is opened in Philadelphia.

title: Battle of Djerba
fact: 1560 — The Ottoman naval forces inflict a defeat on a Spanish fleet in the battle of Djerba. This marks the highpoint of Ottoman naval dominance in the Mediterranean, which starts declining five years later after the failed siege of Malta.

title: Bradford City stadium fire
fact: 1985 — Fifty-six spectators die and more than 200 are injured in the Bradford City stadium fire.

title: Palace of Blachernae
fact: 1157 — A church council presided over by Byzantine emperor Manuel I Komnenos in the Palace of Blachernae investigates the orthodoxy of the patriarch of Antioch, Soterichos Panteugenos.

title: Silverstone Circuit
fact: 1950 — The inaugural Formula One World Championship race takes place at Silverstone Circuit. The race was won by Giuseppe Farina, who would go on to become the inaugural champion that year.

title: Camp Dubois
fact: 1804 — William Clark and 42 men depart from Camp Dubois to join Meriwether Lewis at St Charles, Missouri, marking the beginning of the Lewis and Clark Expedition's historic journey up the Missouri River.

title: Nelson, New Zealand
fact: 1870 — The first game of rugby in New Zealand is played in Nelson between Nelson College and the Nelson Rugby Football Club.

title: Winnipeg general strike
fact: 1919 — The Winnipeg general strike begins. By 11:00, almost the whole working population of Winnipeg had walked off the job.

title: John F. Kennedy International Airport
fact: 1951 — The first regularly scheduled transatlantic flights begin between Idlewild Airport (now John F Kennedy International Airport) in New York City and Heathrow Airport in London, operated by El Al Israel Airlines.
story_label: Wikipedia: John F. Kennedy International Airport

title: Church of Scotland
fact: 1843 — The Disruption in Edinburgh of the Free Church of Scotland from the Church of Scotland.

title: Rosenborg BK
fact: 1917 — The Norwegian football club Rosenborg BK is founded.

title: Schloss Weimar
fact: 1714 — Johann Sebastian Bach leads the first performance of his cantata for Pentecost, Erschallet, ihr Lieder, BWV 172, at the chapel of Schloss Weimar.

title: Church of St. Mary of Blachernae
fact: 1347 — Coronation of John VI Kantakouzenos as Byzantine Emperor by patriarch Isidore I of Constantinople at the Church of St. Mary of Blachernae.
story_label: Wikipedia: Church of St. Mary of Blachernae

title: Rigi
fact: 1871 — Opening of the first rack railway in Europe, the Rigi Bahnen on Mount Rigi.

title: Manchester Ship Canal
fact: 1894 — The Manchester Ship Canal in the United Kingdom is officially opened by Queen Victoria, who later knights its designer Sir Edward Leader Williams.

title: Pedra Branca, Singapore
fact: 2008 — The International Court of Justice (ICJ) awards Middle Rocks to Malaysia and Pedra Branca (Pulau Batu Puteh) to Singapore, ending a 29-year territorial dispute between the two countries.

title: Uppsala Cathedral
fact: 1276 — Magnus Ladulås is crowned King of Sweden in Uppsala Cathedral.

title: Christ Church Cathedral, Dublin
fact: 1487 — The ten-year-old Lambert Simnel is crowned in Christ Church Cathedral, Dublin, Ireland, with the name of Edward VI in a bid to threaten King Henry VII's reign.

title: Ashmolean Museum
fact: 1683 — The Ashmolean Museum in Oxford, England, opens as the world's first university museum.

title: León Cathedral
fact: 1135 — Alfonso VII of León and Castile is crowned in León Cathedral as Imperator totius Hispaniae (Emperor of all of Spain).

title: Milan Cathedral
fact: 1805 — Napoléon Bonaparte assumes the title of King of Italy and is crowned with the Iron Crown of Lombardy in Milan Cathedral, the gothic cathedral in Milan.

title: 24 Hours of Le Mans
fact: 1923 — The first 24 Hours of Le Mans is held in France. Run annually in June thereafter, it became the oldest endurance racing event in the world.

title: Tampa Bay
fact: 1539 — In Florida, Hernando de Soto lands at Tampa Bay with 600 soldiers with the goal of finding gold.

title: Pont Neuf
fact: 1578 — King Henry III lays the first stone of the Pont Neuf (New Bridge), the oldest bridge of Paris, France.

title: Strait of Juan de Fuca
fact: 1790 — Manuel Quimper explores the Strait of Juan de Fuca.
story_label: Wikipedia: Strait of Juan de Fuca

title: Glorious First of June
fact: 1794 — The battle of the Glorious First of June is fought, the first naval engagement between Britain and France during the French Revolutionary Wars.

title: Diamond Rock
fact: 1805 — Napoleonic Wars: A Franco-Spanish fleet recaptures from the British the island of Diamond Rock, which guards the entrance to the bay leading to Fort-de-France, Martinique.

title: Baikonur
fact: 2003 — Europe launches its first voyage to another planet, Mars. The European Space Agency's Mars Express probe launches from the Baikonur space center in Kazakhstan.

title: Ixtoc I oil spill
fact: 1979 — A blowout at the Ixtoc I oil well in the southern Gulf of Mexico causes at least 3,000,000 barrels (480,000 m3) of oil to be spilled into the waters, the second-worst accidental oil spill ever recorded.

title: Great Seattle Fire
fact: 1889 — The Great Seattle Fire destroys all of downtown Seattle.

title: Battle of Ameixial
fact: 1663 — Portuguese Restoration War: Portuguese victory at the Battle of Ameixial ensures Portugal's independence from Spain.

title: Siena Cathedral
fact: 1311 — Duccio's Maestà, a seminal artwork of the early Italian Renaissance, is unveiled and installed in Siena Cathedral in Siena, Italy.

title: Battle of Arklow
fact: 1798 — Irish Rebellion of 1798: Battles of Arklow and Saintfield.

title: Mount Lebanon
fact: 1861 — The Beyoglu Protocol turns the district of Mount Lebanon into an autonomous region within the Ottoman Empire and grants the Christians more power over the Druze.

title: The Blackstone Hotel
fact: 1920 — During the U.S. Republican National Convention in Chicago, U.S. Republican Party leaders gather in a room at the Blackstone Hotel to come to a consensus on their candidate for the U.S. presidential election…

title: Tambov Rebellion
fact: 1921 — Mikhail Tukhachevsky orders the use of chemical weapons against the Tambov Rebellion, bringing an end to the peasant uprising.

title: Veterans Stadium
fact: 1973 — In a game versus the Philadelphia Phillies at Veterans Stadium, Los Angeles Dodgers teammates Steve Garvey, Davey Lopes, Ron Cey and Bill Russell play together as an infield for the first time…

title: Fort Andross
fact: 1632 — The Plymouth Company grants a land patent to Thomas Purchase, the first settler of Pejepscot, Maine, settling at the site of Fort Andross.

title: Switchback Railway
fact: 1884 — The first purpose-built roller coaster, LaMarcus Adna Thompson's "Switchback Railway", opens in New York's Coney Island amusement park.

title: Turku Cathedral
fact: 1300 — Turku Cathedral is consecrated by Bishop Magnus I in the city of Turku (Swedish: Åbo).

title: Aletschhorn
fact: 1859 — First ascent of Aletschhorn, second summit of the Bernese Alps.

title: Waldorf Astoria New York
fact: 1948 — Columbia Records introduces the long-playing record album in a public demonstration at the Waldorf-Astoria Hotel in New York City.

title: Roanoke Island
fact: 1586 — English colonists leave Roanoke Island, after failing to establish England's first permanent settlement in North America.

title: Grand Theatre, Warsaw
fact: 1926 — King Roger, an opera about Roger II of Sicily by Karol Szymanowski, is premiered at the Grand Theatre in Warsaw.

title: Bridgwater
fact: 1685 — Monmouth Rebellion: James Scott, 1st Duke of Monmouth declares himself King of England at Bridgwater.

title: Kiel Canal
fact: 1895 — The Kiel Canal, crossing the base of the Jutland peninsula and the busiest artificial waterway in the world, is officially opened.

title: Psara
fact: 1824 — Greek War of Independence: Egyptian forces capture Psara in the Aegean Sea.

title: Prince Edward Theatre
fact: 1978 — The original production of Tim Rice and Andrew Lloyd Webber's musical, Evita, based on the life of Eva Perón, opens at the Prince Edward Theatre, London.

title: International Olympic Committee
fact: 1894 — The International Olympic Committee is founded at the Sorbonne in Paris, at the initiative of Baron Pierre de Coubertin.

title: Aqua Traiana
fact: 109 CE — Roman emperor Trajan inaugurates the Aqua Traiana, an aqueduct that channels water from Lake Bracciano, 40 kilometres (25 miles) northwest of Rome.

title: Pribilof Islands
fact: 1786 — Gavriil Pribylov discovers St. George Island of the Pribilof Islands in the Bering Sea.

title: Padma Bridge
fact: 2022 — The prime minister of Bangladesh, Sheikh Hasina inaugurates the longest bridge of Bangladesh, Padma Bridge.

title: Hong Kong Island
fact: 1843 — Treaty of Nanking comes into effect; Hong Kong Island is ceded to the British "in perpetuity".

title: Hyde Park, London
fact: 1857 — The first investiture of the Victoria Cross takes place in Hyde Park, London.

title: Illinois Monument
fact: 1914 — The Illinois Monument is dedicated at Cheatham Hill in what is now the Kennesaw Mountain National Battlefield Park.

title: Salle Le Peletier
fact: 1841 — The Paris Opera Ballet premieres Giselle in the Salle Le Peletier.

title: Nakhla meteorite
fact: 1911 — The Nakhla meteorite, the first one to suggest signs of aqueous processes on Mars, falls to Earth, landing in Egypt.

title: Villa Park
fact: 1948 — Boxer Dick Turpin beats Vince Hawkins at Villa Park in Birmingham to become the first black British boxing champion in the modern era.

title: Globe Theatre
fact: 1613 — The Globe Theatre in London, built by William Shakespeare's playing company, the Lord Chamberlain's Men, burns to the ground.

title: Oxford University Museum of Natural History
fact: 1860 — The 1860 Oxford evolution debate at the Oxford University Museum of Natural History takes place.
story_label: Wikipedia: Oxford University Museum of Natural History

title: Battle of Göllheim
fact: 1298 — Battle of Göllheim: Albert I of Habsburg defeats Adolf of Nassau-Weilburg.

title: Siege of Salvador (1822–1823)
fact: 1823 — Bahia Independence Day: The Siege of Salvador ends Portuguese rule in Brazil, with the final defeat of the Portuguese crown loyalists in the province of Bahia.

title: Pitcairn Island
fact: 1767 — Pitcairn Island is discovered by Midshipman Robert Pitcairn on an expeditionary voyage commanded by Philip Carteret.

title: Eternal Light Peace Memorial
fact: 1938 — United States President Franklin D. Roosevelt dedicates the Eternal Light Peace Memorial and lights the eternal flame at Gettysburg Battlefield.

title: Yankee Stadium (1923)
fact: 1939 — Lou Gehrig, recently diagnosed with Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, informs a crowd at Yankee Stadium that he considers himself "The luckiest man on the face of the earth", then announces his retirement from major league baseball.

title: Sucidava
fact: 328 CE — The official opening of Constantine's Bridge built over the Danube between Sucidava (Corabia, Romania) and Oescus (Gigen, Bulgaria) by the Roman architect Theophilus Patricius.

title: Kolozsmonostor Abbey
fact: 1438 — A temporary compromise between the rebellious Transylvanian peasants and the noblemen is signed in Kolozsmonostor Abbey.

title: Battle of Malta (1283)
fact: 1283 — Roger of Lauria, commanding the Aragonese fleet, defeats an Angevin fleet sent to put down a rebellion on Malta.

title: Battle of Dynekilen
fact: 1716 — The Battle of Dynekilen forces Sweden to abandon its invasion of Norway.

title: Sacajawea State Park
fact: 1811 — Explorer David Thompson posts a sign near what is now Sacajawea State Park in Washington state, claiming the Columbia District for the United Kingdom.

title: Honshu
fact: 869 CE — The 8.4–9.0 Mw Sanriku earthquake strikes the area around Sendai in northern Honshu, Japan. Inundation from the tsunami extended several kilometers inland.

title: Soldier Field
fact: 1966 — The Chicago Freedom Movement, co-founded by Martin Luther King Jr., holds a rally at Soldier Field in Chicago; as many as 60,000 people attend.

title: Spitsbergen
fact: 1897 — Salomon August Andrée leaves Spitsbergen to attempt to reach the North Pole by balloon.

title: Charleston Workhouse Slave Rebellion
fact: 1849 — The Charleston Workhouse Slave Rebellion begins in Charleston, South Carolina, United States.

title: Linnanmäki
fact: 1951 — Vuoristorata, one of the oldest still-operating wooden roller coasters in Europe, is opened at the Linnanmäki amusement park in Helsinki, Finland.

title: Exhibition of the Industry of All Nations
fact: 1853 — Opening of the first major US world's fair, the Exhibition of the Industry of All Nations in New York City.
story_label: Wikipedia: Exhibition of the Industry of All Nations

title: Canterbury
fact: 1207 — King John of England expels Canterbury monks for supporting Archbishop Stephen Langton.

title: Mont Blanc Tunnel
fact: 1965 — The Mont Blanc Tunnel linking France and Italy opens.

title: Dent Blanche
fact: 1862 — First ascent of Dent Blanche, one of the highest summits in the Alps.

title: Saguenay flood
fact: 1996 — Storms provoke severe flooding on the Saguenay River, beginning one of Quebec's costliest natural disasters ever.

title: SS Great Britain
fact: 1843 — Brunel's steamship the SS Great Britain is launched, becoming the first ocean-going craft with an iron hull and screw propeller, becoming the largest vessel afloat in the world.

title: Pendine Sands
fact: 1925 — Malcolm Campbell becomes the first man to exceed 150 mph (241 km/h) on land. At Pendine Sands in Wales, he drives Sunbeam 350HP built by Sunbeam at a two-way average speed of 150.33 mph (242 km/h).

title: Pikes Peak
fact: 1893 — Katharine Lee Bates writes "America the Beautiful" after admiring the view from the top of Pikes Peak near Colorado Springs, Colorado.

title: Fort Pontchartrain du Détroit
fact: 1701 — Antoine de la Mothe Cadillac founds the trading post at Fort Pontchartrain, which later becomes the city of Detroit.

title: King's College Chapel, Cambridge
fact: 1441 — King Henry VI of England lays the foundation stone of King's College Chapel, Cambridge.

title: Kadriorg Palace
fact: 1718 — At the behest of Tsar Peter the Great, the construction of Kadriorg Palace, dedicated to his wife Catherine, begins in Tallinn.

title: Valentia Island
fact: 1866 — The first permanent transatlantic telegraph cable is successfully completed, stretching from Valentia Island, Ireland, to Heart's Content, Newfoundland.

title: Puijo tower
fact: 1963 — The Puijo observation tower is opened to the general public at Puijo Hill in Kuopio, Finland.

title: Quecreek Mine rescue
fact: 2002 — Nine coal miners trapped in the flooded Quecreek Mine in Somerset County, Pennsylvania, are rescued after 77 hours underground.

title: Link River Dam
fact: 1920 — Construction of the Link River Dam begins as part of the Klamath Reclamation Project.

title: Siege of Jerusalem (587 BC)
fact: 587 BCE — The Neo-Babylonian Empire sacks Jerusalem and destroys the First Temple.

title: Guanaja
fact: 1502 — Christopher Columbus lands at Guanaja in the Bay Islands off the coast of Honduras during his fourth voyage.

title: Grand Combin
fact: 1859 — First ascent of Grand Combin, one of the highest summits in the Alps.

title: Wilberforce Monument
fact: 1834 — Construction begins on the Wilberforce Monument in Kingston Upon Hull.

title: Brownsea Island Scout camp
fact: 1907 — The start of the first Scout camp on Brownsea Island, the origin of the worldwide Scouting movement.

title: Jungfrau
fact: 1811 — First ascent of Jungfrau, third highest summit in the Bernese Alps by brothers Johann Rudolf and Hieronymus Meyer.

title: Great Spokane Fire
fact: 1889 — The Great Fire of Spokane, Washington destroys some 32 blocks of the city, prompting a mass rebuilding project.

title: Second Temple
fact: 70 CE — Fires resulting from the destruction of the Second Temple in Jerusalem are extinguished.

title: Brooklands
fact: 1926 — The first British Grand Prix was held at Brooklands.

title: Peace Bridge
fact: 1927 — The Peace Bridge opens between Fort Erie, Ontario and Buffalo, New York.

title: Uraniborg
fact: 1576 — The cornerstone for Tycho Brahe's Uraniborg observatory is laid on the island of Hven.

title: Republic of Ploiești
fact: 1870 — The Republic of Ploiești, a failed Radical-Liberal rising against Domnitor Carol of Romania.

title: Rocky Mountains
fact: 1842 — The Webster–Ashburton Treaty is signed, establishing the United States–Canada border east of the Rocky Mountains.

title: Eiger
fact: 1858 — The Eiger in the Bernese Alps is ascended for the first time by Charles Barrington accompanied by Christian Almer and Peter Bohren.

title: League Park
fact: 1929 — Babe Ruth becomes the first baseball player to hit 500 home runs in his career with a home run at League Park in Cleveland, Ohio.

title: ʻIolani Palace
fact: 1898 — The Hawaiian flag is lowered from ʻIolani Palace in an elaborate annexation ceremony and replaced with the flag of the United States to signify the transfer of sovereignty from the Republic of Hawaii to the United States where it is formally recognized as Hawaii.

title: Atlanta–Fulton County Stadium
fact: 1984 — An infamous brawl takes place at the Atlanta-Fulton County Stadium between the Atlanta Braves and San Diego Padres.

title: Enryaku-ji
fact: 1536 — Buddhist monks from Kyoto, Japan's Enryaku-ji temple set fire to 21 Nichiren temples throughout Kyoto in what will be known as the Tenbun Hokke Disturbance.

title: Bayreuth Festival
fact: 1876 — A performance of Wagner's Das Rheingold opens the first Ring cycle at the first Bayreuth Festival.

title: Saint-Domingue
fact: 1791 — Slaves from plantations in Saint-Domingue hold a Vodou ceremony led by houngan Dutty Boukman at Bois Caïman, marking the start of the Haitian Revolution.

title: Vardzia
fact: 1185 — The cave city of Vardzia is consecrated by Queen Tamar of Georgia.

title: San Sebastian Church (Manila)
fact: 1891 — The Basilica of San Sebastian, Manila, the first all-steel church in Asia, is officially inaugurated and blessed.

title: Wave Hill walk-off
fact: 1975 — Australian Prime Minister Gough Whitlam symbolically hands over land to the Gurindji people after the eight-year Wave Hill walk-off, a landmark event in the history of Indigenous land rights in Australia, commemorated in a 1991 song by Paul Kelly and an annual celebration.

title: Pike Place Market
fact: 1907 — Pike Place Market, one of the oldest continuously operated public farmers' markets in the U.S. and a popular tourist attraction, opens in Seattle, Washington.

title: Sack of Shamakhi
fact: 1721 — The city of Shamakhi in Safavid Shirvan is sacked.

title: Thousand Islands Bridge
fact: 1938 — The Thousand Islands Bridge, connecting New York, United States, with Ontario, Canada, over the Saint Lawrence River, is dedicated by U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt.

title: Weisshorn
fact: 1861 — First ascent of Weisshorn, fifth highest summit in the Alps.

title: Kinmon incident
fact: 1864 — Bakumatsu: Kinmon incident: The Chōshū Domain attempts to expel the Satsuma and Aizu Domains from Japan's imperial court.

title: Stadtpark, Vienna
fact: 1862 — The Stadtpark, the first public park in Vienna, opens to the public.

title: Quebec expedition (1711)
fact: 1711 — Britain's Quebec Expedition loses eight ships and almost nine hundred soldiers, sailors and women to rocks at Pointe-aux-Anglais.

title: Possession Island (Queensland)
fact: 1770 — James Cook names and lands on Possession Island, and claims the east coast of Australia for Britain as New South Wales.

title: Nat Turner's Rebellion
fact: 1831 — Nat Turner's rebellion of enslaved Virginians is suppressed.

title: Pontiac Silverdome
fact: 1975 — The Pontiac Silverdome opens in Pontiac, Michigan, 30 miles (48 km) northwest of Detroit, Michigan.

title: Angoulême Cathedral
fact: 1200 — King John of England, signer of the first Magna Carta, marries Isabella of Angoulême in Angoulême Cathedral.

title: European Southern Observatory
fact: 2016 — Proxima Centauri b, the closest exoplanet to Earth, is discovered by the European Southern Observatory.

title: Battle of Castlebar
fact: 1798 — Wolfe Tone's United Irish and French forces clash with the British Army in the Battle of Castlebar, part of the Irish Rebellion of 1798, resulting in the creation of the French puppet Republic of Connacht.

title: Calder Hall nuclear power station
fact: 1956 — The nuclear power station at Calder Hall in the United Kingdom was connected to the national power grid becoming the world's first commercial nuclear power station to generate electricity on an industrial scale.
story_label: Wikipedia: Calder Hall nuclear power station

title: Atauro
fact: 1975 — The Governor of Portuguese Timor abandons its capital, Dili, and flees to Atauro Island, leaving control to a rebel group.

title: Mainz Cathedral
fact: 1009 — Mainz Cathedral suffers extensive damage from a fire, which destroys the building on the day of its inauguration.

title: Mount Washington Cog Railway
fact: 1869 — The Mount Washington Cog Railway opens, making it the world's first mountain-climbing rack railway.

title: Edo Castle
fact: 1590 — Tokugawa Ieyasu enters Edo Castle. (Traditional Japanese date: August 1, 1590)

title: Battle of Jonesborough
fact: 1864 — American Civil War: The Battle of Jonesborough, the culmination of the Atlanta campaign, begins as Union forces under General William T. Sherman clash with Confederate troops under General William J. Hardee south of Atlanta.

title: Lund Cathedral
fact: 1145 — The main altar of Lund Cathedral, at the time the seat of the archiepiscopal see of all the Nordic countries, is consecrated.

title: Old town of Visoki
fact: 1355 — King Tvrtko I of Bosnia writes In castro nostro Vizoka vocatum from the Old town of Visoki.

title: Royal Exchange, London
fact: 1666 — The Royal Exchange burns down in the Great Fire of London.

title: Pearl Street Station
fact: 1882 — The Pearl Street Station in New York City becomes the first power plant to supply electricity to paying customers.

title: Fort Robinson
fact: 1877 — American Indian Wars: Oglala Sioux chief Crazy Horse is bayoneted by a United States soldier after resisting confinement in a guardhouse at Fort Robinson in Nebraska.

title: Gotthard Road Tunnel
fact: 1980 — The Gotthard Road Tunnel opens in Switzerland as the world's longest highway tunnel at 16.9 kilometres (10.5 mi) stretching from Göschenen to Airolo.

title: Greenham Common Women's Peace Camp
fact: 1981 — The first women arrive at what becomes Greenham Common Women's Peace Camp in the UK.
story_label: Wikipedia: Greenham Common Women's Peace Camp

title: La Gomera
fact: 1492 — Christopher Columbus sails from La Gomera in the Canary Islands, his final port of call before crossing the Atlantic Ocean for the first time.

title: Pan-American Exposition
fact: 1901 — Leon Czolgosz, an unemployed anarchist, shoots and fatally wounds US president William McKinley at the Pan-American Exposition in Buffalo, New York.

title: Pro Football Hall of Fame
fact: 1963 — The Pro Football Hall of Fame opens in Canton, Ohio with 17 charter members.
story_label: Wikipedia: Pro Football Hall of Fame

title: Anglican Diocese of Cape Town
fact: 1986 — Desmond Tutu becomes the first black man to lead the Anglican Diocese of Cape Town.
story_label: Wikipedia: Anglican Diocese of Cape Town

title: Piazza della Signoria
fact: 1504 — Michelangelo's David is unveiled in Piazza della Signoria in Florence.

title: Rising of the Priests
fact: 1775 — The unsuccessful Rising of the Priests in Malta.

title: Millennium of Russia
fact: 1862 — Millennium of Russia monument is unveiled in Novgorod.

title: Milwaukee Mile
fact: 1903 — The first race at the Milwaukee Mile in West Allis, Wisconsin is held. It is the oldest major speedway in the world.

title: Newport Transporter Bridge
fact: 1906 — The Newport Transporter Bridge is opened in Newport, South Wales by Viscount Tredegar.

title: Waldbühne
fact: 1964 — Martin Luther King Jr. addresses a crowd of 20,000 West Berliners on Sunday, in Waldbühne.

title: Bishop Gore School
fact: 1682 — Bishop Gore School, one of the oldest schools in Wales, is founded.

title: Fort Manoel
fact: 1723 — Grand Master António Manoel de Vilhena lays down the first stone of Fort Manoel in Malta.

title: Cannikin
fact: 1971 — The first Greenpeace ship departs from Vancouver to protest against the upcoming Cannikin nuclear weapon test in Alaska.

title: Robert College
fact: 1863 — Robert College, in Istanbul, the first American educational institution outside the United States, is founded by Christopher Robert, an American philanthropist.

title: East Germany balloon escape
fact: 1979 — Eight people escape from East Germany to the west in a homemade hot air balloon.

title: San Pedro Bay (Chile)
fact: 1544 — The expedition of Juan Bautista Pastene makes landfall in San Pedro Bay, southern Chile, claiming the territory for Spain.

title: San Siro
fact: 1926 — Football stadium San Siro is inaugurated in Milan, Italy

title: Glastonbury Festival
fact: 1970 — Michael Eavis hosts the first Glastonbury Festival.

title: Battle of Lincoln (1217)
fact: 1217 — Following the French defeat in the battle of Lincoln, Prince Louis of France ratifies the treaty of Lambeth under which he abandons all claims to the English throne and returns to France in exchange of an indemnity payment.

title: Kōtoku-in
fact: 1498 — The Nankai tsunami washes away the building housing the Great Buddha at Kōtoku-in; it has been located outside ever since.

title: Nukapu
fact: 1871 — Bishop John Coleridge Patteson, first bishop of Melanesia, is martyred on Nukapu, now in the Solomon Islands.

title: St. Olaf's Church, Tyrvää
fact: 1997 — St. Olaf's Church, a stone church from the 16th century in Tyrvää, Finland, is burnt down by a burglar.

title: Battle of Blore Heath
fact: 1459 — The Battle of Blore Heath, the first major battle of the English Wars of the Roses, is won by the Yorkists.

title: Little Rock Central High School
fact: 1957 — Little Rock schools integration crisis: President Dwight D. Eisenhower sends the 101st Airborne Division to Little Rock, Arkansas, and federalizes the Arkansas National Guard, ordering both to support the integration of Little Rock Central High School.
story_label: Wikipedia: Little Rock Central High School

title: Meuse–Argonne offensive
fact: 1918 — World War I: The Meuse-Argonne Offensive began which would last until the total surrender of German forces.

title: Ford Piquette Avenue Plant
fact: 1908 — Production of the Model T automobile begins at the Ford Piquette Avenue Plant in Detroit.

title: Battle of Mühldorf
fact: 1322 — Louis IV, Holy Roman Emperor, defeats Frederick I of Austria in the Battle of Mühldorf.

title: Washington National Cathedral
fact: 1907 — The cornerstone is laid at the Cathedral Church of Saint Peter and Saint Paul (better known as Washington National Cathedral) in Washington, D.C.

title: Tampere Hall
fact: 1990 — The Tampere Hall, the largest concert and congress center in the Nordic countries, is inaugurated in Tampere, Finland.

title: Maronite Church
fact: 1736 — The Lebanese Council of 1736 begins, a major turning point in the reform of the Maronite Church. In the following three days, the assembled Maronite and Latin clergy presided by Yusuf ibn Siman as-Simani discuss various reforms and elaborate rules and canons.

title: Vulcan Street Plant
fact: 1882 — Thomas Edison's first commercial hydroelectric power plant, the Vulcan Street Plant, begins operation.

title: Newark Liberty International Airport
fact: 1928 — Newark Liberty International Airport opens, becoming the first airport in the New York City metro area.

title: Opus Dei
fact: 1928 — The "Prelature of the Holy Cross and the Work of God", commonly known as Opus Dei, is founded.

title: Bushy Park
fact: 2004 — The first parkrun, then known as the Bushy Park Time Trial, takes place in Bushy Park, London, UK.

title: Montebello Islands
fact: 1952 — The United Kingdom successfully tests a nuclear weapon in the Montebello Islands, Western Australia, to become the world's third nuclear power.

title: Chalk River Laboratories
fact: 1986 — TASCC, a superconducting cyclotron at the Chalk River Laboratories in Canada, is officially opened.

title: Eastman tunnel
fact: 1869 — The Eastman tunnel, in Minnesota, United States, collapses during construction, causing a landslide that nearly destroys St. Anthony Falls.

title: Enrico Fermi Nuclear Generating Station
fact: 1966 — A reactor at the Enrico Fermi Nuclear Generating Station near Detroit suffers a partial meltdown.
story_label: Wikipedia: Enrico Fermi Nuclear Generating Station

title: Qantas Flight 72
fact: 2008 — Qantas Flight 72 experiences an in-flight upset near Exmouth, Western Australia, Australia, injuring 112.

title: Siege of Alkmaar
fact: 1573 — The Spanish siege of Alkmaar ends with the first Dutch victory in the Eighty Years' War.

title: New York Harbor
fact: 1825 — Restauration arrives in New York Harbor from Norway, the first organized immigration from Norway to the United States.

title: Battle of Camperdown
fact: 1797 — The Royal Navy decisively defeats the Batavian Navy at Camperdown during the French Revolutionary Wars.

title: Morant Bay rebellion
fact: 1865 — Hundreds of black men and women march in Jamaica, starting the Morant Bay rebellion.

title: San Salvador Island
fact: 1492 — Christopher Columbus's first expedition makes landfall on San Salvador Island in the Caribbean. (Julian calendar)

title: Old East
fact: 1793 — The cornerstone of Old East, the oldest state university building in the United States, is laid at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill.

title: Battle of Old Byland
fact: 1322 — Robert the Bruce of Scotland defeats King Edward II of England at the Battle of Old Byland, forcing Edward to accept Scotland's independence.

title: Senghenydd colliery disaster
fact: 1913 — Senghenydd colliery disaster, the United Kingdom's worst coal mining accident, claims the lives of 439 miners.

title: Wrigley Field
fact: 2003 — The Steve Bartman Incident takes place at Wrigley Field in Chicago, Illinois.

title: Siege of Vienna (1529)
fact: 1529 — The Siege of Vienna ends when Austria routs the invading Ottoman forces, ending its European expansion.

title: LaGuardia Airport
fact: 1939 — The New York Municipal Airport (later renamed LaGuardia Airport) is dedicated.

title: University of Utah
fact: 1991 — The "Oh-My-God particle", an ultra-high-energy cosmic ray measured at 40,000,000 times that of the highest energy protons produced in a particle accelerator, is observed at the University of Utah HiRes observatory in Dugway Proving Ground, Utah.

title: Tomb of Seti I
fact: 1817 — Italian explorer and archaeologist Giovanni Belzoni, uncovered the Tomb of Seti I in the Valley of the Kings.

title: Bibliotheca Alexandrina
fact: 2002 — The Bibliotheca Alexandrina opens in Egypt, commemorating the ancient library of Alexandria.

title: Presidents North Carolina Gave the Nation
fact: 1948 — Presidents North Carolina Gave the Nation, a monument honoring three presidents of the United States, was dedicated at the North Carolina State Capitol in Raleigh, North Carolina.
story_label: Wikipedia: Presidents North Carolina Gave the Nation

title: Boston Harbor
fact: 1797 — In Boston Harbor, the 44-gun United States Navy frigate USS Constitution is launched.

title: Battle of Sark
fact: 1448 — Scotland wins a decisive victory over England at the Battle of Sark, the last pitched battle to be fought between the two kingdoms during the Medieval period.

title: Sheffield F.C.
fact: 1857 — Sheffield F.C., the world's oldest association football club still in operation, is founded in England.

title: Uspenski Cathedral
fact: 1868 — The Uspenski Cathedral, designed by Aleksey Gornostayev, is inaugurated in Helsinki, Finland.

title: Malleco Viaduct
fact: 1890 — Malleco Viaduct in Chile, at the time "the highest railroad bridge in the world", is inaugurated by President José Manuel Balmaceda.

title: American Museum of Natural History
fact: 1964 — Biggest jewel heist in American history when Murph the Surf and gang burgle the American Museum of Natural History stealing the Star of India and other gems.
story_label: Wikipedia: American Museum of Natural History

title: Leiden University Library
fact: 1587 — Leiden University Library opens its doors after its founding in 1575.

title: Liceo Classico Massimo d'Azeglio
fact: 1897 — Italian Sport-Club Juventus is founded by a group of students of Liceo Classico Massimo d'Azeglio.

title: Guadalcanal campaign
fact: 1942 — World War II: The Koli Point action begins during the Guadalcanal campaign and ends on November 12.

title: King William Street, London
fact: 1890 — City and South London Railway: London's first deep-level tube railway opens between King William Street and Stockwell.

title: Qantas Flight 32
fact: 2010 — Qantas Flight 32, an Airbus A380, suffers an uncontained engine failure over Indonesia shortly after taking off from Singapore, crippling the jet. The crew manage to safely return to Singapore, saving all 469 passengers and crew.

title: 1811 Independence Movement
fact: 1811 — Salvadoran priest José Matías Delgado rings the bells of La Merced church in San Salvador, calling for insurrection and launching the 1811 Independence Movement.

title: Last spike (Canadian Pacific Railway)
fact: 1885 — The completion of Canada's first transcontinental railway is symbolized by the Last Spike ceremony at Craigellachie, British Columbia.

title: Bodleian Library
fact: 1602 — The Bodleian Library at the University of Oxford is opened to the public.

title: NYU Langone Health
fact: 2023 — U.S. surgeons at NYU Langone Health announce the world's first whole eye transplant.

title: Ujiji
fact: 1871 — Henry Morton Stanley locates missing explorer and missionary, David Livingstone in Ujiji, near Lake Tanganyika, famously greeting him with the words, "Dr. Livingstone, I presume?"

title: Provincetown Harbor
fact: 1620 — The Mayflower Compact is signed in what is now Provincetown Harbor near Cape Cod.

title: San Francisco–Oakland Bay Bridge
fact: 1936 — In California, the San Francisco–Oakland Bay Bridge opens to traffic.

title: Musée Saint-Remi
fact: 954 CE — The 13-year-old Lothair III is crowned at the Abbey of Saint-Remi as king of the West Frankish Kingdom.

title: Chelsea F.C.
fact: 1945 — FC Dynamo Moscow open their exhibition tour of the United Kingdom with a 3–3 draw against Chelsea, breaking the record attendance for a British club football match.

title: Joensuu City Hall
fact: 1914 — The Joensuu City Hall, designed by Eliel Saarinen, was inaugurated in Joensuu, Finland.

title: Lions Gate Bridge
fact: 1938 — The Lions Gate Bridge, connecting Vancouver to the North Shore region, opens to traffic.

title: Battle of Cajamarca
fact: 1532 — Spanish conquest of the Inca Empire: Commanded by Francisco Pizarro, Spanish conquistadors under Hernando de Soto meet Incan Emperor Atahualpa for the first time outside Cajamarca, arranging for a meeting in the city plaza the following day.

title: Castellania (Valletta)
fact: 1760 — The secondly-built Castellania in Valletta is officially inaugurated with the blessing of the interior Chapel of Sorrows.

title: Siege of Lucknow
fact: 1857 — Second relief of Lucknow: Twenty-four Victoria Crosses are awarded, the most in a single day.

title: Schenley Park Casino
fact: 1896 — The Western Pennsylvania Hockey League, which later became the first ice hockey league to openly trade and hire players, began play at Pittsburgh's Schenley Park Casino.

title: Tartu Art Museum
fact: 1940 — The Tartu Art Museum is established in Tartu, Estonia.

title: Dulles International Airport
fact: 1962 — President John F. Kennedy dedicates Washington Dulles International Airport, serving the Washington, D.C., region.

title: Old St. Peter's Basilica
fact: 326 CE — The old St. Peter's Basilica is consecrated by Pope Sylvester I.

title: Gettysburg National Cemetery
fact: 1863 — American Civil War: U.S. President Abraham Lincoln delivers the Gettysburg Address at the dedication ceremony for the military cemetery at Gettysburg, Pennsylvania.

title: Verrazzano–Narrows Bridge
fact: 1964 — The Verrazzano–Narrows Bridge opens to traffic. At the time it is the world's longest bridge span.

title: Holy Trinity Cathedral of Tbilisi
fact: 2004 — The Holy Trinity Cathedral of Tbilisi, the largest religious building in Georgia, is consecrated.
story_label: Wikipedia: Holy Trinity Cathedral of Tbilisi

title: Mont Granier
fact: 1248 — An overnight landslide on the north side of Mont Granier, one of the largest historical rockslope failures ever recorded in Europe, destroys five villages.

title: Cathedral of St. Matthew the Apostle
fact: 1963 — State funeral of John F. Kennedy; after lying in state at the United States Capitol, a Requiem Mass takes place at Cathedral of St. Matthew the Apostle and the President is buried at Arlington National Cemetery.
story_label: Wikipedia: Cathedral of St. Matthew the Apostle

title: Maui
fact: 1778 — In the Hawaiian Islands, Captain James Cook becomes the first European to visit Maui.

title: Jerusalem Church (Berlin)
fact: 1727 — The foundation stone to the Jerusalem Church in Berlin is laid.

title: Notts County F.C.
fact: 1862 — Notts County F.C. is founded in Nottingham, England, making it the oldest professional Association football club in the world.

title: Jackson Park (Chicago)
fact: 1895 — The first American automobile race takes place over the 54 miles from Chicago's Jackson Park to Evanston, Illinois. Frank Duryea wins in approximately 10 hours.

title: FC Barcelona
fact: 1899 — FC Barcelona is founded by Catalan, Spanish and Englishmen. It later develops into one of Spanish and world football's most iconic and strongest teams.

title: Belfast City Hall
fact: 1995 — U.S. President Bill Clinton visits Northern Ireland and speaks in favor of the "Northern Ireland peace process" to a huge rally at Belfast City Hall; he calls IRA fighters "yesterday's men".

title: St James's Park
fact: 1662 — Diarist John Evelyn records skating on the frozen lake in St James's Park, London, watched by Charles II and Queen Catherine.

title: Lick Observatory
fact: 1904 — The Jovian moon Himalia is discovered by Charles Dillon Perrine at California's Lick Observatory.

title: Groote Schuur Hospital
fact: 1967 — At Groote Schuur Hospital in Cape Town, South Africa, a transplant team headed by Christiaan Barnard carries out the first heart transplant on a human (53-year-old Louis Washkansky).

title: Montreux Casino
fact: 1971 — During a concert by Frank Zappa and The Mothers of Invention at the Montreux Casino, an audience member fires a flare gun into the ceiling, causing a fire that destroys the venue. The incident served as the inspiration for Deep Purple's 1973 song Smoke on the Water.

title: Aswan Low Dam
fact: 1902 — The opening of the reservoir of the Aswan Dam in Egypt.

title: San Rafael Lake
fact: 1675 — Antonio de Vea expedition enters San Rafael Lake in western Patagonia.

title: Signal Hill, St. John's
fact: 1901 — Guglielmo Marconi receives the first transatlantic radio signal (the letter "S" [•••] in Morse Code), at Signal Hill in St John's, Newfoundland.

title: Battle of Alton
fact: 1643 — English Civil War: The Battle of Alton takes place in Hampshire.

title: Loew's Grand Theatre
fact: 1939 — Gone with the Wind (highest inflation adjusted grossing film) receives its premiere at Loew's Grand Theatre in Atlanta, Georgia, United States.

title: Sylhet Shahi Eidgah
fact: 1782 — British East India Company: Muharram Rebellion: Hada and Mada Miah lead the first anti-British uprising in the subcontinent against Robert Lindsay and his contingents in Sylhet Shahi Eidgah.

title: Kellingley Colliery
fact: 2015 — Kellingley Colliery, the last deep coal mine in Great Britain, closes.

title: São Paulo Museum of Art
fact: 2007 — The Portrait of Suzanne Bloch (1904), by the Spanish artist Pablo Picasso, and O Lavrador de Café by Brazilian modernist painter Cândido Portinari, are stolen from the São Paulo Museum of Art in Brazil. Both will be recovered a few weeks later.
story_label: Wikipedia: São Paulo Museum of Art

title: Torre Picasso
fact: 1999 — The Spanish Civil Guard intercepts a van loaded with 950 kg of explosives that ETA intended to use to blow up Torre Picasso in Madrid, Spain.

title: Ganges Canal
fact: 1851 — India's first freight train is operated in Roorkee, to transport material for the construction of the Ganges Canal.

title: Santiniketan
