fact: 1921 — Opening of Visva-Bharati College, also known as Santiniketan College, now Visva Bharati University, India.

title: Moscow State Academy of Choreography
fact: 1773 — Moscow State Academy of Choreography is founded under the reign of Catherine II. It is the second ballet school in Russia after Vaganova Academy of Russian Ballet.
story_label: Wikipedia: Moscow State Academy of Choreography

title: Nikolauskirche, Oberndorf
fact: 1818 — The first performance of "Silent Night" takes place in the Nikolauskirche in Oberndorf, Austria.

title: Temple of the Sun (Rome)
fact: 274 CE — A temple to Sol Invictus is dedicated in Rome by Emperor Aurelian.

title: RAF Woodbridge
fact: 1980 — Witnesses report the first of several sightings of unexplained lights near RAF Woodbridge, in Rendlesham Forest, Suffolk, England, United Kingdom, an incident called "Britain's Roswell".

title: Radio City Music Hall
fact: 1932 — Radio City Music Hall, "Showplace of the Nation", opens in New York City.

title: Cave of Swallows
fact: 1966 — The Cave of Swallows, the largest known cave shaft in the world, is discovered in Aquismón, San Luis Potosí, Mexico.

title: Capture of Savannah
fact: 1778 — American Revolutionary War: British forces under the command of Lieutenant Colonel Archibald Campbell defeat American forces under Major General Robert Howe and capture the port city of Savannah, Georgia.

title: Corral Bay
fact: 1670 — The expedition of John Narborough leaves Corral Bay, having surveyed the coast and lost four hostages to the Spanish.

title: Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas
fact: 1949 — The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas, the central bank of the Philippines, is established.

title: Palais Garnier
fact: 1875 — The Palais Garnier, one of the most famous opera houses in the world, is inaugurated in Paris.

title: Graniteville, South Carolina
fact: 2005 — A train collision in Graniteville, South Carolina, United States, releases about 60 tons of chlorine gas.

title: Calais
fact: 1785 — Frenchman Jean-Pierre Blanchard and American John Jeffries travel from Dover, England, to Calais, France, in a gas balloon.

title: Chonos Archipelago
fact: 1835 — HMS Beagle, with Charles Darwin on board, drops anchor off the Chonos Archipelago.

title: Trans-en-Provence
fact: 1981 — A local farmer reports a UFO sighting in Trans-en-Provence, France, claimed to be "perhaps the most completely and carefully documented sighting of all time".

title: Republika Srpska
fact: 1992 — The Assembly of the Serb People in Bosnia and Herzegovina proclaims the creation of Republika Srpska, a new state within Yugoslavia.

title: Spindletop
fact: 1901 — The first great Texas oil gusher is discovered at Spindletop in Beaumont, Texas.

title: Colony of Vancouver Island
fact: 1849 — Establishment of the Colony of Vancouver Island.

title: Reserve Bank of Australia
fact: 1960 — The Reserve Bank of Australia, the country's central bank and banknote issuing authority authorized by the 1959 Reserve Bank Act, is established.

title: Royal Society
fact: 1818 — A paper by David Brewster is read to the Royal Society, belatedly announcing his discovery of what we now call the biaxial class of doubly-refracting crystals. On the same day…

title: Antarctic Circle
fact: 1773 — Captain James Cook leads the first expedition to sail south of the Antarctic Circle.

title: Second Triumvirate
fact: 38 BCE — Octavian divorces his wife Scribonia and marries Livia Drusilla, ending the fragile peace between the Second Triumvirate and Sextus Pompey.

title: Teatro Filarmonico
fact: 1749 — The Teatro Filarmonico in Verona is destroyed by fire, as a result of a torch being left behind in the box of a nobleman after a performance. It is rebuilt in 1754.

title: Vilna Ghetto
fact: 1942 — The Jewish resistance organization, Fareynikte Partizaner Organizatsye, based in the Vilna Ghetto is established.

title: Liechtenstein
fact: 1719 — The Principality of Liechtenstein is created within the Holy Roman Empire.

title: Georgetown (Washington, D.C.)
fact: 1789 — Georgetown College, the first Catholic university in the United States, is founded in Georgetown, Maryland (now a part of Washington, D.C.) when Bishop John Carroll, Rev. Robert Molyneux, and Rev…

title: Operation Coburg
fact: 1968 — Vietnam War: The 1st Australian Task Force launches Operation Coburg against the North Vietnamese Army and Viet Cong during wider fighting around Long Bình and Biên Hòa.

title: Port Egmont
fact: 1765 — A British naval expedition arrives at and names Port Egmont in the Falkland Islands, founding a settlement there eight days later. (Arrival was 15 January 1765 O.S.)

title: Henry Morgan's Panama expedition
fact: 1671 — Original city of Panama (founded in 1519) is destroyed by a fire when privateer Henry Morgan sacks and sets fire to it. The site of the previously devastated city is still in ruins (see Panama Viejo).

title: Panama Canal Railway
fact: 1855 — A locomotive on the Panama Canal Railway runs from the Atlantic Ocean to the Pacific Ocean for the first time.

title: National Baseball Hall of Fame and Museum
fact: 1936 — The first inductees into the Baseball Hall of Fame are announced.
story_label: Wikipedia: National Baseball Hall of Fame and Museum

title: Hanthawaddy kingdom
fact: 1287 — King Wareru founds the Hanthawaddy kingdom, and proclaims independence from the Pagan Kingdom.

title: Skirmish at Bender
fact: 1713 — The Kalabalik or Skirmish at Bender results from the Ottoman Sultan Ahmed III's order that his unwelcome guest, King Charles XII of Sweden, be seized.

title: Upper Canada
fact: 1796 — The capital of Upper Canada is moved from Newark to York.

title: Texas Instruments
fact: 2000 — First digital cinema projection in Europe (Paris) realized by Philippe Binant with the DLP CINEMA technology developed by Texas Instruments.

title: British Hong Kong
fact: 1930 — The Communist Party of Vietnam is founded at a "Unification Conference" held in Kowloon, British Hong Kong.

title: French West Indies
fact: 1794 — The French legislature abolishes slavery throughout all territories of the French First Republic. It would be reestablished in the French West Indies in 1802.

title: Miami and Erie Canal
fact: 1825 — The Ohio Legislature authorizes the construction of the Ohio and Erie Canal and the Miami and Erie Canal.

title: Pagan Kingdom
fact: 1313 — King Thihathu founds the Pinya Kingdom as the de jure successor state of the Pagan Kingdom.

title: Battle of Mansurah (1250)
fact: 1250 — Seventh Crusade: Crusaders engage Ayyubid forces in the Battle of Al Mansurah.

title: La Scala
fact: 1893 — Verdi's last opera, Falstaff, premieres at La Scala, Milan.

title: Nombre de Jesús (Patagonia)
fact: 1584 — A naval expedition led by Pedro Sarmiento de Gamboa founds Nombre de Jesús, the first of two short-lived Spanish settlements in the Strait of Magellan.

title: Lourdes
fact: 1858 — Bernadette Soubirous's first vision of the Blessed Virgin Mary occurs in Lourdes, France.

title: National Gallery (Norway)
fact: 1994 — Four thieves break into the National Gallery of Norway and steal Edvard Munch's iconic painting The Scream.

title: Christ Church Cathedral, Oxford
fact: 1556 — Having been declared a heretic and laicized by Pope Paul IV on 4 December 1555, Archbishop of Canterbury Thomas Cranmer is publicly defrocked at Christ Church Cathedral.

title: Pavia
fact: 1002 — At an assembly at Pavia of Lombard nobles, Arduin of Ivrea is restored to his domains and crowned King of Italy.

title: MS Mikhail Lermontov
fact: 1986 — The Soviet liner MS Mikhail Lermontov runs aground in the Marlborough Sounds, New Zealand.

title: Kherrata
fact: 2021 — Five thousand people gathered in the town of Kherrata, Bejaia Province to mark the second anniversary of the Hirak protest movement. Demonstrations had been suspended because of the COVID-19 pandemic in Algeria.

title: Evangelistas Islets
fact: 1676 — Sixteen men of Pascual de Iriate's expedition are lost at Evangelistas Islets at the western end of the Strait of Magellan.

title: North Caucasus
fact: 1944 — The Soviet Union begins the forced deportation of the Chechen and Ingush people from the North Caucasus to Central Asia.

title: Piedra Movediza
fact: 1912 — The Piedra Movediza (Moving Stone) of Tandil falls and breaks.

title: Compiègne
fact: 888 CE — Odo, count of Paris, is crowned king of West Francia (France) by Archbishop Walter of Sens at Compiègne.

title: Vicenza
fact: 1585 — The Olympic Theatre, designed by Andrea Palladio, is inaugurated in Vicenza.

title: Shoshone National Forest
fact: 1891 — Shoshone National Forest is established as the first national forest in the US and world.

title: Parliament House, Helsinki
fact: 1931 — The Parliament House of Finland is officially inaugurated in Helsinki, Finland.

title: Kingdom of Ireland
fact: 1702 — Queen Anne, the younger sister of Mary II, becomes Queen regnant of England, Scotland, and Ireland.

title: Sakai incident
fact: 1868 — Sakai incident: Japanese samurai kill 11 French sailors in the port of Sakai, Osaka.

title: Rancho San Francisco
fact: 1842 — The first documented discovery of gold in California occurs at Rancho San Francisco, six years before the California Gold Rush.

title: Jagorawi Toll Road
fact: 1978 — President Soeharto inaugurates Jagorawi Toll Road, the first toll highway in Indonesia, connecting Jakarta, Bogor and Ciawi, West Java.

title: Province of Canada
fact: 1848 — Louis-Hippolyte Lafontaine and Robert Baldwin become the first Prime Ministers of the Province of Canada to be democratically elected under a system of responsible government.

title: Pelican Island National Wildlife Refuge
fact: 1903 — Pelican Island National Wildlife Refuge, the first national wildlife refuge in the US, is established by President Theodore Roosevelt.
story_label: Wikipedia: Pelican Island National Wildlife Refuge

title: Kraków Ghetto
fact: 1943 — The Holocaust: The liquidation of the Kraków Ghetto is completed.

title: The Oval
fact: 1872 — The Wanderers F.C. win the first FA Cup, the oldest football competition in the world, beating Royal Engineers A.F.C. 1–0 at The Oval in Kennington, London.

title: Rmelan
fact: 2016 — Rojava conflict: At a conference in Rmelan, the Movement for a Democratic Society declares the establishment of the Democratic Federation of Northern Syria.

title: Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum theft
fact: 1990 — In the largest art theft in US history, 12 paintings, collectively worth around $500 million, are stolen from the Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum in Boston.
story_label: Wikipedia: Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum theft

title: Principality of Wales
fact: 1284 — The Statute of Rhuddlan incorporates the Principality of Wales into England.

title: Credit Suisse
fact: 2023 — The Swiss Government brokers a deal for UBS to buy out rival Credit Suisse in an attempt to calm the 2023 banking crisis.

title: Opéra de Monte-Carlo
fact: 1925 — Ravel's opera L'enfant et les sortilèges, to a libretto by Colette, is premiered at the Opéra de Monte-Carlo.

title: San Diego Comic-Con
fact: 1970 — San Diego Comic-Con, the largest pop and culture festival in the world, hosts its inaugural event.

title: Port Chalmers
fact: 1848 — The ship John Wickliffe arrives at Port Chalmers carrying the first Scottish settlers for Dunedin, New Zealand. Otago province is founded.

title: Great Lakes
fact: 1920 — Palm Sunday tornado outbreak of 1920 affects the Great Lakes region and Deep South states.

title: French Madagascar
fact: 1947 — The Malagasy Uprising against French colonial rule begins in Madagascar.

title: Vézelay
fact: 1146 — Bernard of Clairvaux preaches his famous sermon in a field at Vézelay, urging the necessity of a Second Crusade. Louis VII is present, and joins the Crusade.

title: Catalonia
fact: 1706 — The last session of history of the Catalan Courts, the parliament of the Principality of Catalonia, ends. Catalonia's constitutional modernisation passed by the Courts aims to improve the guarantee of individual…

title: Bechuanaland Protectorate
fact: 1885 — The United Kingdom establishes the Bechuanaland Protectorate.

title: Bijeljina massacre
fact: 1992 — Forty-two civilians are massacred in the town of Bijeljina in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

title: Whitechapel
fact: 1888 — Jack the Ripper: The first of 11 unsolved brutal murders of women committed in or near the impoverished Whitechapel district in the East End of London, occurs.

title: French Sudan
fact: 1960 — France agrees to grant independence to the Mali Federation, a union of Senegal and French Sudan.

title: Septinsular Republic
fact: 1800 — The Treaty of Constantinople establishes the Septinsular Republic, the first autonomous Greek state since the Fall of the Byzantine Empire. (Under the Old Style calendar then still in use in the Ottoman Empire, the treaty was signed on 21 March.)

title: North Pole
fact: 1909 — Robert Peary and Matthew Henson become the first people to reach the North Pole; Peary's claim has been disputed because of failings in his navigational ability.

title: Passapatanzy, Virginia
fact: 1613 — Samuel Argall, having captured Pocahontas in Passapatanzy, Virginia, sets off with her to Jamestown with the intention of exchanging her for English prisoners held by her father.

title: Royal Academy of History
fact: 1738 — Real Academia de la Historia ("Royal Academy of History") is founded in Madrid.

title: International Court of Justice
fact: 1946 — The International Court of Justice holds its inaugural meeting in The Hague, Netherlands.

title: San Miguel, Chile
fact: 1925 — Colo-Colo, the most successful and popular soccer football team in the South American nation of Chile, was founded at the El Llano Stadium in San Miguel, Santiago, by footballer David Arellano and some of his teammates who had also left the Deportes Magallanes club.

title: Grays Ferry, Philadelphia
fact: 1789 — George Washington arrives at Grays Ferry, Philadelphia, while en route to Manhattan for his inauguration.

title: Duchy of Estonia (1219–1346)
fact: 1343 — St. George's Night Uprising commences in the Duchy of Estonia.

title: Flint water crisis
fact: 2014 — The Flint water crisis begins when officials at Flint, Michigan switch the city's water supply to the Flint River, leading to lead and bacteria contamination.

title: Cape Henry
fact: 1607 — The Virginia Company colonists make landfall at Cape Henry.

title: 801 Apennine earthquake
fact: 801 CE — An earthquake in the Central Apennines hits Rome and Spoleto, damaging the basilica of San Paolo Fuori le Mura.

title: Council of Constance
fact: 1415 — Religious reformer John Wycliffe is condemned as a heretic at the Council of Constance.

title: Hilderston, West Lothian
fact: 1608 — A newly nationalized silver mine in Scotland at Hilderston, West Lothian is re-opened by Bevis Bulmer.

title: Jagiellonian University
fact: 1364 — Jagiellonian University, the oldest university in Poland, is founded in Kraków.

title: Fátima, Portugal
fact: 1917 — Three children report the first apparition of Our Lady of Fátima in Fátima, Portugal.

title: First French Empire
fact: 1809 — Emperor Napoleon I orders the annexation of the Papal States to the French Empire.

title: Monaco
fact: 1814 — Occupation of Monaco changes from French to Austrian.

title: Sierra Gorda
fact: 1997 — The Sierra Gorda biosphere, the most ecologically diverse region in Mexico, is established as a result of grassroots efforts.

title: Matthew (1497 ship)
fact: 1497 — John Cabot sets sail from Bristol, England, on his ship Matthew looking for a route to the west (other documents give a May 2 date).

title: Kozhikode
fact: 1498 — Portuguese explorer Vasco da Gama discovers the sea route to India when he arrives at Kozhikode (previously known as Calicut), India.

title: Sack of Damietta (853)
fact: 853 CE — A Byzantine fleet sacks and destroys undefended Damietta in Egypt.

title: The Last Supper (Leonardo)
fact: 1999 — In Milan, Italy, after 22 years of restoration work, Leonardo da Vinci's masterpiece The Last Supper is put back on display.

title: North magnetic pole
fact: 1831 — James Clark Ross becomes the first European at the North Magnetic Pole.

title: 2008 Universal Studios fire
fact: 2008 — A fire on the back lot of Universal Studios breaks out, destroying the attraction King Kong Encounter and a large archive of master tapes for music and film, the full extent of which was not revealed until 2019.

title: 1950 French Annapurna expedition
fact: 1950 — Herzog and Lachenal of the French Annapurna expedition become the first climbers to reach the summit of an 8,000-metre peak.

title: Roquefort-sur-Soulzon
fact: 1411 — King Charles VI grants a monopoly for the ripening of Roquefort cheese to the people of Roquefort-sur-Soulzon, as they had been doing for centuries.

title: Puget Sound
fact: 1792 — Captain George Vancouver claims Puget Sound for the Kingdom of Great Britain.

title: Reims
fact: 1775 — The Coronation of Louis XVI in Reims, the last coronation before the French Revolution.

title: Blackheath, London
fact: 1381 — Peasants' Revolt: In England, rebels assemble at Blackheath, just outside London.

title: Woolwich Dockyard
fact: 1514 — Henry Grace à Dieu, at over 1,000 tons the largest warship in the world at this time, built at the new Woolwich Dockyard in England, is dedicated.

title: Battle of Rozgony
fact: 1312 — At the Battle of Rozgony, King Charles I of Hungary wins a decisive victory over the family of Palatine Amade Aba.

title: British North America
fact: 1846 — The Oregon Treaty extends the border between the United States and British North America, established by the Treaty of 1818, westward to the Pacific Ocean.

title: Assyrian eclipse
fact: 763 BCE — Assyrians record a solar eclipse that is later used to fix the chronology of Mesopotamian history.

title: Tennis Court Oath
fact: 1789 — Deputies of the French Third Estate take the Tennis Court Oath.

title: HMT Empire Windrush
fact: 1948 — The ship HMT Empire Windrush brought the first group of 802 West Indian immigrants to Tilbury, marking the start of modern immigration to the United Kingdom.

title: Elie, Manitoba
fact: 2007 — The small town of Elie, Manitoba is hit by Canada's most intense tornado on record.

title: Acadia
fact: 1713 — The French residents of Acadia are given one year to declare allegiance to Britain or leave Nova Scotia, Canada.

title: Field of the Cloth of Gold
fact: 1520 — The Field of the Cloth of Gold, a summit meeting between Henry VIII of England and Francis I of France, ends.
story_label: Wikipedia: Field of the Cloth of Gold

title: Dunhuang manuscripts
fact: 1900 — The Taoist monk Wang Yuanlu discovers the Dunhuang manuscripts, a cache of ancient texts that are of great historical and religious significance, in the Mogao Caves of Dunhuang, China.

title: Abbeville
fact: 1766 — François-Jean de la Barre, a young French nobleman, is tortured and beheaded before his body is burnt on a pyre along with a copy of Voltaire's Dictionnaire philosophique nailed to his torso for the crime of not saluting a Roman Catholic religious procession in Abbeville,…

title: British Somaliland
fact: 1960 — The Trust Territory of Somaliland (the former Italian Somaliland) gains its independence from Italy. Concurrently, it unites as scheduled with the five-day-old State of Somaliland (the former British Somaliland) to form the Somali Republic.

title: San Francisco Mint
fact: 1852 — Congress establishes the United States' 2nd mint in San Francisco.

title: Erie Canal
fact: 1817 — In Rome, New York, construction on the Erie Canal begins.

title: Patriarchate of Aquileia
fact: 1751 — Pope Benedict XIV suppresses the Patriarchate of Aquileia and establishes from its territory the Archdiocese of Udine and Gorizia.

title: Capitoline Hill
fact: 83 BCE — The Temple of Jupiter on the Capitoline Hill in Rome is burned down and the Sibylline books of prophecy destroyed with it.

title: Puebla (city)
fact: 2019 — The final Volkswagen Beetle rolls off the line in Puebla, Mexico; the last of 5,961 "Special Edition" cars will be exhibited in a museum.

title: Zheng He
fact: 1405 — Ming admiral Zheng He sets sail to explore the world for the first time.

title: Coutances
fact: 1476 — Giuliano della Rovere is appointed bishop of Coutances.

title: Deheubarth
fact: 927 CE — King Constantine II of Scotland, King Hywel Dda of Deheubarth, Ealdred of Bamburgh and King Owain of the Cumbrians accept the overlordship of King Æthelstan of England, leading to seven years of peace in the north.

title: Mission San Antonio de Padua
fact: 1771 — Foundation of the Mission San Antonio de Padua in modern California by the Franciscan friar Junípero Serra.
story_label: Wikipedia: Mission San Antonio de Padua

title: Mission San Diego de Alcalá
fact: 1769 — Father Junípero Serra founds California's first mission, Mission San Diego de Alcalá. Over the following decades, it evolves into the city of San Diego, California.
story_label: Wikipedia: Mission San Diego de Alcalá

title: Dieppe
fact: 1632 — Three hundred colonists bound for New France depart from Dieppe, France.

title: Surrey Iron Railway
fact: 1803 — The Surrey Iron Railway, arguably the world's first public railway, opens in south London, United Kingdom.

title: Catherine Labouré
fact: 1947 — In Vatican City, Rome, canonization of Catherine Labouré, the saint whose apparitions of the Virgin Mary originated the worldwide distribution of the Miraculous Medal.

title: Watkins Glen International
fact: 1973 — Summer Jam at Watkins Glen: Nearly 600,000 people attend a rock festival at the Watkins Glen International Raceway.

title: Kennewick Man
fact: 1996 — The remains of a prehistoric man are discovered near Kennewick, Washington. Such remains will be known as the Kennewick Man.

title: Amboise
fact: 1469 — Louis XI of France founds the chivalric order called the Order of Saint Michael in Amboise.

title: Tortona
fact: 461 CE — Western Roman Emperor Majorian is arrested near Tortona (northern Italy) and deposed by the Suebian general Ricimer.

title: Matica slovenská
fact: 1863 — Matica slovenská, Slovakia's public-law cultural and scientific institution focusing on topics around the Slovak nation, is established in Martin.

title: House of Representatives (Japan)
fact: 1991 — Takako Doi, chair of the Social Democratic Party, becomes Japan's first female speaker of the House of Representatives.

title: SS Deutschland (1900)
fact: 1900 — The steamer Deutschland of Hamburg America Lines sets a new record for the eastward passage when it docks in Plymouth, England, five days, 11 hours and 45 minutes after sailing from New York, breaking by three hours…

title: Chamberlain Basin
fact: 1948 — An Idaho Department of Fish and Game program to relocate beavers known as Beaver drop occurred. This program relocated beavers from Northwestern Idaho to Central Idaho by airplane and then parachuting the beavers into the Chamberlain Basin.

title: Secunderabad
fact: 1946 — The All Hyderabad Trade Union Congress is founded in Secunderabad.

title: Andorra
fact: 1933 — The Integral Nationalist Group wins the 1933 Andorran parliamentary election, the first election in Andorra held with universal male suffrage.

title: San Marino
fact: 301 CE — San Marino, one of the smallest nations in the world and the world's oldest republic still in existence, is founded by Saint Marinus.

title: Great Fire of Turku
fact: 1827 — The Great Fire of Turku almost completely destroys Finland's former capital city.

title: Battle of Qatwan
fact: 1141 — Yelü Dashi, the Liao dynasty general who founded the Qara Khitai, defeats the Seljuq and Kara-Khanid forces at the Battle of Qatwan.

title: Melfi
fact: 1089 — The first synod of pope Urban II starts in Melfi, with seventy bishops and twelve abbots in attendance. The synod issues several decrees about church law and deals with the relation with the Greek part of the Church.

title: Glastonbury Tor
fact: 1275 — An earthquake occurs in the south of Great Britain, notably causing multiple fatalities as well as destroying St Michael's Church on Glastonbury Tor.

title: Hope Diamond
fact: 1792 — The Hope Diamond is stolen along with other French crown jewels when six men break into the house where they are stored.

title: Northern Rock
fact: 2007 — Prelude to the 2008 financial crisis: Northern Rock bank experiences the first bank run in the United Kingdom in 150 years.

title: Pamir (ship)
fact: 1957 — Pamir, a four-masted barque, was shipwrecked and sank off the Azores during Hurricane Carrie.

title: Tammerkoski
fact: 1891 — The first hydropower plant of Finland is commissioned along the Tammerkoski rapids in Tampere, Pirkanmaa.

title: Duke of York's Picture House, Brighton
fact: 1910 — The Duke of York's Picture House opens in Brighton, now the oldest continually operating cinema in Britain.
story_label: Wikipedia: Duke of York's Picture House, Brighton

title: Cape Virgenes
fact: 1884 — On the night of 23–24 September, the steamship Arctique runs aground near Cape Virgenes leading to the discovery of nearby placer gold, beginning the Tierra del Fuego gold rush.

title: Locomotion No. 1
fact: 1825 — The world's first public railway to use steam locomotives, the Stockton and Darlington Railway, is ceremonially opened with the engine Locomotion pulling wagons with coal and passengers from Shildon to Darlington to Stockton.

title: Port of Iloilo
fact: 1855 — The Philippine port of Iloilo is opened to world trade by the Spanish administration.

title: Basutoland
fact: 1966 — Basutoland becomes independent from the United Kingdom and is renamed Lesotho.

title: Granite Railway
fact: 1826 — The Granite Railway begins operations as the first chartered railway in the U.S.

title: Jeanne Mance
fact: 1645 — Jeanne Mance opens the first lay hospital of North America in Montreal.

title: Second Hellenic Republic
fact: 1935 — In Greece, a coup d'état ends the Second Hellenic Republic.

title: Eliezer Ben-Yehuda
fact: 1881 — First known conversation in modern Hebrew by Eliezer Ben-Yehuda and friends.

title: 2010 Copiapó mining accident
fact: 2010 — The mining accident in Copiapó, Chile ends as all 33 trapped miners arrive at the surface after a record 69 days underground.

title: Warsaw Ghetto
fact: 1940 — Holocaust in Poland: The Warsaw Ghetto is established.

title: Burma Railway
fact: 1943 — The Burma Railway (Burma–Thailand Railway) is completed.

title: Frendraught Castle
fact: 1630 — Frendraught Castle in Scotland, the home of James Crichton of Frendraught, burns down.

title: British West Indies
fact: 1774 — American Revolution: The Continental Association, a nonconsumption and nonimportation agreement against the British Isles and the British West Indies, is adopted by the First Continental Congress.

title: Saint Pierre and Miquelon
fact: 1520 — João Álvares Fagundes discovers the islands of Saint Pierre and Miquelon, bestowing them their original name of "Islands of the 11,000 Virgins".

title: Siege of Plei Me
fact: 1965 — Vietnam War: The 1st Cavalry Division (Airmobile), in conjunction with the Army of the Republic of Vietnam, launches an operation seeking to destroy Communist forces during the siege of Plei Me.

title: West Florida
fact: 1810 — United States annexes the former Spanish colony of West Florida.

title: Union of South Africa
fact: 1922 — A referendum in Rhodesia rejects the country's annexation to the South African Union.

title: Antinoöpolis
fact: 130 CE — Emperor Hadrian establishes the city of Antinoöpolis on the Nile in honour of his companion Antinous, creating a new Hellenizing foundation in Roman Egypt.

title: Dutch East Indies
fact: 1949 — The Dutch–Indonesian Round Table Conference ends with the Netherlands agreeing to transfer sovereignty of the Dutch East Indies to the United States of Indonesia.

title: M10 motorway (Great Britain)
fact: 1959 — The first section of the M1 motorway, the first inter-urban motorway in the United Kingdom, is opened between the present junctions 5 and 18, along with the M10 motorway and M45 motorway.

title: 2008 Brazilian Grand Prix
fact: 2008 — Lewis Hamilton secured his maiden Formula One Drivers' Championship Title by one point ahead of Felipe Massa at the Brazilian Grand Prix, after a pass for fifth place against the Toyota of Timo Glock on the final lap of the race.

title: Fashoda Incident
fact: 1898 — France withdraws its troops from Fashoda (now in Sudan), ending the Fashoda Incident.

title: Teatro di San Carlo
fact: 1737 — The Teatro di San Carlo, the oldest working opera house in Europe, is inaugurated in Naples, Italy.

title: Tréguier
fact: 1499 — The Catholicon, written in 1464 by Jehan Lagadeuc in Tréguier, is published; this is the first Breton dictionary as well as the first French dictionary.

title: Republic of Negros
fact: 1898 — Negrese nationalists revolt against Spanish rule and establish the short-lived Republic of Negros.

title: Battle of Jemappes
fact: 1792 — Battle of Jemappes in the French Revolutionary Wars.

title: Ensisheim
fact: 1492 — The Ensisheim meteorite, the oldest meteorite with a known date of impact, strikes the Earth in a wheat field outside the village of Ensisheim, Alsace, France.

title: Tun Tavern
fact: 1775 — The United States Marine Corps is founded at Tun Tavern in Philadelphia by Samuel Nicholas.

title: Carnuntum
fact: 308 CE — At Carnuntum, Emperor emeritus Diocletian confers with Galerius, Augustus of the East, and Maximianus, the recently returned former Augustus of the West, in an attempt to end the civil wars of the Tetrarchy.

title: Alki Point, Seattle
fact: 1851 — The Denny Party lands at Alki Point, before moving to the other side of Elliott Bay to what would become Seattle.

title: Birmingham and Midland Institute
fact: 1855 — In Birmingham, England, Albert, Prince Consort lays the foundation stone of the Birmingham and Midland Institute.

title: Cutty Sark
fact: 1869 — In Dumbarton, Scotland, the clipper Cutty Sark is launched.

title: China Clipper
fact: 1935 — The China Clipper inaugurates the first commercial transpacific air service, connecting Alameda, California with Manila.

title: Danish West Indies
fact: 1733 — The start of the 1733 slave insurrection on St. John in what was then the Danish West Indies.

title: Dolce & Gabbana
fact: 2018 — Founders of Italian fashion brand Dolce & Gabbana issue an apology following a series of offensive advertisements on social media promoting a fashion show in Shanghai, China, which was canceled.

title: Hibiscus Rising
fact: 2023 — Hibiscus Rising, commemorating David Oluwale, is unveiled in Leeds.

title: Religious of the Virgin Mary
fact: 1755 — King Ferdinand VI of Spain grants royal protection to the Beaterio de la Compañia de Jesus, now known as the Congregation of the Religious of the Virgin Mary.
story_label: Wikipedia: Religious of the Virgin Mary

title: Berners Street hoax
fact: 1809 — The Berners Street hoax is perpetrated by Theodore Hook in the City of Westminster, London.

title: Hamilton Crescent
fact: 1872 — The first-ever international football match takes place at Hamilton Crescent, Glasgow, between Scotland and England.

title: Irish Free State
fact: 1922 — Ireland is partitioned, with Northern Ireland and the Irish Free State coming into existence, one year to the day after the signing of the Anglo-Irish Treaty.

title: Capture of Saddam Hussein
fact: 2003 — Iraq War: Operation Red Dawn: Former Iraqi President Saddam Hussein is captured near his home town of Tikrit.

title: Schuyler Mansion
fact: 1780 — Founding Father Alexander Hamilton marries Elizabeth Schuyler Hamilton at the Schuyler Mansion in Albany, New York.

title: Messina
fact: 1167 — Sicilian Chancellor Stephen du Perche moves the royal court to Messina to prevent a rebellion.

title: Lyttelton, New Zealand
fact: 1850 — The Charlotte Jane and the Randolph bring the first of the Canterbury Pilgrims to Lyttelton, New Zealand.

title: Aztec sun stone
fact: 1790 — The Aztec calendar stone is discovered at El Zócalo, Mexico City.

title: Sucha Beskidzka
fact: 2005 — A passenger train from Sucha Beskidzka to Żywiec in Poland loses its brakes while on a steep downhill part of the route. It is stopped in a controlled collision in Świnna by a train travelling in opposite direction. 2 drivers and 6 passengers are injured.

title: USS Pueblo (AGER-2)
fact: 1968 — The 82 sailors from the USS Pueblo are released after eleven months of internment in North Korea.

title: Siege of Edessa (1144)
fact: 1144 — The capital of the crusader County of Edessa falls to Imad ad-Din Zengi, the atabeg of Mosul and Aleppo.

title: Aire-sur-l'Adour
fact: 484 CE — Alaric II succeeds his father Euric and becomes king of the Visigoths. He establishes his capital at Aire-sur-l'Adour (Southern Gaul).

title: Gadsden Purchase
fact: 1853 — Gadsden Purchase: The United States buys land from Mexico to facilitate railroad building in the Southwest.

title: 1975 British Mount Everest Southwest Face expedition
fact: 1975 — Southwest Face expedition members become the first persons to reach the summit of Mount Everest by any of its faces, instead of using a ridge route.
story_label: Wikipedia: 1975 British Mount Everest Southwest Face expedition

title: Cardiff Metropolitan Cathedral
fact: 1941 — World War II: The Cardiff Blitz severely damages the cathedral in Cardiff, Wales.

title: Iran hostage crisis
fact: 1981 — Twenty minutes after Ronald Reagan is inaugurated as the 40th President of the United States of America, Iran releases 52 American hostages.

title: Great Ormond Street Hospital
fact: 1852 — Great Ormond St Hospital for Sick Children, the first hospital in England to provide in-patient beds specifically for children, is founded in London.

title: Melbourne Cricket Ground
fact: 1877 — First ever official cricket test match is played: Australia vs England at the MCG Stadium, in Melbourne, Australia.

title: Grand Hotel Bucharest
fact: 1971 — The Intercontinental Hotel in Bucharest opens, becoming the second-tallest building in the city.

title: Presidio San Agustín del Tucsón
fact: 1775 — The Spanish establish the Presidio San Augustin del Tucson in the town that became Tucson, Arizona.
story_label: Wikipedia: Presidio San Agustín del Tucsón

title: Belzec extermination camp
fact: 1942 — The Holocaust in Ukraine: On the Jewish holiday of Yom Kippur, Nazis send over 1,000 Jews of Pidhaitsi to Bełżec extermination camp.

title: Sobibor extermination camp
fact: 1943 — Nazi Holocaust in Poland: Sobibór extermination camp is closed.

title: 1343 Naples tsunami
fact: 1343 — A tsunami, caused by an earthquake in the Tyrrhenian Sea, devastates Naples and the Maritime Republic of Amalfi, among other places.

title: Worcester, England
fact: 1275 — Edward I permits his mother Eleanor of Provence to expel the Jews from the towns Worcester, Marlborough, Cambridge and Gloucester.

title: Bowery Amphitheatre
fact: 1843 — The first minstrel show in the United States, The Virginia Minstrels, opens (Bowery Amphitheatre in New York City).

title: Battle of the Aegates
fact: 241 BCE — First Punic War: Battle of the Aegates: The Romans sink the Carthaginian fleet bringing the First Punic War to an end.

title: Treaty of Le Goulet
fact: 1200 — King John of England and King Philip II of France sign the Treaty of Le Goulet.

title: Operation Opera
fact: 1981 — The Israeli Air Force destroys Iraq's Osiraq nuclear reactor during Operation Opera.

title: Daniel K. Inouye International Airport
fact: 1946 — Aloha Airlines begins service from Honolulu International Airport.
story_label: Wikipedia: Daniel K. Inouye International Airport

title: St. Nicholas Rink
fact: 1956 — After going bankrupt in 1955, the American broadcaster DuMont Television Network makes its final broadcast, a boxing match from St. Nicholas Arena in New York in the Boxing from St. Nicholas Arena series.

title: Archdiocese of Utrecht (Catholic)
fact: 1248 — The Dutch city of Ommen receives city rights and fortification rights from Otto III, the Archbishop of Utrecht.

title: Cathedral of the Holy Cross, Tyre
fact: 1167 — King Amalric of Jerusalem marries Byzantine princess Maria Komnene in the cathedral of Tyre.
story_label: Wikipedia: Cathedral of the Holy Cross, Tyre

title: Diocese of Nantes
fact: 1440 — Gilles de Rais, one of the earliest known serial killers, is taken into custody upon an accusation brought against him by Jean de Malestroit, Bishop of Nantes.

title: Columbia University Graduate School of Journalism
fact: 1912 — Columbia University Graduate School of Journalism is founded in New York City.
story_label: Wikipedia: Columbia University Graduate School of Journalism

title: Texas A&M University
fact: 1876 — The Agricultural and Mechanical College of Texas (now known as Texas A&M) opens as the first public college in Texas.

title: Mor Bar Sauma Monastery
fact: 1166 — Michael the Syrian, one of the most important Syriac historians, is consecrated as Syriac Orthodox Patriarch at the Mor Bar Sauma Monastery.

title: October 2009 Baghdad bombings
fact: 2009 — The October 2009 Baghdad bombings kill 155 and wound at least 721.

title: Battle of Dengbu Island
fact: 1949 — Chinese Civil War: The Battle of Dengbu Island occurs.

title: Beşiktaş Stadium
fact: 2016 — Two explosions outside a football stadium in Istanbul, Turkey, kill 38 people and injure 166 others.

title: 893 Dvin earthquake
fact: 893 CE — An earthquake destroys the city of Dvin, Armenia.

title: Hurricane Creek mine disaster
fact: 1970 — Hurricane Creek mine disaster, near Hyden, Kentucky

title: John Brown & Company
fact: 1906 — Cunard Line's RMS Lusitania is launched from the John Brown Shipyard, Glasgow (Clydebank), Scotland.

title: January 1998 North American ice storm
fact: 1998 — A massive ice storm hits eastern Canada and the northeastern United States, continuing through January 10 and causing widespread destruction.
story_label: Wikipedia: January 1998 North American ice storm

title: 1975 Algiers Agreement
fact: 1975 — Algiers Accord: Iran and Iraq announce a settlement of their border dispute.

title: St. Nicholas Church, Leipzig
fact: 1725 — J. S. Bach's later Easter Oratorio in its first version is performed at the Nikolaikirche in Leipzig on Easter Sunday.

title: Allan Hills 84001
fact: 1996 — NASA announces that the ALH 84001 meteorite, thought to originate from Mars, contains evidence of primitive life-forms.

title: Cape Bojador
fact: 1454 — The papal bull Romanus Pontifex awards the Kingdom of Portugal exclusive trade and colonization rights to all of Africa south of Cape Bojador.

title: Penydarren Ironworks
fact: 1804 — The first self-propelling steam locomotive makes its outing at the Pen-y-Darren Ironworks in Wales.

title: East Indies
fact: 1500 — The fleet of Pedro Álvares Cabral leaves Lisbon for the Indies. The fleet will discover Brazil which lies within boundaries granted to Portugal in the Treaty of Tordesillas in 1494.

title: Jefferson Street Grounds
fact: 1876 — The first National League baseball game is played at the Jefferson Street Grounds in Philadelphia.

title: Dorchester, Boston
fact: 1631 — In Dorchester, Massachusetts, John Winthrop takes the oath of office and becomes the first Governor of Massachusetts.

title: Nasdaq Helsinki
fact: 1912 — The Helsinki Stock Exchange sees its first transaction.

title: Berkeley Plantation
fact: 1619 — Thirty-eight colonists arrive at Berkeley Hundred, Virginia. The group's charter proclaims that the day "be yearly and perpetually kept holy as a day of thanksgiving to Almighty God."

title: 2025 Beninese coup attempt
fact: 2025 — An attempted coup takes place in Benin, but is thwarted, and order restored.

title: Our Lady of Guadalupe
fact: 1531 — The Virgin of Guadalupe first appears to Juan Diego at Tepeyac, Mexico City.

title: Lordship of Argos and Nauplia
fact: 1388 — Maria of Enghien sells the lordship of Argos and Nauplia to the Republic of Venice.
story_label: Wikipedia: Lordship of Argos and Nauplia

title: Hollywood, Los Angeles
fact: 1913 — Cecil B. DeMille starts filming Hollywood's first feature film, The Squaw Man.

title: 1980 Surinamese coup d'état
fact: 1980 — The government of Suriname is overthrown by a military coup led by Dési Bouterse.

title: Space Shuttle Challenger disaster
fact: 1986 — Challenger Disaster: Divers from the USS Preserver locate the crew cabin of Challenger on the ocean floor.

title: Mirza Fatali Akhundov
fact: 1873 — The first Azerbaijani play, The Adventures of the Vizier of the Khan of Lenkaran, prepared by Akhundov, is performed by Hassan-bey Zardabi and dramatist and Najaf-bey Vezirov.

title: 16th Street Baptist Church
fact: The 16th Street Baptist Church is a Baptist church in Birmingham, Alabama, United States. In 1963, the church was bombed by Ku Klux Klan members. The bombing killed four young girls in the midst of the Civil Rights Movement.

title: Abbey Road, London
fact: Abbey Road is a thoroughfare in the borough of Camden and the City of Westminster in Greater London running roughly northwest to southeast through St John's Wood near Lord's Cricket Ground. It is part of the road B507.

title: Alamo Mission
fact: The Alamo is a historic Spanish mission and fortress compound founded in the 18th century by Catholic missionaries in what is now San Antonio, Texas, United States.

title: Alcatraz Island
fact: Alcatraz Island is a small island about 1.25 miles offshore from San Francisco in San Francisco Bay, California, near the Golden Gate strait. The island was developed in the mid-19th century with facilities for a lighthouse, a military fortification, and a military prison.

title: Anne Frank House
fact: The Anne Frank House is a writer's house and biographical museum dedicated to Jewish wartime diarist Anne Frank. The building is located on the Prinsengracht, close to the Westerkerk, in central Amsterdam in the Netherlands.

title: Antietam National Battlefield
fact: Antietam National Battlefield is a National Park Service-protected area along Antietam Creek in Sharpsburg, Washington County, northwestern Maryland. It commemorates the American Civil War Battle of Antietam that occurred on September 17, 1862.

title: ANZAC Cove
fact: ANZAC Cove is a small cove on the Gallipoli peninsula in Turkey. It became famous as the site of World War I landing of the ANZACs (Australian and New Zealand Army Corps) on 25 April 1915.

title: Appomattox Court House National Historical Park
fact: The Appomattox Court House National Historical Park is the preserved 19th-century village named Appomattox Court House in Appomattox County, Virginia. The village was named for the presence nearby of what is now preserved as the Old Appomattox Court House.
story_label: Wikipedia: Appomattox Court House National Historical Park

title: Arlington National Cemetery
fact: Arlington National Cemetery is the largest cemetery in the United States National Cemetery System, one of two maintained by the United States Army. More than 400,000 people are buried in its 639 acres (259 ha) in Arlington County, Virginia.

title: Auschwitz concentration camp
fact: Auschwitz, also known as Oświęcim, was a complex of over 40 concentration and extermination camps operated by Nazi Germany in occupied Poland (in a portion annexed into Germany in 1939) during World War II and the Holocaust.

title: Babi Yar
fact: Babi Yar or Babyn Yar is a ravine in the Ukrainian capital Kyiv and a site of massacres carried out by Nazi Germany's forces during its campaign against the Soviet Union in World War II.

title: Battle of Blair Mountain
fact: The Battle of Blair Mountain was the largest labor uprising in United States history and is the largest armed uprising since the American Civil War.

title: Battle of Bosworth Field
fact: The Battle of Bosworth or Bosworth Field was the last significant battle of the Wars of the Roses, the civil war between the houses of Lancaster and York that extended across England and Wales in the latter half of the 15th century.

title: Battle of Chosin Reservoir
fact: The Battle of Chosin Reservoir, also known as the Chosin Reservoir Campaign or the Battle of Lake Changjin, was a battle in the Korean War. The name "Chosin" is derived from the Japanese pronunciation "Chōshin", instead of the Korean pronunciation.

title: Battle of Kasserine Pass
fact: The Battle of Kasserine Pass was a series of engagements which took place from 19–24 February 1943 around Kasserine Pass, a 2-mile-wide (3.2 km) gap in the Grand Dorsal chain of the Atlas Mountains in west central Tunisia. It was a part of the Tunisian campaign of World War II.

title: Battle of Rorke's Drift
fact: The Battle of Rorke's Drift, also known as the Defence of Rorke's Drift, was an engagement in the Anglo-Zulu War.

title: Battle of the Bulge Monument
fact: The Battle of the Bulge Monument, formerly known as the Mardasson Memorial, is a monument honoring the memory of American soldiers wounded or killed during World War II's Battle of the Bulge.
story_label: Wikipedia: Battle of the Bulge Monument

title: Bay of Pigs
fact: The Bay of Pigs is an inlet of the Gulf of Cazones, located on the southern coast of Cuba.

title: Bergen-Belsen concentration camp
fact: Bergen-Belsen, or Belsen, was a Nazi concentration camp in what is today Lower Saxony in northern Germany, southwest of the town of Bergen near Celle. Originally established as a prisoner of war camp, in 1943, parts of it became a concentration camp.

title: Berghof (residence)
fact: The Berghof was Adolf Hitler's holiday home in the Obersalzberg of the Bavarian Alps near Berchtesgaden, Bavaria, Germany.

title: Berlin Tempelhof Airport
fact: Berlin Tempelhof Airport (IATA: THF, ICAO: EDDI) was one of the first airports in Berlin, Germany. Situated in the south-central Berlin borough of Tempelhof-Schöneberg, the airport ceased operating in 2008 amid controversy.

title: Bethel Woods Center for the Arts
fact: The Bethel Woods Center for the Arts is an amphitheatre, performing arts center and museum located at the site of the 1969 Woodstock Music & Art Fair in Bethel, New York.
story_label: Wikipedia: Bethel Woods Center for the Arts

title: Blood River
fact: Blood River, also known as the Ncome River, is situated between Nquthu and Vryheid in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa.

title: Boston Massacre
fact: The Boston Massacre, known in Great Britain as the Incident on King Street, was a confrontation on March 5, 1770, in the prelude to the American Revolution in Boston, in what was then the colony of the Province of Massachusetts Bay.

title: Brandenburg Gate
fact: The Brandenburg Gate is an 18th-century neoclassical monument in Berlin, Germany. One of the best-known landmarks of the country, it was erected on the site of a former city gate that marked the start of the road from Berlin to Brandenburg an der Havel…

title: Brattahlíð
fact: Brattahlíð, often anglicised as Brattahlid, was Erik the Red's estate in the Eastern Settlement Viking colony he established in south-western Greenland toward the end of the 10th century. The present settlement of Qassiarsuk is now located on the former estate.

title: Bunker Hill Monument
fact: The Bunker Hill Monument is a war memorial on Breed's Hill in the Charlestown neighborhood of Boston, Massachusetts, United States. It commemorates the Battle of Bunker Hill, a major American Revolutionary War battle that took place there on June 17, 1775.

title: Canadian National Vimy Memorial
fact: The Canadian National Vimy Memorial is a war memorial site in France dedicated to the memory of Canadian Expeditionary Force members killed during the First World War.

title: Cape Coast Castle
fact: Cape Coast Castle is one of about forty "slave castles", or large commercial forts, built on the Gold Coast of West Africa (now Ghana) by European traders. Cape Coast Castle is located in the Central Region of Ghana.

title: Cape Trafalgar
fact: Cape Trafalgar is a headland in the Province of Cádiz in the southwest of Spain. Cape Trafalgar lies on the shore of the Atlantic Ocean, northwest of the Strait of Gibraltar.

title: CBGB
fact: CBGB was a New York City music club opened in 1973 by Hilly Kristal and his ex-wife Karen Kristal at 315 Bowery in the East Village in Manhattan, New York City. The club was previously a biker bar and before that it was a dive bar.

title: Cecilienhof
fact: Cecilienhof Palace is a palace in Potsdam, Brandenburg, Germany, built from 1914 to 1917 in the look and layout of an English Tudor manor house.

title: Checkpoint Charlie
fact: Checkpoint Charlie (or "Checkpoint C") was the Western Bloc's name for the best-known Berlin Wall crossing point between East Berlin and West Berlin during the Cold War (1947–1991), becoming a symbol of the Cold War, representing the separation of East and West.

title: Chicxulub crater
fact: The Chicxulub crater is an impact crater buried underneath the Yucatán Peninsula in Mexico. The crater is named after the onshore inland community of Chicxulub Pueblo.

title: Choeung Ek
fact: Choeung Ek is a site in Dangkao on the outskirts of Phnom Penh, capital of Cambodia, that was used as a Killing Field between 1977 and 1979 by the Khmer Rouge to perpetrate the Cambodian genocide.

title: Colonial National Historical Park
fact: Colonial National Historical Park is a large national historical park located in the Hampton Roads region of Virginia operated by the National Park Service.

title: Colonial Williamsburg
fact: Colonial Williamsburg is a living-history museum and private foundation presenting a part of the historic district in Williamsburg, Virginia.

title: Corregidor
fact: Corregidor is an island located at the entrance of Manila Bay in the southwestern part of Luzon in the Philippines, and is considered part of Cavite City in the province of Cavite despite being closer to Maragondon and Bataan.

title: Cowpens National Battlefield
fact: Cowpens National Battlefield is a unit of the National Park Service just east of Chesnee, South Carolina, and near the state line with North Carolina. It preserves a major battlefield of the American Revolutionary War.

title: Củ Chi tunnels
fact: The tunnels of Củ Chi are an immense network of connecting tunnels located in the Củ Chi District of Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon), Vietnam, and are part of a much larger network of tunnels that underlie much of the country.

title: Dachau concentration camp
fact: Dachau was one of the first concentration camps built by Nazi Germany and the longest-running one, opening on 22 March 1933. The camp was initially intended to intern the Nazi Party's political opponents, which consisted of communists, social democrats, and other dissidents.

title: Dealey Plaza
fact: Dealey Plaza, named after George Dealey, is a city park in the West End Historic District of downtown Dallas, Texas. It is sometimes called the "birthplace of Dallas", and was the location of the assassination of John F. Kennedy in 1963.

title: Devil's Island
fact: The penal colony of Cayenne, commonly known as Devil's Island, was a French penal colony that operated for 100 years, from 1852 to 1952, and officially closed in 1953, in the Salvation Islands of French Guiana.

title: Douaumont Ossuary
fact: The Douaumont Ossuary is a memorial containing the skeletal remains of soldiers who died on the battlefield during the Battle of Verdun in World War I. It is located in Douaumont-Vaux, France, within the Verdun battlefield…

title: Edmund Pettus Bridge
fact: The Edmund Pettus Bridge carries U.S. Route 80 Business (US 80 Bus.) across the Alabama River in Selma, Alabama, United States.

title: Ellis Island
fact: Ellis Island is an island in New York Harbor, within the U.S. states of New Jersey and New York. Owned by the U.S. government, Ellis Island was once the busiest immigrant inspection and processing station in the United States.

title: Elmina Castle
fact: Elmina Castle, or Fort St. George, was erected by the Portuguese in 1482 as Castelo de São Jorge da Mina ('St. George of the Mine Castle'), also known as Castelo da Mina or simply Mina (or Feitoria da Mina), in present-day Elmina, Ghana, formerly the Gold Coast.

title: Federal Hall
fact: Federal Hall was the first capitol building of the United States established under the Constitution.

title: Ford's Theatre
fact: Ford's Theatre is a theater in Washington, D.C., which opened in 1863. In 1865, it was the site of the assassination of Abraham Lincoln by John Wilkes Booth. The theater was later used as a warehouse and government office building.

title: Fort Clatsop
fact: Fort Clatsop was the encampment of the Lewis and Clark Expedition in the Oregon Country near the mouth of the Columbia River during the winter of 1805–1806.

title: Fort Duquesne
fact: Fort Duquesne was a fort established by the French in 1754, at the confluence of the Allegheny and Monongahela rivers. It was later taken over by the British, and later the Americans, and developed as Pittsburgh in Pennsylvania.

title: Fort Laramie National Historic Site
fact: Fort Laramie was a significant 19th-century trading post, diplomatic site, and military installation located at the confluence of the Laramie and the North Platte Rivers. They joined in the upper Platte River Valley in the eastern part of the present-day US state of Wyoming.
story_label: Wikipedia: Fort Laramie National Historic Site

title: Fort McHenry
fact: Fort McHenry is a historical American coastal pentagonal bastion fort on Locust Point, now a neighborhood of Baltimore, Maryland.

title: Fort Michilimackinac
fact: Fort Michilimackinac was an 18th-century French, and later British, fort and trading post at the Straits of Mackinac; it was built on the northern tip of the lower peninsula of the present-day state of Michigan in the United States.

title: Fort Necessity National Battlefield
fact: Fort Necessity National Battlefield is a National Battlefield in Fayette County, Pennsylvania, United States, which preserves the site of the Battle of Fort Necessity.

title: Fort Niagara
fact: Fort Niagara, also known as Old Fort Niagara, is a fortification originally built by New France to protect its interests in North America, specifically control of access between the Niagara River and Lake Ontario, the easternmost of the Great Lakes.

title: Fort Ross, California
fact: Fort Ross is a former Russian establishment on the west coast of North America in what is now Sonoma County, California, United States. It was the first multi-ethnic community north of the Spanish missions in what is now the U.S. state of California.

title: Fort Snelling
fact: Fort Snelling is a former military fortification and National Historic Landmark in the U.S. state of Minnesota on the bluffs overlooking the confluence of the Minnesota and Mississippi Rivers.

title: Fort Sumter
fact: Fort Sumter is an incomplete sea fort at the mouth of Charleston Harbor, South Carolina, where the battle that sparked the American Civil War took place.

title: Fort Ticonderoga
fact: Fort Ticonderoga, formerly Fort Carillon, is a large 18th-century star fort built by the French at a narrows near the south end of Lake Champlain in northern New York.

title: Fort Vancouver
fact: Fort Vancouver was an early 19th-century British fur trading post in the disputed region of Oregon Country in the Pacific Northwest. The factory was the principal settlement of the Hudson's Bay Company (HBC) in what was known as the Columbia Department.

title: Fort William Henry
fact: Fort William Henry was a British fort at the southern end of Lake George, in the province of New York.

title: Fraunces Tavern
fact: Fraunces Tavern is a museum, bar and restaurant in New York City, situated at 54 Pearl Street at the corner of Pearl and Broad Streets in the Financial District of Lower Manhattan.

title: Führerbunker
fact: The Führerbunker was an air raid shelter located near the Reich Chancellery in Berlin, Germany. It was part of a subterranean bunker complex constructed in two phases in 1936 and 1944. It was the last of the Führer Headquarters used by Adolf Hitler during World War II.

title: Fulda Gap
fact: The Fulda Gap, an area between the Hesse-Thuringian border, the former Inner German border, and Frankfurt am Main, contains two corridors of lowlands through which tanks might have driven in a surprise attack by the Soviets and their Warsaw Pact allies to gain crossings of the…

title: Gdańsk Shipyard
fact: The Gdańsk Shipyard is a large Polish shipyard, located in the city of Gdańsk, northern Poland. The yard gained international fame when Polish trade union Solidarity (Solidarność) was founded there in September 1980.

title: Gedenkstätte Berliner Mauer
fact: The Gedenkstätte Berliner Mauer (Berlin Wall Memorial) commemorates the division of Berlin by the Berlin Wall and the deaths that occurred there. The monument was created in 1998 by the Federal Republic of Germany and the Federal State of Berlin.

title: Gettysburg Battlefield
fact: The Gettysburg Battlefield is the area of the July 1–3, 1863, military engagements of the Battle of Gettysburg in and around Gettysburg, Pennsylvania.

title: Glienicke Bridge
fact: The Glienicke Bridge is a bridge across the Havel River in Germany, connecting the Wannsee district of Berlin with the Brandenburg capital, Potsdam. It is named after nearby Glienicke Palace.

title: Golden Spike National Historical Park
fact: Golden Spike National Historical Park is a United States National Historical Park located at Promontory Summit, north of the Great Salt Lake in east-central Box Elder County, Utah, United States.
story_label: Wikipedia: Golden Spike National Historical Park

title: Gorée
fact: Île de Gorée is one of the 19 communes d'arrondissement (i.e. districts) of the city of Dakar, Senegal.

title: Graceland
fact: Graceland is a mansion on a 13.8-acre (5.6-hectare) estate in Memphis, Tennessee, United States, which American singer Elvis Presley once owned. He is buried there, as are his parents Vernon and Gladys, paternal grandmother Minnie Mae, grandson Benjamin, and daughter Lisa Marie.

title: Guilford Courthouse National Military Park
fact: Guilford Courthouse National Military Park, at 2332 New Garden Road in Greensboro, Guilford County, North Carolina, commemorates the Battle of Guilford Court House, fought on March 15, 1781. This battle opened the campaign that led to American victory in the Revolutionary War.
story_label: Wikipedia: Guilford Courthouse National Military Park

title: Gunfight at the O.K. Corral
fact: The gunfight at the O.K. Corral pitted lawmen against members of a loosely organized group of cattle rustlers and horse thieves called the Cochise County Cowboys on October 26, 1881. While lasting less than a minute, the gunfight has been the subject of many books and films.
story_label: Wikipedia: Gunfight at the O.K. Corral

title: Harpers Ferry National Historical Park
fact: Harpers Ferry National Historical Park, originally Harpers Ferry National Monument, is located at the confluence of the Potomac and Shenandoah rivers in and around Harpers Ferry, West Virginia.
story_label: Wikipedia: Harpers Ferry National Historical Park

title: Harriet Tubman Underground Railroad National Historical Park
fact: Harriet Tubman Underground Railroad National Historical Park is a 480-acre (190 ha) National Park Service unit in the U.S. state of Maryland.
story_label: Wikipedia: Harriet Tubman Underground Railroad National Historical Park

title: Hellfire Pass
fact: Hellfire Pass, known locally as Chong Khao Kard and in Japanese as Konyu Cutting, is the name of a railway cutting on the former Burma Railway ("Death Railway") in Thailand, which was built with forced labour during World War II.

title: Helmstedt–Marienborn border crossing
fact: The Helmstedt–Marienborn border crossing, named Grenzübergangsstelle Marienborn (GÜSt) (border crossing Marienborn) by the German Democratic Republic (GDR), was the largest and most important border crossing on the Inner German border during the division of Germany.

title: Hiroshima Peace Memorial
fact: The Hiroshima Peace Memorial, originally the Hiroshima Prefectural Industrial Promotion Hall, and now commonly called the Genbaku Dome, Atomic Bomb Dome or A-Bomb Dome, is part of Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park in Hiroshima, Japan…

title: Historic Jamestown
fact: Historic Jamestowne is the cultural heritage site that was the location of the 1607 James Fort and the later 17th-century town of Jamestown in America.

title: Hitsville U.S.A.
fact: "Hitsville U.S.A." is the nickname given to Motown's first headquarters and recording studio. The house is located at 2648 West Grand Boulevard in Detroit near the New Center area of the city. Motown founder Berry Gordy bought the house in 1959.

title: Hỏa Lò Prison
fact: Hỏa Lò Prison was a prison in Hanoi originally used by the French colonists in Indochina for political prisoners, and later by North Vietnam for U.S. prisoners of war during the Vietnam War. During this later period, it was known to American POWs as the "Hanoi Hilton".

title: Hof, Bavaria
fact: Hof is a town on the banks of the Saale river in the northeastern corner of the Upper Franconia region of the German state of Bavaria. The town lies close to the Czech border and is in the forested Fichtel Mountains and Franconian Forest upland regions.

title: Independence Hall
fact: Independence Hall is a historic civic building in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, where both the Declaration of Independence and the Constitution of the United States were debated and adopted by the Founding Fathers of the United States.

title: Iona
fact: Iona is an island in the Inner Hebrides, off the Ross of Mull on the western coast of Scotland. It is mainly known for Iona Abbey, though there are other buildings on the island.

title: Isandlwana
fact: Isandlwana (older spelling Isandhlwana, also sometimes seen as Isandula) is an isolated hill in the KwaZulu-Natal province of South Africa. It is located 169 kilometres (105 mi) north by northwest of Durban.

title: Iwo Jima
fact: Iwo Jima is one of the Japanese Volcano Islands, which lie south of the Bonin Islands and together with them make up the Ogasawara Archipelago. Together with the Izu Islands, they make up Japan's Nanpō Islands.

title: Jelling stones
fact: The Jelling stones are massive carved runestones from the 10th century, found at the town of Jelling in Denmark. The older of the two Jelling stones was raised by King Gorm the Old in memory of his wife Thyra.

title: John Frost Bridge
fact: John Frost Bridge is the road bridge over the Lower Rhine at Arnhem, in the Netherlands. The bridge was inaugurated after the end of World War II, and is named after Major-General John Dutton Frost (1912–1993)…

title: Joint Security Area
fact: The Joint Security Area (JSA, often referred to as the Truce Village or Panmunjom) is the only portion of the Korean Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) where North and South Korean forces stand face-to-face.

title: Katyn massacre
fact: The Katyn massacre was a series of mass executions of Poles carried out by the Soviet Union between April and May 1940.

title: Kent State shootings
fact: The Kent State shootings were the killing of four and wounding of nine unarmed college students by the Ohio National Guard on the Kent State University campus in Kent, Ohio, United States.

title: Khe Sanh Combat Base
fact: Khe Sanh Combat Base was a United States Marine Corps outpost south of the Vietnamese Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) in Quang Tri province used during the Vietnam War.

title: Kigali Genocide Memorial
fact: The Kigali Genocide Memorial commemorates the 1994 Rwandan genocide. The remains of over 250,000 people are interred there. There is a visitor centre for students and others wishing to understand the events leading up to the Rwanda genocide against Tutsi in 1994.

title: Kings Mountain National Military Park
fact: Kings Mountain National Military Park is a National Military Park near Blacksburg, South Carolina, along the North Carolina/South Carolina border.
story_label: Wikipedia: Kings Mountain National Military Park

title: Kohima War Cemetery
fact: Kohima War Cemetery is a memorial dedicated to soldiers of the 2nd British Division of the Allied Forces who died in the Second World War at Kohima, the capital of the Indian state of Nagaland in April 1944.

title: Kremlin Wall Necropolis
fact: The Kremlin Wall Necropolis is the former national cemetery of the Soviet Union, located in Red Square in Moscow beside the Kremlin Wall. Burials there began in November 1917, when 240 pro-Bolsheviks who died during the Moscow Bolshevik Uprising were buried in mass graves.

title: L'Anse aux Meadows
fact: L'Anse aux Meadows is an archaeological site, first excavated in the 1960s, of a Norse settlement dating to approximately 1,000 years ago.

title: La Isabela
fact: La Isabela in Puerto Plata Province, Dominican Republic was the first stable Spanish settlement and town in the Americas. It was established in late December 1493 to early January 1494. The site is 42 km west of the city of Puerto Plata, adjacent to the village of El Castillo.

title: Landsberg Prison
fact: Landsberg Prison is a prison in the town of Landsberg am Lech in the southwest of the German state of Bavaria, about 65 kilometres (40 mi) west-southwest of Munich and 35 kilometres (22 mi) south of Augsburg.

title: Latin Bridge
fact: Latin Bridge is an Ottoman-era bridge over the river Miljacka in Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina.

title: Lewis and Clark National Historic Trail
fact: The Lewis and Clark National Historic Trail is a route across the United States commemorating the Lewis and Clark Expedition of 1804 to 1806. It is part of the National Trails System of the United States.
story_label: Wikipedia: Lewis and Clark National Historic Trail

title: Lincoln Memorial
fact: The Lincoln Memorial is a U.S. national memorial honoring Abraham Lincoln, the 16th president of the United States, located on the western end of the National Mall of Washington, D.C. The memorial is built in a neoclassical style in the form of a classical temple.

title: Lindisfarne
fact: Lindisfarne, also known as Holy Island, is a tidal island off the northeast coast of England, which constitutes the civil parish of Holy Island in Northumberland.

title: Little Bighorn Battlefield National Monument
fact: Little Bighorn Battlefield National Monument preserves the site of the June 25 and 26, 1876, Battle of the Little Bighorn, near Crow Agency, Montana, in the United States.
story_label: Wikipedia: Little Bighorn Battlefield National Monument

title: Livadia Palace
fact: Livadia Palace is a former summer retreat of the last Russian tsar, Nicholas II, and his family in Livadiya, Crimea.

title: Ludendorff Bridge
fact: The Ludendorff Bridge, also known as the Bridge at Remagen, was the bridge across the river Rhine in Germany which was captured by United States Army forces in early March 1945 during the Battle of Remagen, in the closing weeks of World War II…

title: Ludlow Massacre
fact: The Ludlow Massacre was a mass killing perpetrated by anti-striker militia during the Colorado Coalfield War.

title: Malbork Castle
fact: The Castle of the Teutonic Order in Malbork, commonly known as Malbork Castle, is a Brick Gothic castle complex located in the town of Malbork, Poland, built in the 13th and significantly expanded in the 14th century.

title: Mamayev Kurgan
fact: Mamayev Kurgan is a hill and memorial complex overlooking the city of Volgograd in Southern Russia. The name in Russian means "tumulus of Mamai". The formation is dominated by a memorial complex commemorating the Battle of Stalingrad (July 1942 to February 1943).

title: Manassas National Battlefield Park
fact: Manassas National Battlefield Park is a unit of the National Park Service located in Prince William County, Virginia, United States, north of Manassas.

title: Marienborn
fact: Marienborn is a village and a former municipality in the Börde district in Saxony-Anhalt, Germany. Since 1 January 2010, it has been part of the municipality of Sommersdorf. It is about 27 km (17 mi) southwest of Haldensleben.

title: Menin Gate
fact: The Menin Gate, officially the Menin Gate Memorial to the Missing, is a war memorial in Ypres, Belgium, dedicated to the British and Commonwealth soldiers who were killed in the Ypres Salient of World War I and whose graves are unknown.

title: Midway Atoll
fact: Midway Atoll is a 2.4 sq mi (6.2 km2) atoll in the North Pacific Ocean. Midway Atoll is an insular area of the United States, and is an unorganized and unincorporated territory of the U.S. Midway Atoll consists of three islands.

title: Monmouth Battlefield State Park
fact: Monmouth Battlefield State Park is a 1,818-acre (7.36 km2) New Jersey state park located on the border of Manalapan and Freehold Township, in Monmouth County, New Jersey, United States.

title: Monte Cassino
fact: The Abbey of Monte Cassino (today usually spelled Montecassino) is a Benedictine monastery on a rocky hill about 130 kilometres (80 mi) southeast of Rome, in the Latin Valley.

title: Monticello
fact: Monticello ( MON-tih-CHEL-oh) was the primary residence and plantation of Thomas Jefferson, a Founding Father, author of the Declaration of Independence, and the third president of the United States.

title: Monument to the Ghetto Heroes
fact: The Monument to the Ghetto Heroes is a monument in Warsaw, Poland, commemorating the Warsaw Ghetto Uprising of 1943 during the Second World War.
story_label: Wikipedia: Monument to the Ghetto Heroes

title: Moores Creek National Battlefield
fact: Moores Creek National Battlefield is a battlefield managed by the U.S. National Park Service. The park commemorates the 1776 victory of a thousand patriots over about eight hundred loyalists at Moore's Creek.

title: Mount Vernon
fact: Mount Vernon is the former residence and plantation of George Washington, a Founding Father, commander of the Continental Army in the Revolutionary War, and the first president of the United States, and his wife, Martha.

title: Mount Washington Hotel
fact: The Omni Mount Washington Resort is a historic luxury resort hotel in Bretton Woods, New Hampshire, United States, near Mount Washington. It was designed by Charles Alling Gifford.

title: Nagasaki Peace Park
fact: Nagasaki Peace Park is a park located in Nagasaki, Japan, commemorating the atomic bombing of the city on August 9, 1945 during World War II. It is next to the Atomic Bomb Museum and near the Peace Memorial Hall.

title: National Civil Rights Museum
fact: The National Civil Rights Museum is a complex of museums and historic buildings in Memphis, Tennessee; its exhibits trace the history of the civil rights movement in the United States from the 17th century to the present.

title: National September 11 Memorial & Museum
fact: The National September 11 Memorial & Museum is a memorial and museum that are part of the World Trade Center complex, in New York City, created for remembering the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks which killed 2,977 people, as well as the February 26, 1993…

title: Old North Church
fact: Old North Church (officially Christ Church in the City of Boston) is an Episcopal church on Salem Street in the North End neighborhood of Boston, Massachusetts, United States. The church, built in 1723, is the oldest standing church in the city.

title: Omaha Beach
fact: Omaha Beach was one of five Allied beach landing sectors of the amphibious assault component of Operation Overlord during the Second World War. On June 6, 1944, the Allies invaded German-occupied France with the Normandy landings.

title: Oskar Schindler's Enamel Factory
fact: Oskar Schindler's Enamel Factory is a former metal item factory in Kraków. It now hosts two museums: the Museum of Contemporary Art in Kraków, on the former workshops, and a branch of the Historical Museum of the City of Kraków, situated at ul.

title: Palace of Justice, Nuremberg
fact: The Nuremberg Palace of Justice is a building complex in Nuremberg, Bavaria, Germany. It was constructed from 1909 to 1916 and houses the appellate court (Oberlandesgericht), the regional court (Landgericht)…

title: Palace of the Republic, Berlin
fact: The Palace of the Republic was a building in Berlin that hosted the Volkskammer, the parliament of East Germany, from 1976 to 1990.
story_label: Wikipedia: Palace of the Republic, Berlin

title: Palace of Versailles
fact: The Palace of Versailles is a château and historic monument in Versailles in the Yvelines department of France, southwest of Paris. It served as the principal residence of the French kings Louis XIV, Louis XV, and Louis XVI.

title: Pearl Harbor National Memorial
fact: Pearl Harbor National Memorial is a unit of the National Park System of the United States on the island of Oahu, Hawaii.

title: Pegasus Bridge
fact: Pegasus Bridge, originally called the Bénouville Bridge after the neighbouring village, is a road crossing over the Caen Canal, between Caen and Ouistreham in Normandy.

title: Peleliu
fact: Peleliu (or Beliliou) is an island in the island nation of Palau. Peleliu, along with two small islands to its northeast, forms one of the sixteen states of Palau.

title: Peter and Paul Fortress
fact: The Peter and Paul Fortress is the original citadel of Saint Petersburg, Russia, founded by Peter the Great in 1703 and built to Domenico Trezzini's designs from 1706 to 1740 as a star fortress.

title: Place de la Bastille
fact: The Place de la Bastille is a square in Paris where the Bastille Prison once stood, until the storming of the Bastille and its subsequent physical destruction between 14 July 1789 and 14 July 1790 during the French Revolution. No vestige of the prison remains.

title: Plains of Abraham
fact: The Plains of Abraham is a historic area within the Battlefields Park in Quebec City, Quebec, Canada. It was established on 17 March 1908.

title: Plymouth Rock
fact: Plymouth Rock is a boulder in Plymouth, Massachusetts, United States, which was claimed to have been at the site where the Mayflower Pilgrims landed to found Plymouth Colony in December 1620.

title: Pointe du Hoc
fact: La Pointe du Hoc is a promontory with a 35-metre (110 ft) cliff overlooking the English Channel on the northwestern coast of Normandy in the Calvados department, France. In World War II, Pointe du Hoc was the location of a series of German bunkers and machine gun posts.

title: Pompeys Pillar National Monument
fact: Pompeys Pillar National Monument is a rock formation located in south central Montana, United States.

title: Port Arthur, Tasmania
fact: Port Arthur is a town and former convict settlement on the Tasman Peninsula, in Tasmania, Australia. It is located approximately 97 kilometres (60 mi) southeast of the state capital, Hobart.

title: Potsdamer Platz
fact: Potsdamer Platz is a public square and traffic intersection in the centre of Berlin, Germany, lying about 1 km (1,100 yd) south of the Brandenburg Gate and the Reichstag, and close to the southeast corner of the Tiergarten park.

title: Princeton Battlefield
fact: The Princeton Battlefield in Princeton, Mercer County, New Jersey, United States, is where American and British troops fought each other on January 3, 1777, in the Battle of Princeton during the American Revolutionary War.

title: Pullman National Historical Park
fact: Pullman National Historical Park is a historic district located in Chicago, Illinois, which in the 19th century was the first model, planned industrial community in the United States.

title: Roanoke Colony
fact: The Roanoke Colony was the site of two attempts by Sir Walter Raleigh to found the first permanent English settlement in North America. The first colony was established at Roanoke Island in 1585 as a military outpost, and was evacuated in 1586.

title: Robben Island
fact: Robben Island is an island in Table Bay, 6.9 kilometres (4.3 mi) west of the coast of Bloubergstrand, north of Cape Town, South Africa.

title: Runnymede
fact: Runnymede is a water-meadow alongside the River Thames in the English county of Surrey, bordering Berkshire and just over 20 miles (32 km) west of central London.

title: Salem Witch Museum
fact: The Salem Witch Museum is a history museum located at 19 1/2 Washington Square North in downtown Salem, Massachusetts across from Salem Common.

title: Salem witch trials
fact: The Salem witch trials were a series of hearings and prosecutions of people accused of witchcraft in colonial Massachusetts between February 1692 and May 1693. More than 200 people were accused.

title: Sand Creek massacre
fact: The Sand Creek massacre was a massacre of Cheyenne and Arapaho people by the U.S. Army in the American Indian Wars that occurred on November 29, 1864…

title: Sarajevo Olympic Bobsleigh and Luge Track
fact: Sarajevo Olympic Bobsleigh and Luge Track is a derelict bobsleigh and luge track situated on Trebević mountain overlooking the City of Sarajevo, built for the 1984 Winter Olympics.
story_label: Wikipedia: Sarajevo Olympic Bobsleigh and Luge Track

title: Sarajevo Tunnel
fact: The Sarajevo Tunnel (Bosnian: Sarajevski Tunel) also known as the Tunnel of Salvation (Bosnian: Tunel spasa), the Tunnel of Hope, or the Tunnel of Life, was a tunnel constructed between March and June 1993 during the Siege of Sarajevo in the midst of the Bosnian War.

title: Saratoga National Historical Park
fact: Saratoga National Historical Park is a United States National Historical Park located in the Town of Stillwater in eastern New York, 30 miles (48 km) north of Albany. The park preserves the site of the Battles of Saratoga.

title: Scapa Flow
fact: Scapa Flow is a body of water in the Orkney Islands, Scotland, sheltered by the islands of Mainland, Graemsay, Burray, South Ronaldsay and Hoy. Its sheltered waters have played an important role in travel, trade and conflict throughout the centuries.

title: Spandau Prison
fact: Spandau Prison was a military prison located in the Spandau borough of West Berlin (present-day Berlin, Germany). Built in 1876, it became a proto-concentration camp under Nazi Germany. After the Second World War, it held seven top Nazi leaders convicted in the Nuremberg trials.

title: Srebrenica Genocide Memorial
fact: The Srebrenica Genocide Memorial, officially known as the Srebrenica–Potočari Memorial and Cemetery for the Victims of the 1995 Genocide, is the memorial-cemetery complex in Srebrenica set up to honour the victims of the 1995 Srebrenica massacre.

title: Stari Most
fact: The Old Bridge, also known as the Mostar Bridge, is a rebuilt 16th-century Ottoman bridge in the city of Mostar in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

title: Stasimuseum
fact: The Stasimuseum is a research and memorial centre concerning the political system of the former East Germany. It is located in the Lichtenberg locality of Berlin, in the former headquarters of the Stasi, on Ruschestraße, near Frankfurter Allee and U-Bahn station Magdalenenstraße.

title: Stonewall Inn
fact: The Stonewall Inn is a gay bar and recreational tavern at 53 Christopher Street in the Greenwich Village neighborhood of Lower Manhattan in New York City.

title: Strawberry Field
fact: Strawberry Field is a visitor attraction and training centre in the Liverpool suburb of Woolton that is owned and operated by the Salvation Army. It operated as a children's home between 1936 and 2005.

title: Sun Studio
