fact: Sun Studio is a recording studio opened by rock-and-roll pioneer Sam Phillips at 706 Union Avenue in Memphis, Tennessee, on January 3, 1950. It was originally called Memphis Recording Service, sharing the same building with the Sun Records label business.

title: Sutter's Mill
fact: Sutter's Mill was a water-powered sawmill on the bank of the South Fork American River in the foothills of the Sierra Nevada in California. It was named after its owner John Sutter. A worker constructing the mill, James W. Marshall, found gold there in 1848.

title: Sutton Hoo
fact: Sutton Hoo is the site of two Anglo-Saxon cemeteries dating from the 6th to 7th centuries near Woodbridge, Suffolk, England. Archaeologists have excavated the site since the discovery of a previously undisturbed ship burial containing a wealth of artifacts in 1938.

title: Templo Mayor
fact: The Templo Mayor was the main temple of the Mexica people in their capital city of Tenōchtitlan, which is now Mexico City. Its architectural style belongs to the late Postclassic period of Mesoamerica.

title: The Cavern Club
fact: The Cavern Club is a music venue on Mathew Street, Liverpool, England. The Cavern Club opened on 16 January 1957 as a jazz club, later becoming a centre of the rock and roll scene in Liverpool in the late 1950s and early 1960s.

title: The Dakota
fact: The Dakota, also known as the Dakota Apartments, is a cooperative apartment building at 1 West 72nd Street on the Upper West Side of Manhattan in New York City, New York, US.

title: The Pentagon
fact: The Pentagon is the headquarters of the United States Department of Defense, in Arlington County, Virginia, across the Potomac River from Washington, D.C. The building was constructed on an accelerated schedule during World War II.

title: Thermopylae
fact: Thermopylae is a narrow pass and modern town in Lamia, Phthiotis, Greece. It derives its name from its hot sulphur springs. In Greek mythology the Hot Gates is one of the entrances to Hades.

title: Thiepval Memorial
fact: The Thiepval Memorial to the Missing of the Somme is a war memorial to 72,337 missing British and South African servicemen who died in the Battles of the Somme of the First World War between 1915 and 1918, with no known grave.

title: Þingvellir
fact: Þingvellir was the site of the Alþing, the annual parliament of Iceland from the year 930 until the last session held at Þingvellir in 1798.

title: Tiananmen Square
fact: Tiananmen Square or Tian'anmen Square is a city square in the city centre of Beijing, China, named after the Tiananmen ("Gate of Heavenly Peace") located to its north, which separates it from the Forbidden City imperial palace complex.

title: Tora Bora
fact: Tora Bora is a cave complex, part of the Spin Ghar (White Mountains) mountain range of eastern Afghanistan.

title: Tower of London
fact: The Tower of London, officially His Majesty's Royal Palace and Fortress of the Tower of London, is a historic citadel and castle on the north bank of the River Thames in London, England.

title: Treblinka extermination camp
fact: Treblinka was the second-deadliest extermination camp to be built and operated by Nazi Germany in occupied Poland during World War II, second only to Auschwitz.

title: Trenton Battle Monument
fact: The Trenton Battle Monument is a massive column-type structure in the Battle Monument section of Trenton, Mercer County, New Jersey, United States.

title: Triangle Shirtwaist Factory fire
fact: The Triangle Shirtwaist Factory fire occurred in the Greenwich Village neighborhood of Manhattan, a borough of New York City, on Saturday, March 25, 1911. The fire was the deadliest industrial disaster in the history of the city, and one of the deadliest in U.S. history.

title: Tunguska event
fact: The Tunguska event was the explosion of between 3 and 50 megatons TNT equivalent in the Russian Empire's Yeniseysk Governorate, near the Podkamennaya Tunguska River in modern Krasnoyarsk Krai, on the morning of 30 June 1908.

title: USS Arizona Memorial
fact: The USS Arizona Memorial, at Pearl Harbor in Honolulu, Hawaii, marks the resting place of 1,102 of the 1,177 sailors and Marines killed on USS Arizona during the attack on Pearl Harbor on December 7, 1941, and commemorates the events of that day.

title: Valley Forge
fact: Valley Forge was the winter encampment of the Continental Army, under the command of George Washington, during the Philadelphia campaign of the American Revolutionary War.

title: Vicksburg National Military Park
fact: Vicksburg National Military Park preserves the site of the Siege of Vicksburg, waged from March 29 to July 4, 1863 during the American Civil War.

title: Vilcabamba, Peru
fact: Vilcabamba (in Hispanicized spelling) or Willkapampa, often called the Lost City of the Incas, is a lost city in the Echarate District of La Convención Province in the Cuzco Region of Peru. Vilcabamba, in Quechua, means "sacred plain".

title: Vukovar water tower
fact: The Vukovar water tower is a structure in Vukovar, Croatia. Built in 1968 in the Socialist Republic of Croatia in Yugoslavia, it became a symbol of the Croatian War of Independence.

title: Wannsee Conference
fact: The Wannsee Conference was a meeting of senior government officials of Nazi Germany and Schutzstaffel (SS) leaders, held in the Berlin suburb of Wannsee on 20 January 1942.

title: Warsaw Uprising Monument
fact: Warsaw Uprising Monument is a monument in Warsaw, Poland, dedicated to the Warsaw Uprising of 1944. Unveiled in 1989, it was designed by Jacek Budyn and sculpted by Wincenty Kućma. It is located on the southern side of Krasiński Square.

title: Wawel Castle
fact: The Wawel Royal Castle and the Wawel Hill on which it sits constitute the most historically and culturally significant site in Poland.

title: Westerplatte
fact: Westerplatte is a peninsula in Gdańsk, Poland, located on the Baltic Sea coast mouth of the Dead Vistula (one of the Vistula delta estuaries), in the Gdańsk harbour channel.

title: Whitney Plantation Historic District
fact: The Whitney Plantation Historic District is preserved by the Whitney Institute, a non-profit whose mission is to educate the public about the history and legacies of slavery in the Southern United States.

title: Winter Palace
fact: The Winter Palace is a palace in Saint Petersburg that served as the official residence of the House of Romanov, the emperors of Russia, from 1732 to 1917. The palace and its precincts now house the Hermitage Museum. The floor area is 233,345 square metres.

title: Wolf's Lair
fact: The Wolf's Lair was Adolf Hitler's first Eastern Front military headquarters in World War II. Currently, it is a museum open to the public, as well as a hotel, conference room and restaurant.

title: Women's Rights National Historical Park
fact: The Women's Rights National Historical Park is a United States National Historical Park in Seneca Falls and Waterloo, New York, United States. Founded by an act of Congress in 1980, the park was first opened in 1982.
story_label: Wikipedia: Women's Rights National Historical Park

title: Wounded Knee Massacre
fact: The Wounded Knee Massacre, also known as the Battle of Wounded Knee, was an 1890 armed conflict between Native Americans and the United States Army. It was part of the U.S. Army’s Pine Ridge Campaign.

title: Wright Brothers National Memorial
fact: Wright Brothers National Memorial (originally the Kill Devil Hill Monument), located in Kill Devil Hills, North Carolina, commemorates Wright Flyer; the first successful, sustained, powered flights in a heavier-than-air machine.

title: Yad Vashem
fact: Yad Vashem is Israel's official memorial institution to the victims of the Holocaust, known in Hebrew as the Shoah (שואה).

title: Jesuits
fact: 1622 — Ignatius of Loyola and Francis Xavier, founders of the Society of Jesus, are canonized by the Roman Catholic Church.

title: Floyd Bennett Field
fact: 1938 — Douglas Corrigan takes off from Brooklyn to fly the "wrong way" to Ireland and becomes known as "Wrong Way" Corrigan.

title: 1420 Caldera earthquake
fact: 1420 — The 8.8–9.4 Caldera earthquake shakes Chile's Atacama Region causing tsunami in Chile, Hawaii, and Japan.

title: Hagia Sophia, İznik
fact: 787 CE — The Second Council of Nicaea begins at the Church of Holy Wisdom in the city of Nicaea in Bithynia.

title: Battle of the Thames
fact: 1813 — War of 1812: The Army of the Northwest defeats a British and Native Canadian force threatening Detroit.

title: 1138 Aleppo earthquake
fact: 1138 — A massive earthquake strikes Aleppo; it is one of the most destructive earthquakes ever.

title: 1114 Marash earthquake
fact: 1114 — A large earthquake damages the areas of the Crusaders in the Middle East. Antioch, Mamistra, Marash and Edessa are hit by the shocks.

title: Kingdom of Yugoslavia
fact: 1929 — King Alexander of the Serbs, Croats and Slovenes suspends his country's constitution, starting the January 6th Dictatorship.

title: SSLV Launch Complex
fact: 2024 — Prime Minister Modi of India inaugurates the 2nd Space Port of India - Kulasekarapattinam Spaceport.

title: Lawn Hill crater
fact: Lawn Hill ‘crater’ refers to an Ordovician impact structure, the eroded remnant of a former impact crater, situated approximately 220 km north-north-west of Mount Isa in northwestern Queensland, Australia. The site is marked by an 18 km diameter ring of dolomite hills.

title: Liverpool crater
fact: Liverpool is a meteorite impact crater situated in Arnhem Land within the Northern Territory, Australia. It was named after the nearby Liverpool River. Liverpool is remote and difficult to access. The crater has a raised, near-circular rim averaging about 1.6 km in diameter.

title: Rotmistrivka crater
fact: Rotmistrivka is an impact crater in Cherkasy Oblast, Ukraine, which is located near the village of Rotmistrivka. The crater is 2.7 kilometres (1.7 mi) in diameter, with an age estimated at 120 ± 10 million years (Lower Cretaceous).

title: Sobolev crater
fact: Impact crater, 53 m across. Sobolev (or Sobolevskiy, Sobolevskii) Crater is a meteorite crater in the Far Eastern Federal District of Russia. It is 53 metres (174 ft) in diameter and is estimated to be less than 1000 years old. The crater is exposed at the surface.

title: Steen River impact structure
fact: Steen River is an impact structure in Alberta, Canada. It is 25 km (16 mi) in diameter and the age is estimated to be 91 ± 7 million years (Late Cretaceous). The structure is not exposed at the surface.

title: Tabun-Khara-Obo crater
fact: Tabun-Khara-Obo is an impact crater in the Dornogovi Aimag (province) the south-east of Mongolia. The crater, which is exposed at the surface, is 1.3 km (0.81 mi) in diameter.

title: Tswaing crater
fact: Impact crater, 1.1 km across. Tswaing is an impact crater enclosed by a 1,946 ha nature reserve, situated in northern Gauteng province, South Africa.

title: Agen (meteorite)
fact: Meteorite, 30 kg. Agen is an H chondrite meteorite that fell to earth on September 5, 1814, in Aquitaine, France. It is an ordinary chondrite that belongs to the petrologic type 5, thus was assigned to the group H5.

title: Erg Chech 002
fact: Erg Chech 002 (EC 002) is an ancient andesite meteorite discovered in the Erg Chech region of the Sahara Desert in Algeria.

title: Imilac
fact: Imilac is a pallasite meteorite found in the Atacama Desert of Northern Chile in 1822.

title: Itqiy meteorite
fact: Meteorite recorded 1990. The Itqiy meteorite is an enstatite-rich stony-iron meteorite. It is classified as an enstatite chondrite of the EH group that was nearly melted and is therefore very unusual for that group.

title: Neuschwanstein (meteorite)
fact: Neuschwanstein was an enstatite chondrite (type EL6) meteorite that fell to Earth on 6 April 2002 at 22:20:18 GMT near Neuschwanstein Castle, Bavaria, at the Germany–Austria border.

title: Old Woman meteorite
fact: Meteorite recorded 1975. The Old Woman Meteorite is the largest meteorite to have been found in California and the second largest in the United States. It was discovered in the Old Woman Mountains in southern California in late March 1976.

title: Tenham (meteorite)
fact: Tenham meteorites are the fragments of a larger meteorite that fell in 1879 in a remote area of Australia near the Tenham station, South Gregory, in western Queensland. Although the fall was seen by a number of people, its exact date has not been established.

title: Toms Canyon impact crater
fact: Impact crater, 20 km across. The Toms Canyon impact crater is a probable impact crater where one or more asteroids struck the Atlantic continental shelf, about 100 miles (160 km) east of Atlantic City, New Jersey.

title: Uhackatik
fact: Impact crater, 25 km across. Uhackatik Crater is an impact crater in Quebec, Canada, near the border with Labrador. The crater is about 25 kilometres (16 mi) in diameter. The crater contains sheets of melt rock up to 50 metres (160 ft) thick.

title: Ames crater
fact: Ames crater is a meteorite crater (astrobleme) in Major County, Oklahoma, United States. Ames, Oklahoma is near the center of the structure, which is 30 miles (48 km) southwest of Enid, Oklahoma. Buried under a thick layer of sediment, it was not discovered until 1991.

title: Bedout
fact: Bedout, or more specifically the Bedout High, is a geological and geophysical feature centered about 250 km (160 miles) off the northwestern coast of Australia in the Canning and overlying Roebuck basins.

title: BP Impact Structure
fact: The BP Impact Structure, also known as Gebel Dalma, is a deeply eroded impact structure that is located 165 km (103 mi) northeast of the Kufra Oasis in southwest Libya.

title: Burckle Crater
fact: The Burckle crater is an undersea topographic feature about 29 kilometres (18 mi; 16 nmi) in diameter in the southwestern Indian Ocean.

title: Chukcha crater
fact: Chukcha is an impact crater in Taimyr Peninsula, Russia. It is 6 kilometres (3.7 mi) in diameter and the age is estimated to be less than 70 million years old (Cretaceous or younger). The crater is exposed to the surface.

title: Crawford crater
fact: Crawford is an impact crater near Adelaide in South Australia, Australia. The Crawford crater is up to 8.5 km long, and is thought to have been formed by oblique (low angle) impact. Its age is estimated to be greater than 35 million years (probably Eocene).

title: Dalgaranga crater
fact: Dalgaranga crater is a small meteorite impact crater located on Dalgaranga pastoral station 75 km (47 mi) northwest of Mount Magnet (or north of Yalgoo) in Western Australia.

title: Goat Paddock crater
fact: Goat Paddock Crater is an impact crater in a range of gently dipping Proterozoic sandstone in the Kimberley Region of northern Western Australia, 106 km west-southwest of Halls Creek.

title: Goyder crater
fact: Goyder is an impact structure (or astrobleme), the eroded remnant of a former impact crater. It is situated in Arnhem Land in the Northern Territory, Australia, and was named after the nearby Goyder River.

title: Haviland Crater
fact: The Haviland Crater, also called the Brenham Crater, is a meteorite crater (astrobleme) in Kiowa County, Kansas. The oval crater is 50 feet (15 m) in diameter, making it one of the smallest impact craters in the world. Its age is estimated to be less than 1,000 years.

title: Kamil Crater
fact: The Kamil Crater is a 44.8-metre-wide (147 ft) and 15.8-metre-deep (52 ft) (original depth, a part covered by sand at present) meteorite impact crater in the East Uweinat Desert in southwestern New Valley Governorate, Egypt…

title: Luizi crater
fact: Luizi is a meteorite impact structure that lies on the Kundelungu Plateau of Haut-Katanga province, in an underexplored region of southeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo.

title: Mahuika crater
fact: Mahuika crater was a hypothesized impact crater named after the Māori god of fire. It was described as being about 20 ± 2 km (12.4 ± 1.2 mi) wide and over 153 meters (502 ft) deep and on the New Zealand continental shelf at 48.3 South and 166.4 East, to the south of The Snares.

title: Nicholson crater
fact: Nicholson is a meteorite crater in the Northwest Territories, Canada. It is 12.5 kilometres (7.8 mi) in diameter and the age is estimated to be less than 400 million years (Devonian or earlier). The crater is not exposed at the surface.

title: Piccaninny crater
fact: Piccaninny crater is an impact structure, the eroded remnant of a former impact crater, situated in northern Western Australia in the Kimberley region. It was named after Piccaninny Creek and lies within the Purnululu (Bungle Bungle) National Park.

title: Pilot crater
fact: Impact crater, 6 km across. Pilot crater is an impact crater in the Northwest Territories, Canada, just north of the Alberta border and near Fort Smith 54 km (34 mi). It is 6 km (3.7 mi) in diameter and the age is estimated to be 445 ± 2 million years (Upper Ordovician).

title: Ragozinka crater
fact: Ragozinka is a meteorite crater in the Urals in Russia. It is 9 kilometres (5.6 mi) in diameter and the age is estimated to be 46 ± 3 million years old (Eocene). The crater is not exposed at the surface.

title: Riachão Ring
fact: The Riachão Ring is a meteorite impact crater in Brazil. It lies within the Parnaíba Basin. It is 4.5 kilometres (2.8 mi) in diameter and the age is estimated to be less than 200 million years (Jurassic or younger). The crater is exposed at the surface.

title: Sierra Madera crater
fact: The Sierra Madera crater is a complex impact crater (astrobleme) in southwestern Pecos County, Texas, United States.

title: Vista Alegre crater
fact: The Vista Alegre crater is a meteorite crater in Coronel Vivida, Paraná State, Brazil. On the surface it appears as a circular, relatively flat plain within otherwise hilly terrain.

title: Wells Creek crater
fact: Wells Creek is an impact crater located near Cumberland City, Tennessee. It is 12 kilometers (7.5 mi) in diameter and the age is estimated to be 200±100 Ma (million years old), placing it in the Jurassic or a neighboring period. The crater is exposed to the surface.

title: Zapadnaya crater
fact: Zapadnaya (Bilylivka) is an impact crater in Ukraine near the village of Bilylivka in the southeasternmost edge of Zhytomyr Oblast and near the border of Vinnytsia Oblast. It is situated in the northwestern part of the Ukrainian crystalline shield.

title: Zeleny Gai crater
fact: Zeleny Gai is an impact crater in Ukraine (Kirovohrad Oblast). It is 3.5 kilometres (2.2 mi) in diameter and the age is estimated to be 80 ± 20 million years (Upper Cretaceous). The crater is not exposed at the surface.

title: Akbarpur (meteorite)
fact: Meteorite, 1.8 kg. Akbarpur is an H chondrite meteorite that fell to earth on April 18, 1838, in Uttar Pradesh, India. It is notable for being the first Indian meteorite for which an official report accompanied by a legal deposition was filed.

title: Allegan (meteorite)
fact: Meteorite, 32 kg. Allegan is a type 5 H chondrite meteorite that landed west of Allegan, Michigan on July 10, 1899. Allegan weighed around fifty pounds after its landing. As of 1964, it was one of only seven known meteorites to land in Michigan.

title: Avanhandava (meteorite)
fact: Meteorite, 9.3 kg. Avanhandava is an H chondrite meteorite that fell to earth in 1952 in São Paulo, Brazil. It is classified as H4-ordinary chondrite. A total of 9.33 kilograms (20.6 lb) of this meteorite was collected after it broke up during its impact with the Earth.

title: Elbogen (meteorite)
fact: Elbogen, also the Loket Iron, is an iron meteorite that fell in the town of Loket, Karlovy Vary Region, Kingdom of Bohemia, about the year 1400.

title: Goose Lake meteorite
fact: The Goose Lake meteorite is a meteorite that was found at Goose Lake in the United States by two hunters from Oakland, California on October 13, 1938. In 1939 it was acquired by the United States National Museum.

title: Karoonda meteorite
fact: The Karoonda meteorite is a meteorite that fell to earth on 25 November 1930 at 10:53 pm near the South Australian town of Karoonda. It is of a rare composition, being carbonaceous chondrite, and is also rare in that it was found so soon after its landing.

title: Kesen meteorite
fact: The Kesen meteorite fell on 13 June 1850, landing in a swamp in the outskirts of the city of Rikuzentakata, Kesen District in Iwate Prefecture, Japan.

title: Park Forest (meteorite)
fact: Park Forest is an L5 chondrite meteorite that fell on 26 March 2003 in Illinois, United States.

title: Patos de Minas (meteorite)
fact: Meteorite, 200 kg. Patos de Minas is an octahedrite meteorite. It was found in 1925 and 2002 in Patos de Minas, Minas Gerais, Brazil. It weighs 200 kilograms (440 lb) and has average dimensions of 54 by 33 by 22 centimetres (21.3 in × 13.0 in × 8.7 in).

title: Weston meteorite
fact: The Weston meteorite is an H4 ordinary chondrite meteorite which fell to earth above the town of Weston, Connecticut on the morning of December 14, 1807.

title: Winona meteorite
fact: Meteorite recorded 1928. The Winona meteorite is a primitive achondrite meteorite. It is the type specimen and by far the largest meteorite of the winonaite group.

title: Zabrodje meteorite
fact: Zabrodje is an ordinary chondrite that fell through a roof of a house in the village of Zabroddzie, Stowbtsy District approximately two hours before dawn on 22 September 1893. Only one fragment was recovered.

title: Avak crater
fact: Impact crater, 8 km across. Avak is an impact crater centered approximately 12 km (7.5 mi) southeast of Utqiagvik, Alaska, United States. Avak is a subcircular structure about 12 km (7.5 mi) in diameter and 1 km (0.62 mi) deep.

title: Azuara impact structure
fact: The Azuara structure is a structural feature of about 30 kilometres (19 mi) diameter, located in northeastern Spain, roughly 50 kilometres (31 mi) south of Zaragoza. The name is attributed to the small town of Azuara located near the center of the structure.

title: Couture crater
fact: Couture Crater is a crater in Northern Quebec, Canada. It was filled with water, making it also a lake. It is located near Hudson Bay in the Kativik territory. The crater is around 150 meters deep. Most of the lake covers an 8 km in diameter impact crater.

title: Crooked Creek crater
fact: Crooked Creek is an impact crater in Crawford County, Missouri, United States. It is 4.3 miles (7 km) in diameter and the age is estimated to be 320 ± 80 million years (Mississippian). The crater is exposed to the surface.

title: Darwin Crater
fact: Darwin Crater is a suspected meteorite impact crater in Western Tasmania about 26 km (16 mi) south of Queenstown, just within the Franklin-Gordon Wild Rivers National Park.

title: Deep Bay crater
fact: Deep Bay is a bay near the south-western tip of Reindeer Lake in Saskatchewan, Canada. The bay is strikingly circular and very deep (220 m) in an otherwise irregular and shallow lake. It is the deepest body of water in Saskatchewan.

title: Foelsche crater
fact: Foelsche is a partly buried impact structure (or astrobleme), the eroded remnant of a former impact crater. It is situated about 85 km southeast of Borroloola in the Northern Territory, Australia, and named after the nearby Foelsche River.

title: Hickman crater
fact: The Hickman crater is a recently discovered meteorite impact crater, 16 kilometres northeast of the Hope Downs 4 Mine and 35 kilometres north of Newman in the Ophthalmia Range, Western Australia.

title: Jabel Waqf as Suwwan crater
fact: The Jabal Waqf es Suwwan crater is an impact crater in Ma'an Governorate, Jordan, near the Saudi border. The crater has a diameter of 5.5 kilometres (3.4 mi). It is estimated at 37–56 million years old. It is exposed at the surface.
story_label: Wikipedia: Jabel Waqf as Suwwan crater

title: Kentland crater
fact: The Kentland structure, also known as the Kentland crater or the Kentland disturbed area, is an impact structure located near the town of Kentland in Newton County, Indiana, United States. It was discovered about 1880 when two farmers began to quarry crushed rock there.

title: Kgagodi crater
fact: Impact crater, 3.5 km across. Kgagodi is an exposed meteorite impact crater in Botswana. It is located south of the village of Kgagodi in Central Botswana.

title: Marquez crater
fact: Marquez crater is a meteorite crater located in Leon County, Texas near the small town of Marquez about 177 km (110 mi) northeast of Austin, Texas, United States. It is 12.7 km (8 mi) in diameter and the age is estimated to be 58 ± 2 million years (Paleocene).

title: Mishina Gora crater
fact: Mishina Gora is an impact crater in European Russia, 180 kilometres southwest of St. Petersburg. It is located in Pskov Oblast of the Northwestern Federal District.

title: Mizarai crater
fact: Mizarai is a meteorite impact crater in Druskininkai municipality, Lithuania. The crater, being the second largest in the country, is not exposed to the surface and the site now hosts Mizarai village.

title: Mount Toondina crater
fact: Mount Toondina crater is an impact structure (or astrobleme), the eroded remnant of a former impact crater, located in northern South Australia in the locality of Allandale Station about 24 km (15 mi) south of the town of Oodnadatta.

title: Río Cuarto craters
fact: The Río Cuarto craters is the name given to a set of ten elongate, rimmed depressions that lie within the Pampas of Córdoba Province, (central Argentina). These depressions are aligned and distributed along a northeast to southwest trending line for a distance of 50 km (31 mi).

title: Ritland crater
fact: The Ritland crater is an impact crater at Ritland farm in Hjelmeland Municipality in eastern Rogaland county, Norway. The crater is about 15 kilometres (9.3 mi) east of the village of Hjelmelandsvågen and about 8 kilometres (5.0 mi) south of the Jøsenfjorden.

title: Wetumpka crater
fact: The Wetumpka impact crater is the only confirmed impact crater in Alabama, United States. It is located east of downtown Wetumpka in Elmore County.

title: Adzhi-Bogdo
fact: Meteorite recorded 1949. The Adzhi-Bogdo is a chondrite meteorite weighing 910 grams (32 oz). It was found on October 30, 1949, in Govi-Altay, Mongolia.

title: Angers (meteorite)
fact: Angers is an ordinary chondrite meteorite that fell in Pays de la Loire, France, at 8:15 PM on 3 June 1822.

title: Angra dos Reis meteorite
fact: Meteorite, 1.5 kg. The Angra dos Reis meteorite is the type specimen of the angrite group. It was observed when it fell to Earth in 1869.

title: Anlong (meteorite)
fact: Anlong is an H chondrite meteorite that fell to earth on May 2, 1971, in Guizhou, China.

title: Appley Bridge meteorite
fact: Meteorite, 15 kg. The Appley Bridge meteorite is a meteorite that hit ground at Halliwell Farm in Appley Bridge, Lancashire, England at around 8:45 p.m. on Tuesday, 13 October 1914.

title: Brachina meteorite
fact: Meteorite recorded 26 May 1974. The Brachina meteorite is the type specimen of the brachinites class of the asteroidal achondrites.

title: Buzzard Coulee meteorite
fact: Meteorite, 41 kg. Buzzard Coulee is the collective name of the meteorites fallen on November 20, 2008, over Saskatchewan, Canada.

title: Esquel (meteorite)
fact: Meteorite recorded 1951. Esquel is a meteorite found near Esquel, a Patagonian town in the northwest part of the province of Chubut in Argentina. It is a pallasite, a type of stony–iron meteorite that when cut and polished shows yellowish olivine (peridot) crystals.

title: Kainsaz meteorite
fact: Fifteen pieces of the Kainsaz meteorite were seen to fall near Kainsaz, Muslyumovo, Tatarstan in the Russian SFSR on September 13, 1937. The largest weighed 102.5 kilograms (226 lb), the total weight was ~200 kilograms (440 lb).

title: Mineo (meteorite)
fact: Mineo was one of the only four witnessed fall pallasite meteorites in the world, and the only one from Italy.

title: Richardton meteorite
fact: The Richardton meteorite is a 90 kilograms (200 lb) H5 Ordinary chondrite that was seen to fall at 21:48 on 30 June 1918 between Mott, North Dakota and Richardton, North Dakota, United States.

title: Winchcombe meteorite
fact: Meteorite, 602 g. The Winchcombe meteorite is a carbonaceous chondrite meteorite that was observed entering the Earth's atmosphere as a fluorescent green fireball over Gloucestershire, England, at 21:54 on 28 February 2021.

title: Wold Cottage meteorite
fact: The Wold Cottage meteorite fell near Wold Cottage farm in 1795, a few miles away from the village of Wold Newton in Yorkshire, England.

title: Calvin crater
fact: Calvin is an impact crater located in Calvin Township, Cass County, in the U.S. state of Michigan. It was discovered in 1987 by Randall Milstein of the Michigan Geological Survey while examining data from about 100 test wells drilled in the area.

title: Cerro do Jarau crater
fact: Cerro do Jarau crater is a 13.5 kilometres (8.4 mi) diameter circular feature in the Paraná Basin, Rio Grande do Sul in southern Brazil, close to the border with Uruguay. The Russian Academy of Sciences lists the structure as a probable impact crater.

title: Colônia crater
fact: The Colônia crater is a recently confirmed impact crater located in the municipality of São Paulo, Brazil.

title: Connolly Basin crater
fact: Connolly Basin is a 9 km-diameter impact crater located in the Gibson Desert of central Western Australia. It lies adjacent to the Talawana Track 45 km west of the junction (Windy Corner) with the Gary Highway, but is difficult to access due to the remoteness of the area.

title: Kalkkop crater
fact: Kalkkop is an impact crater which can be found on a private farm 50 kilometres (31 mi) south east of the town of Aberdeen, Eastern Cape, in the Eastern Cape Province of South Africa.

title: La Moinerie crater
fact: La Moinerie is an impact crater in Quebec, Canada. It is 8 km in diameter and the age is estimated to be 400 ± 50 million years (Silurian or Devonian). The crater is exposed to the surface and filled with water, forming Lac La Moinerie.

title: Luna crater
fact: The Luna crater or Luna structure is an impact crater at Luna village in Bhuj taluka of Kutch district of Gujarat, India.

title: Serpent Mound crater
fact: Serpent Mound crater, also known as the Serpent Mound Disturbance, is an eroded meteorite impact crater in Ohio, United States. It lies largely in Adams County, with the northern part mostly in Highland County, except for a small northeast part in Pike County.

title: Vargeão Dome
fact: Vargeão Dome is an impact crater in Santa Catarina, Brazil, straddling the municipalities of Vargeão, Faxinal dos Guedes, and Passos Maia.

title: Viewfield crater
fact: Viewfield is an impact crater in Saskatchewan, Canada. It is 2.5 kilometres (1.6 mi) in diameter and the age is estimated to be 190 ± 20 million years (Early Jurassic or Late Triassic). The crater is not exposed at the surface.

title: Whitecourt crater
fact: Impact crater, 36 m across. Whitecourt crater is a meteorite impact crater in central Alberta, Canada, located approximately 10 km (6.2 mi) southeast of the Town of Whitecourt within Woodlands County.

title: Yilan crater
fact: Impact crater, 1.9 km across. Yilan crater is an impact crater in China, situated to the northwest of the town of Yilan in Heilongjiang province. Its southern rim has eroded, but its northern rim is visible on the surface as a crescent-shaped ridge.

title: Adhi Kot (meteorite)
fact: Meteorite, 4.2 kg. Adhi Kot is a meteorite that fell on 1 May 1919 in the Punjab region, located in now Pakistan.

title: Alais meteorite
fact: Meteorite, 6 kg, recorded 1806. Alais or Allais is the first carbonaceous chondrite meteorite identified. It fell near Alès in 1806 in multiple fragments which together weighed 6 kg (13 lb 4 oz), although only 0.26 kg (9.2 oz) remains.

title: Ambapur Nagla meteorite
fact: Meteorite, 6.4 kg. Ambapur Nagla is an H chondrite meteorite that fell to earth on May 27, 1895, in Uttar Pradesh, India. It is classified as H5-ordinary chondrite.

title: Arbol Solo (meteorite)
fact: Arbol Solo is an H chondrite meteorite that fell to earth on September 11, 1954, in the province of San Luis, Argentina.

title: Assisi (meteorite)
fact: Assisi is an H chondrite meteorite that fell to earth at 7:00 am on May 24, 1886, in Perugia, Umbria, Italy. Only one single 2 kilograms (4.4 lb) stone was found.

title: Bassikounou meteorite
fact: Bassikounou meteorite is a chondrite meteorite whose fall was observed on October 16, 2006, near the town of Bassikounou, in the Hodh Ech Chargui Region, south-east of Mauritania, near the border with Mali.

title: Bear Creek (meteorite)
fact: Meteorite, 227 kg. The Bear Creek meteorite, formerly known as the Colorado meteorite, is an octahedrite meteorite that was found in 1866 in Jefferson County, Colorado, United States.

title: Bovedy (meteorite)
fact: Meteorite, 5.5 kg. Bovedy is a meteorite that fell in the area of Bovedy, Northern Ireland, on 25 April 1969. After entering the atmosphere over the Bristol Channel, it traversed Wales and the Irish Sea before landing near Limavady. The meteorite had broken into two pieces.

title: Braunschweig meteorite
fact: The Braunschweig meteorite is a 1.3 kilograms (2.9 pounds) meteorite that hit Melverode, a suburb in Braunschweig, Germany, at around 2:05 AM on 23 April 2013.

title: Claxton meteorite
fact: Claxton is an L6 chondrite meteorite that fell to earth on December 10, 1984 in Georgia, United States. It is the only known meteorite to directly strike a mailbox.

title: Coahuila meteorite
fact: Meteorite recorded 1837. The Coahuila meteorite is a hexahedrite iron meteorite found in Coahuila, Mexico. The large number of fragments has led to many synonyms and many authors think that more than one meteorite is represented by the fragments.

title: Grant meteorite
fact: Meteorite recorded 1929. The Grant Meteorite is a meteorite that was discovered in the Zuni Mountains, about 45 miles (72 km) south of Grants, New Mexico (for which it was named). It was unearthed in 1929 although the date of its original groundfall is unknown.

title: Homestead (meteorite)
fact: Homestead is a L5 meteorite fallen on 12 February 1875 in Iowa, United States, first described by Gustavus Detlef Hinrichs.

title: Khatyrka meteorite
fact: Khatyrka is a meteorite found in 2011 in the valley of the Iomrautvaam, a tributary of the Khatyrka river, Chukotka Autonomous Okrug, Russian Far East. It is a CV3 (oxidized) chondrite meteorite.

title: Lake Murray meteorite
fact: Meteorite recorded 1933. The Lake Murray Meteorite, the largest of its kind ever found in Oklahoma. It was discovered on a farm in Carter County, Oklahoma in 1933.

title: Middlesbrough meteorite
fact: The Middlesbrough meteorite fell in Middlesbrough, North Yorkshire, England on 14 March 1881. The meteorite fell in the afternoon, hitting the ground around 3:35 pm.

title: Monte Milone (meteorite)
fact: Monte Milone is meteorite that fell in 1846 in central Italy.

title: Norton County (meteorite)
fact: Norton County is an Aubrite meteorite that fell in 1948 in Kansas, United States.

title: Novato meteorite
fact: The Novato meteorite is an ordinary chondrite which entered the Earth's atmosphere and broke up over Northern California at 19:44 Pacific Time on 17 October 2012.

title: Oesel meteorite
fact: The Oesel meteorite, also known as the Kaande meteorite or Kaanda meteorite, was a meteorite that fell in the village of Merise on the island of Saaremaa, Estonia, in 1855.

title: Omolon (meteorite)
fact: Omolon is a meteorite fallen in 1981 in the Omolon River basin, Magadan (Russia). It is a pallasite.

title: Padvarninkai meteorite
fact: Padvarninkai meteorite is a meteorite that fell on 9 February 1929 near the village of Padvarninkai located near Andrioniškis, Anykščiai District Municipality, Lithuania.

title: Seymchan (meteorite)
fact: Seymchan is a pallasite meteorite found in the dry bed of the river Hekandue, a left tributary of river Yasachnaya in the Magadan district, Russia, near the settlement of Seymchan, in June 1967.

title: Springwater meteorite
fact: The Springwater meteorite is a stony-iron pallasite, found near Springwater, Saskatchewan in 1931. At that time the find consisted of three large masses.6 kilograms (85 lb), 18.6 kilograms (41 lb) and 10.6 kilograms (23 lb).

title: Tucson Ring meteorite
fact: The Tucson Ring meteorite is a brezinaite meteorite fragment, first described by Bunch and Fuchs.

title: Yamato 691
fact: The Yamato 691 is a 4.5 billion year old chondrite meteorite discovered by members of the Japanese Antarctic Research Expedition on the blue ice field of the Queen Fabiola Mountains (Yamato Mountains) in Antarctica, on December 21, 1969.

title: Zaisho
fact: Meteorite, 330 g. Zaisho is the name of a stony-iron pallasite meteorite whose fall in Japan in February 1898 was recorded by observers on the ground. Zaisho made landfall in the city of Kami, located in the prefecture of Kōchi on Shikoku Island.

title: Žemaitkiemis meteorite
fact: Žemaitkiemis meteorite is an ordinary chondrite that fell near Žemaitkiemis, Lithuania at about 8:33 pm on 2 February 1933. Using the argon–argon dating method, scientists have calculated its age to be about 520 million years. The fall was observed by the Koenigsberg Observatory.

title: Corossol crater
fact: The Corossol structure, which is also known as the Corossol crater, is a circular, 4.3-by-3.9-kilometre (2.7 by 2.4 mi) in diameter…

title: Decaturville crater
fact: The Decaturville crater, also referred to as the Decaturville Dome, is an impact crater near the town of Decaturville, Missouri, United States.

title: Des Plaines crater
fact: The Des Plaines crater or Des Plaines disturbance is recognized as an impact crater in Cook County, Illinois, United States. It is located beneath the eastern part of the city of Des Plaines, which is a suburb of Chicago.

title: Dhala impact structure
fact: The Dhala impact structure is an impact structure formed by an asteroid impact. It is situated near Bhonti village in Pichhore block of Shivpuri district of Madhya Pradesh state in India.

title: Flynn Creek crater
fact: Flynn Creek crater is an impact crater situated in Jackson County, Tennessee, approximately 8 km south of Gainesboro.

title: Glikson crater
fact: Glikson crater is an impact structure (or astrobleme), the eroded remnant of an impact crater, situated in the Little Sandy Desert of central Western Australia.

title: Glover Bluff crater
fact: The Glover Buff crater is an impact crater located in Wisconsin, United States. It has a diameter of about 8 kilometres (5.0 miles) and is partially exposed, however it has eroded significantly. Shatter cones are associated with this impact structure.

title: Maple Creek crater
fact: Maple Creek is a subterranean meteorite crater in Saskatchewan, Canada. It is 6 km (3.7 mi) in diameter and the age is estimated to be less than 75 million years (Late Cretaceous or younger). The crater is buried beneath younger sediment and cannot be seen at the surface.

title: Matt Wilson (crater)
fact: Matt Wilson is a confirmed impact crater, elliptical in shape and situated in Gregory National Park about 17 kilometres (11 mi) north of the Victoria River Roadhouse in the Northern Territory, Australia.

title: Middlesboro crater
fact: The Middlesboro crater (or astrobleme) is a meteorite crater in Kentucky, United States. It is named after the city of Middlesboro, Kentucky, which today occupies much of the crater.

title: Newporte crater
fact: Newporte is a meteorite crater in North Dakota, United States. It is 3.2 km in diameter and the age is estimated to be less than 500 million years (Cambrian or younger). The crater is not exposed at the surface.

title: Red Wing crater
fact: Red Wing or Red Wing Creek structure is a meteor crater located in McKenzie County, North Dakota, about 24 km (15 mi) southwest of Watford City, North Dakota, United States.

title: Sirente crater
fact: The Sirente crater is a small shallow seasonal lake in Abruzzo, central Italy. The depression, which is located at the center of the Prati del Sirente, a mountainous highland north of the Sirente massif in the Apennines, is 13 km (8.1 mi) from the village of Secinaro.

title: Tunnunik impact structure
fact: The Tunnunik impact structure, formerly known as the Prince Albert Impact Crater, is a recently confirmed meteorite impact structure. It is located on Prince Albert Peninsula in the northwestern part of Victoria Island in Canada's Northwest Territories.

title: Archie (meteorite)
fact: Archie is an H chondrite meteorite that fell to earth on August 10, 1932, in Archie, Missouri.

title: Atoka meteorite
fact: The Atoka meteorite is an L6 meteorite which fell to earth near Atoka, Oklahoma, in 1945. It weighs 1,384 grams (48.8 oz).

title: Auckland (meteorite)
fact: The Auckland meteorite, also known as the Ellerslie meteorite, landed in Ellerslie, a suburb of Auckland, New Zealand, on 12 June 2004. It crashed through the roof of a house and landed in the living room.

title: Beardsley meteorite
fact: The Beardsley meteorite is a meteorite that fell in Beardsley, Kansas, on October 15, 1929. Three samples were preserved, one collected the following day, at Michigan State University, and two collected two years later, at the Smithsonian Institution and Arizona State University.

title: Benton meteorite
fact: Benton is a meteorite found near the village of Benton, New Brunswick following a fireball. Two masses were found but the meteorites were split up. The largest fragment is now in the Canadian National Meteorite Collection, Ottawa.

title: Blithfield meteorite
fact: Meteorite recorded 13 August 1910. The Blithfield meteorite was found by Joseph Legree in Blithfield Township, Renfrew County, Ontario and measured about 8 centimetres (3.1 in) x 10 centimetres (3.9 in) x 13.5 centimetres (5.3 in).

title: Cranbourne meteorite
fact: Meteorite recorded 1854. The Cranbourne meteorite is an octahedrite iron meteorite, classified as a main group IAB meteorite.

title: D'Orbigny meteorite
fact: D'Orbigny meteorite was found near Buenos Aires, Argentina in September 1979. It is the largest angrite found to date.

title: Huckitta (meteorite)
fact: Meteorite recorded 1924. Huckitta is a pallasite meteorite recovered in 1937 from Huckitta Cattle Station in the Northern Territory of Australia.

title: Jodzie
fact: Jodzie is a meteorite that fell on 17 June 1877 near the village of Juodžiai near Panevėžys. It is a relatively rare howardite with some carbonaceous inclusions that were likely a result of an asteroid collision.

title: Moss meteorite
fact: Moss is a carbonaceous chondrite meteorite that fell over the communities of Rygge and Moss in Østfold county, southeast southern Norway in the morning of midsummer day, July 14, 2006. The last time a type CO3 meteorite fell from the sky was in 1937 with Kainsaz, Russia.

title: Paragould meteorite
fact: The Paragould Meteorite at 41 inches (1,000 mm) by 24 inches (610 mm) by 16 inches (410 mm) and weighing 370 kilograms (820 lb) is the second largest witnessed meteorite fall ever recovered in North America (after the Norton County meteorite) and the largest stony meteorite…

title: Pavlovka (meteorite)
fact: Pavlovka is a howardite meteorite fallen in 1882 near a village of Pavlovka, in the western part of modern Saratov Oblast, Russia. It is currently stored in the meteorite collection of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

title: Peace River (meteorite)
fact: Peace River is a small L6 chondrite meteorite that detonated over Alberta, Canada on the morning of March 31, 1963.

title: Santa Vitoria do Palmar meteorite
fact: The Santa Vitoria do Palmar meteorite was found near the city of Santa Vitoria do Palmar in Brazil in 2003 (three stones) and 2004 (one stone).
story_label: Wikipedia: Santa Vitoria do Palmar meteorite

title: Serra Pelada (meteorite)
fact: Serra Pelada meteorite is a meteorite found in Curionópolis, in the state of the Pará, Brazil. Its fall was observed on June 29, 2017, by people in Eldorado dos Carajás, Marabá and Parauapebas.

title: St-Robert meteorite
fact: St-Robert is an ordinary chondrite meteorite that fell in Quebec on June 14, 1994.

title: Tamdakht meteorite
fact: Meteorite recorded 2009. The Tamdakht meteorite fell near Ouarzazate, Morocco on 20 December 2008 producing a strewn field of approximately 25 kilometres (16 mi) by 2 kilometres (1.2 mi) and two small impact craters…

title: Vermillion meteorite
fact: Meteorite recorded 1991. The Vermillion meteorite is a pallasite (stony-iron) meteorite and one of two members of the pyroxene pallasite grouplet.

title: Bloody Creek crater
fact: Bloody Creek crater, which is also known as the Bloody Creek structure, is a 420-by-350-meter (1,380 by 1,150 ft) in diameter elliptical feature that is located in southwestern Nova Scotia, Canada.

title: Cloud Creek crater
fact: Cloud Creek crater is an impact crater in Wyoming, United States. The crater is located in Natrona County, about 48 miles (77 km) northwest of Casper, near the center of a geological feature known as the Casper Arch.

title: Decorah crater
fact: The Decorah crater, also called the Decorah impact structure, is a possible impact crater located on the east side of the city of Decorah in Iowa, United States.

title: Île Rouleau crater
fact: Île Rouleau is an impact crater in Baie-James, Quebec, Canada, located on a small, uninhabited island in Lake Mistassini in the centre of the province. The crater is 4 kilometres (2.5 mi) in diameter and the age is estimated to be less than 300 million years (Permian or younger).

title: Johnsonville crater
fact: The Johnsonville crater or the Snow's Island crater is a circular geophysical feature situated at the junction of the Lynches River and the Pee Dee River in South Carolina, United States, which has been interpreted by some scientists as an impact crater.

title: List of impact structures in Asia and Russia
fact: This list includes all 31 confirmed impact structures in Asia and Russia as listed in the Earth Impact Database. These features were caused by the collision of large meteorites or comets with the Earth.
story_label: Wikipedia: List of impact structures in Asia and Russia

title: Målingen Crater
fact: Målingen was confirmed as an impact crater in 2014. It is located near the city of Östersund in northern Sweden. It is "probable" that it formed simultaneously with the nearby Lockne crater.

title: Santa Marta crater
fact: Santa Marta crater is a confirmed impact crater in Piauí State, northeastern Brazil. It is 10 kilometres (6.2 mi) in diameter and it is estimated to have formed between 100 and 66 Ma, during the Late Cretaceous.

title: Stac Fada Member
fact: The Stac Fada Member is a distinctive layer towards the top of the Mesoproterozoic Bay of Stoer Formation, part of the Stoer Group (lowermost Torridonian Supergroup) in northwest Scotland.

title: West Hawk Lake
fact: West Hawk Lake is an impact crater lake on the Whiteshell River located in the Whiteshell Provincial Park in southeastern Manitoba, Canada.

title: 2024 Lekki flood
fact: On 4 July 2024, heavy rainfall caused flooding in Lekki, a city in Lagos State, Nigeria. The flooding caused significant damage to residential areas in Ibeju-Lekki and other affected locations. The streets were covered in water, buildings collapsed, and cars were swept away.

title: 2026 Niscemi landslide
fact: A major landslide happened at the town of Niscemi, in Province of Caltanissetta, Sicily, Italy in 2026. A 4 km section of land collapsed, damaging buildings and infrastructure and causing the evacuation of over 1000 residents.

title: Lenin Peak disaster
fact: The Lenin Peak disaster occurred on 13 July 1990 when 43 climbers were killed during an avalanche on the 7,134-meter-high mountain peak in northeast Tajikistan and Kyrgyzstan (then part of the USSR).

title: Tuve landslide
fact: The Tuve landslide was a large landslide in Tuve, Gothenburg, Sweden on 30 November 1977. Some 67 houses were destroyed, killing 9, injuring about 60 and making around 600 people homeless. The slide began at 16.05 and lasted 5–6 minutes.

title: 2011–2012 Puyehue-Cordón Caulle eruption
fact: The 2011–2012 Puyehue-Cordón Caulle eruption was a volcanic eruption that began in the Puyehue-Cordón Caulle volcanic complex in Chile on 4 June 2011.

title: 2011 Nabro eruption
fact: The 2011 Nabro eruption was an eruption of the Nabro stratovolcano in the Southern Red Sea Region of Eritrea, which began on 12 June 2011 after a series of earthquakes.

title: 2026 Zona da Mata floods
fact: In February 2026, floods and landslides caused by extreme precipitation events occurred in the Zona da Mata region of the state of Minas Gerais, Brazil, leaving 73 people dead. The disaster is the deadliest of its type in the country since the Rio Grande do Sul floods in 2024.

title: Eruption of Trevejo
fact: The eruption of the Trevejo volcano, also called the eruption of the Arenas Negras volcano, was a volcanic eruption that took place from 5 to 14 May 1706, about 8 km (5.0 mi) kilometers south of the Garachico in the north of the island of Tenerife (Spain).

title: 2025 Rio Bonito do Iguaçu tornado
fact: During the evening hours of November 7, 2025, a destructive and extremely large tornado devastated the municipality of Rio Bonito do Iguaçu in Paraná, Brazil, killing five people (one indirectly), injuring 835 others, and causing widespread damage.
story_label: Wikipedia: 2025 Rio Bonito do Iguaçu tornado

title: 2025 Vale do Aço floods
fact: The 2025 Vale do Aço floods were a series of floods and landslides, caused by extreme precipitation events that occurred in the Vale do Aço metropolitan area in the interior of the state of Minas Gerais, Brazil on 12 and 13 January 2025.

title: Port Royal
fact: Port Royal (Jamaican Patois: Puot Rayal) is a small town located at the end of the Palisadoes, at the mouth of Kingston Harbour, in southeastern Jamaica.

title: Prince Edward Islands
fact: The Prince Edward Islands are two small uninhabited subantarctic volcanic islands in the southern Indian Ocean that are administered by South Africa. They are named Marion Island and Prince Edward Island.

title: Pripyat
fact: Pripyat, also known as Prypiat, is an abandoned industrial city in Kyiv Oblast, Ukraine, located near the border with Belarus. Named after the nearby river Pripyat, it was founded on 4 February 1970.

title: Puerto Ayora
fact: Puerto Ayora, sometimes referred to as Santa Cruz, is a town in central Galápagos, Ecuador, on the southern shore of Santa Cruz Island. It is the seat of Santa Cruz Canton and is named for Isidro Ayora, a president of Ecuador.

title: Puerto Baquerizo Moreno
fact: Puerto Baquerizo Moreno is the capital of Galápagos Province, Ecuador. It is located on the southwestern coast of San Cristóbal, the easternmost island in the archipelago, and is the capital of San Cristóbal Canton.

title: Puerto Williams
fact: Puerto Williams is a city, port and naval base on Navarino Island in Chile. It faces the Beagle Channel.

title: Punta Arenas
fact: Punta Arenas is the capital city of Chile's southernmost region, Magallanes and Antarctica Chilena. Although the city officially was renamed Magallanes in 1927, its name was changed back to Punta Arenas in 1938.

title: Pyramiden
fact: Pyramiden is an abandoned Soviet coal mining settlement on the Norwegian archipelago of Svalbard which has become a tourist destination.

title: Qaanaaq
fact: Qaanaaq, formerly known as New Thule, is the main town in the northern part of the Avannaata municipality in northwestern Greenland. The town has a population of 591 as of 2025.

title: Rábida Island
fact: Rábida or Rabida Island is one of the Galápagos Islands. It is 5 km2 (1.9 sq mi) in area.

title: Resolute, Nunavut
fact: Resolute or Resolute Bay is an Inuit hamlet on Cornwallis Island in Nunavut, Canada. It is at the northern end of Resolute Bay and the Northwest Passage and is part of the Qikiqtaaluk Region.

title: Rhyolite, Nevada
fact: Rhyolite is a ghost town in Nye County, Nevada, United States. It is in the Bullfrog Hills, about 120 miles (190 km) northwest of Las Vegas, near the eastern boundary of Death Valley National Park.

title: Robinson Crusoe Island
fact: Robinson Crusoe Island is the second largest of the Juan Fernández Islands, situated 670 km (362 nmi; 416 mi) west of San Antonio, Chile, in the South Pacific Ocean.

title: Roscigno
fact: Roscigno is a small town and comune in Salerno, Campania, Italy. It is located on the slope of Monte Pruno.

title: Ross Island, South Andaman district
fact: Ross Island, officially named Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Island, is an island of the Andaman Islands. It belongs to the South Andaman administrative district, Andaman and Nicobar Islands. The island is situated 3 km (2 mi) east from central Port Blair.
story_label: Wikipedia: Ross Island, South Andaman district

title: Ryugyong Hotel
fact: The Ryugyong Hotel, sometimes spelled as Yu-Kyung Hotel, is a 330 m (1,080 ft) tall unfinished pyramid-shaped skyscraper in Pyongyang, North Korea. Its name is also one of the historical names for Pyongyang.

title: Saint Elmo, Colorado
fact: Saint Elmo is a ghost town in Chaffee County, Colorado, United States. Founded in 1880, Saint Elmo lies in the heart of the Sawatch Range, 20 miles (32 km) southwest of Buena Vista and sits at an elevation of 9,961 feet (3,036 m).

title: Saint Helena
fact: Saint Helena is a volcanic tropical island located in the South Atlantic Ocean, west of Africa. The nearest countries geographically are Angola and Namibia.

title: Salas y Gómez Island
fact: Isla Salas y Gómez, also known as Isla Sala y Gómez, is a small uninhabited Chilean island in the Pacific Ocean. It is sometimes considered the easternmost point in the Polynesian Triangle.

title: Salton Sea
fact: The Salton Sea is a shallow, landlocked, highly saline endorheic lake in Riverside and Imperial counties in Southern California. It lies on the San Andreas Fault within the Salton Trough, which stretches to the Gulf of California in Mexico.

title: Santa Claus, Indiana
fact: Santa Claus is a town in Spencer County, Indiana, United States, in the southwestern part of the state. The population was 2,586 at the 2020 census. It is home to numerous Christmas themed attractions, including Holiday World & Splashin' Safari and Santa's Candy Castle.

title: Santa Cruz Island (Galápagos)
fact: Santa Cruz Island, also known as Indefatigable Island and by other names, is the most populous and second-largest island in the Galápagos Islands, Ecuador.

title: Sanzhi UFO houses
fact: The Sanzhi UFO Houses, also known as the UFO houses of Sanjhih, Sanjhih pod houses or Sanjhih Pod City, were a set of abandoned and never-completed pod-shaped buildings in Sanzhi District, New Taipei, Taiwan.

title: Shemya
fact: Shemya or Simiya is a small island in the Semichi Islands group of the Near Islands chain in the Aleutian Islands archipelago southwest of Alaska, at 52°43′27″N 174°07′08″E. It has a land area of 5.903 sq mi (15.29 km2)…

title: Siorapaluk
fact: Siorapaluk or Hiurapaluk (Polar Inuit) is a settlement in the Qaanaaq area of the Avannaata municipality in northern Greenland. The settlement is located in the northern shore of the Siorapaluup Kangerlua (Robertson Fjord).

title: Slab City, California
fact: Slab City, also called The Slabs, is an unincorporated, off-the-grid alternative lifestyle community consisting largely of snowbirds in the Salton Trough area of the Sonoran Desert, in Imperial County, California.

title: Snowflake, Arizona
fact: Snowflake is a town in Navajo County, Arizona, United States. It was founded in 1878 by Erastus Snow and William Jordan Flake, Mormon pioneers. As of the 2020 census, Snowflake had a population of 6,104. Snowflake is 25 miles (40 km) south of Interstate 40 via Highway 77.

title: Socorro Island
fact: Socorro Island is a volcanic island in the Revillagigedo Islands, a Mexican possession lying 600 kilometres (370 mi) off the country's western coast. The size is 16.5 by 11.5 km (10.3 by 7.1 mi), with an area of 132 km2 (51 sq mi).

title: South Georgia
fact: South Georgia is an island in the South Atlantic Ocean that is part of the British Overseas Territory of South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands. It lies around 1,400 kilometres (870 mi; 756 nmi) east of the Falkland Islands.

title: South Plaza Island
fact: South Plaza is a small island off the east coast of Santa Cruz in the Galápagos Islands. Described as having a crescent-shaped structure, the island has cliffs on the south side and low-lying shores on the north side.

title: Spreepark
fact: Spreepark is a former amusement park in the north of the Plänterwald in the Berlin district Treptow-Köpenick. It was also known by its earlier name Kulturpark Plänterwald Berlin.

title: St Kilda, Scotland
fact: St Kilda is a remote archipelago situated 35 nautical miles (65 kilometres) west-northwest of North Uist in the North Atlantic Ocean. It contains the westernmost islands of the Outer Hebrides of Scotland.

title: Stanley, Falkland Islands
fact: Stanley is the capital city of the Falkland Islands. It is located on the island of East Falkland, on a north-facing slope in one of the wettest parts of the islands.

title: Supai, Arizona
fact: Supai (Havasupai: Havasuuw) is a census-designated place (CDP) in Coconino County, Arizona, United States, within the Grand Canyon on the valley floor. As of the 2010 census, the CDP had a population of 208.

title: Taumatawhakatangi­hangakoauauotamatea­turipukakapikimaunga­horonukupokaiwhen­uakitanatahu
fact: Taumata­whakatangihanga­koauau­o­tamatea­turi­pukaka­piki­maunga­horo­nuku­pokai­whenua­ki­tana­tahu is a hill near Pōrangahau, south of Waipukurau, in southern Hawke's Bay, New Zealand. The summit of the hill is 305 metres (1,001 ft) above sea level.

title: Thurmond, West Virginia
fact: Thurmond is a town in Fayette County, West Virginia, United States, on the New River. The population was recorded as 5 in the 2020 census.

title: Tiksi
fact: Tiksi is an urban locality (an urban-type settlement) and the administrative center of Bulunsky District in the Sakha Republic, Russia, located on the shore of the Buor-Khaya Gulf of the Laptev Sea, southeast of the delta of the Lena River.

title: Times Beach, Missouri
fact: Times Beach is a ghost town in St. Louis County, Missouri, United States, 17 miles (27 km) southwest of St. Louis and 2 miles (3 km) east of Eureka.

title: Toad Suck, Arkansas
fact: Toad Suck is an unincorporated community in Perry County, Arkansas, United States. It is the location of (or is the nearest community to) Bigelow Rosenwald School, which is located at the junction of Arkansas Highway 60 and Bethel AME Road and is listed on the National Register…

title: Tortel
fact: Tortel is a Chilean commune located at the outflow of the Baker River and Pascua River to the Pacific Ocean. It lies between the Northern and Southern Patagonian Ice Field in the Capitán Prat Province in the Aysén Region.

title: Tristan da Cunha
fact: Tristan da Cunha, colloquially known as Tristan, is a remote group of volcanic islands in the South Atlantic Ocean. It is one of three constituent parts of the British Overseas Territory of Saint Helena, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha, with its own constitution.

title: Truth or Consequences, New Mexico
fact: Truth or Consequences (commonly T or C; founded as Hot Springs) is a city in the U.S. state of New Mexico, and the county seat of Sierra County. In 2020, the population was 6,052. The city is historically defined and economically shaped by local geothermal hot springs.
story_label: Wikipedia: Truth or Consequences, New Mexico

title: Tuktoyaktuk
fact: Tuktoyaktuk is an Inuvialuit hamlet near the Mackenzie River delta in the Inuvik Region of the Northwest Territories, Canada, at the northern terminus of the Inuvik–Tuktoyaktuk Highway.

title: Tyneham
fact: Tyneham is a ghost village abandoned in 1943 and former civil parish, now in the parish of Steeple with Tyneham, in the Dorset district, in the south of Dorset, England, near Lulworth on the Isle of Purbeck. In 2001 the civil parish had a population of 0.

title: Ushuaia
fact: Ushuaia is the capital of Tierra del Fuego, Antártida e Islas del Atlántico Sur Province, Argentina. With a population of 89,606 and a location below the 54th parallel south latitude, Ushuaia claims the title of world's southernmost city.

title: Utqiagvik, Alaska
fact: Utqiaġvik, formerly known as Barrow, is the borough seat and largest city of the North Slope Borough in the U.S. state of Alaska.

title: Varosha, Famagusta
fact: Varosha is the southern quarter of Famagusta, a de jure territory of Cyprus, currently under the control of Northern Cyprus. Varosha had a population of 226 in the 2011 Northern Cyprus census. The area of Varosha is 6.19 km2 (2.39 sq mi).

title: Verkhoyansk
fact: Verkhoyansk is a town in Verkhoyansky District of the Sakha Republic, Russia, located on the Yana River in the Arctic Circle, 92 kilometers (57 mi) from Batagay, the administrative center of the district, and 675 kilometers (419 mi) north of Yakutsk…

title: Vilarinho da Furna
fact: Vilarinho da Furna (alternately called Vilarinho das Furnas) was a former village, located in the civil parish of Campo de Gerês, in the municipality of Terras de Bouro, in the northern Portuguese district of Braga.

title: Villa Epecuén
fact: Villa Epecuén is an abandoned tourist village in Buenos Aires Province, Argentina, on the eastern shore of Laguna Epecuén, about 7 kilometres (4.3 mi) north of the city of Carhué.

title: Villa O'Higgins
fact: Villa O'Higgins is a small town in the Aysén Region of southern Chile, located 220 km south of Cochrane and 550 km south of Coyhaique.

title: Villa Puerto Edén
fact: Villa Puerto Edén is a Chilean hamlet and minor port located in Wellington Island, in Natales commune, Última Esperanza Province, Magallanes Region. It is considered one of Chile's most isolated inhabited places together with Easter Island and Villa Las Estrellas.

title: Why, Arizona
fact: Why is an unincorporated rural community in Pima County, Arizona, United States. It lies near the western border of the Tohono Oʼodham Indian Reservation and due north of Organ Pipe Cactus National Monument in Southern Arizona.

title: Wittenoom, Western Australia
fact: Wittenoom is a former mining town and a declared contaminated site, 1,420 kilometres (880 mi) north-north-east of Perth, in the Hamersley Range in the Pilbara region of Western Australia.

title: Y (commune)
fact: Y is a commune in the Somme department in Hauts-de-France in northern France. Y bears the shortest place name in France, and one of the shortest in the world.

title: Zzyzx, California
fact: Zzyzx ( ZY-ziks), formerly Soda Springs, is an unincorporated area in San Bernardino County, California, United States, within the boundaries of the Mojave National Preserve, managed by the National Park Service (NPS), an agency of the U.S. Department of Interior, as public land.

title: La Güera
fact: La Güera is a ghost town on the Atlantic coast at the southern tip of Western Sahara, on the western side of the Ras Nouadhibou peninsula which is split in two by the Mauritania–Western Sahara border, 15 kilometres (9.3 mi) west of Nouadhibou.

title: Oatman, Arizona
fact: Oatman is a census-designated place (CDP) in the Black Mountains of Mohave County, Arizona, United States, at an elevation of 2,710 feet (830 m).

title: Yukhari Askipara
fact: Yukhari Askipara, also known as Verin Voskepar, is an abandoned village in an exclave of the Gazakh District of Azerbaijan.

title: Chinese Camp, California
fact: Chinese Camp is a census-designated place (CDP) in Tuolumne County, California, United States. The population was 90 at the 2020 census, down from 126 at the 2010 census, which was down from 146 at the 2000 census.

title: Darwin, California
fact: Darwin is an unincorporated former mining community in Inyo County, California, United States. It is located 22 miles (35 km) southeast of Keeler. For statistical purposes, the United States Census Bureau has defined Darwin as a census-designated place (CDP).

title: Bayport, Florida
fact: Bayport is an unincorporated community and census-designated place (CDP) in Hernando County, Florida, United States. As of the 2020 census, Bayport had a population of 45.

title: Tuleta, Texas
fact: Tuleta is a census-designated place (CDP) in Bee County, Texas, United States. The population was 231 at the 2020 census.

title: Keeler, California
fact: Keeler, formerly known as Hawley, is an unincorporated community in Inyo County, California, United States. Keeler is located on the east shore of Owens Lake 11.5 miles (19 km) south-southeast of New York Butte.

title: Laupāhoehoe, Hawaii
fact: Laupāhoehoe is a census-designated place (CDP) in Hawaiʻi County, Hawaii, United States, in the District of North Hilo. The population was 581 at the 2010 census, up from 473 at the 2000 census.

title: Tehuacana, Texas
fact: Tehuacana is a town near the Tehuacana Hills in Limestone County, Texas, United States. The population was 228 at the 2020 census. From 1869 until 1902, the town was home to Trinity University.

title: Cayuga, Oklahoma
fact: Cayuga, originally known as Cayuga Springs, is an unincorporated community and census-designated place (CDP) in Delaware County, Oklahoma, United States.

title: Pyote, Texas
fact: Pyote ( PY-oht) is a town in Ward County, Texas, United States. Its population was 72 at the 2020 census.

title: Shasta, California
fact: Shasta is a census-designated place (CDP) in Shasta County, California, United States. Shasta sits at an elevation of 843 feet (257 m). Its population is 1,043 as of the 2020 census, down from 1,771 from the 2010 census.

title: Eola, Oregon
fact: Eola is an unincorporated community in Polk County, Oregon, United States. It lies four miles west of Salem on Oregon Route 22 at the confluence of Rickreall Creek and the Willamette River.

title: Verulamium
fact: Verulamium was a town in Roman Britain. It was sited southwest of the modern city of St Albans in Hertfordshire, England. The major ancient Roman route Watling Street passed through the city, but was realigned in medieval times to bring trade to St Albans.

title: Cardin, Oklahoma
fact: Cardin is a ghost town in Ottawa County, Oklahoma, United States. The population was 150 at the 2000 census, but declined all the way to a population of 3 at the 2010 census in April 2010. By November 2010, the population of the town was listed as zero.

title: Treece, Kansas
fact: Treece is a ghost town in Cherokee County, Kansas, United States, and part of the historic Tri-State Mining District. As of the 2010 census, the city population was 138.

title: Chisana, Alaska
fact: Chisana (also Shushanna) (Tsetsaan' Na in Ahtna) is a census-designated place (CDP) in the Copper River Census Area in the U.S. state of Alaska. As of the 2020 census, Chisana had a population of 0.

title: Terlingua, Texas
fact: Terlingua is a mining district and census-designated place (CDP) in southwestern Brewster County, Texas, United States. It is located near the Rio Grande and the villages of Lajitas and Study Butte, Texas, as well as the Mexican state of Chihuahua.

title: White Hills, Arizona
fact: White Hills is an unincorporated community and census-designated place (CDP) in Mohave County, Arizona, United States. It is 12.5 miles (20.1 km) northwest of Dolan Springs. As of the 2020 census, White Hills had a population of 345.

title: Avard, Oklahoma
fact: Avard is a current settlement and former incorporated town located in Woods County, Oklahoma, United States. It is southwest of Alva, and northeast of Waynoka. As of the 2020 census, the community had 11 residents. After initial growth, Avard began declining in the 1930s.

title: Hackberry, Arizona
fact: Hackberry is an unincorporated community and census-designated place (CDP) in Mohave County, Arizona, United States. It is located on State Route 66 (former U.S. Route 66), 28 miles (45 km) northeast of Kingman.

title: Hanford, Washington
fact: Hanford was a small agricultural community in Benton County, Washington, United States. It and White Bluffs were depopulated in 1943 in order to make room for the nuclear production facility known as the Hanford Site.

title: Nuugaatsiaq
fact: Nuugaatsiaq is a now abandoned settlement in the Avannaata municipality, in northwestern Greenland, located on an island off the southern coast of Sigguup Nunaa peninsula, in the Uummannaq Fjord basin.

title: Table Rock, Wyoming
fact: Table Rock is a ghost town in Sweetwater County, Wyoming, United States. The former town is part of a census-designated place. In the 2000 census, it had a population of 82, but the 2010 census reported a population of 0.

title: Amboy, California
fact: Amboy is an unincorporated community in San Bernardino County, in California's Mojave Desert, west of Needles and east of Ludlow on historic Route 66. It is roughly 60 miles (97 km) northeast of Twentynine Palms.

title: Forest City, Johor
fact: Forest City is an integrated property development and special financial zone (SFZ) in Iskandar Puteri, Johor, Malaysia. It is located on reclaimed land in the southwestern part of Johor Bahru District, the second largest district in Malaysia by population.

title: Washington-on-the-Brazos, Texas
fact: Washington-on-the-Brazos, also known simply as Washington, is an unincorporated community along the Brazos River in Washington County, Texas, United States.

title: Elkhorn, Montana
fact: Elkhorn is a census-designated place (CDP) in Jefferson County, Montana, United States, in the Elkhorn Mountains of the southwestern part of the state. It was originally established as a mining town in the 19th century. As of the 2020 census, Elkhorn had a population of 12.

title: Loring, Alaska
fact: Loring was established in 1885 with the first post office in the District of Alaska and is a census-designated place (CDP) in Ketchikan Gateway Borough in the U.S. state of Alaska.

title: Marysville, Montana
fact: Marysville is an unincorporated community and census-designated place (CDP) in Lewis and Clark County, Montana, United States. As of the 2020 census, Marysville had a population of 82. Elevation is 5,413 ft (1,650 m).

title: White Bluffs, Washington
fact: White Bluffs was an agricultural town in Benton County, Washington, United States. It was depopulated in 1943 along with the town of Hanford to make room for the nuclear production facility known as the Hanford Site.

title: Bağanıs Ayrım
fact: Bağanıs Ayrım is an abandoned village in the Qazakh District of Azerbaijan. The village was controlled by Armenia from the First Nagorno-Karabakh War in the early 1990s until 2024, when Armenia agreed to return the village to Azerbaijan.

title: Ludlow, Colorado
fact: Ludlow is a ghost town in Las Animas County, Colorado, United States. It was the site of the Ludlow Massacre–part of the Colorado Coalfield War–in 1914. The town site is located at the entrance to a canyon in the foothills of the Sangre de Cristo Mountains.

title: Qullissat
fact: Qullissat (old spelling: Qutdligssat) is a former settlement in the Qeqertalik municipality, located on the northeast coast of Disko Island on the west coast of Greenland. It was a coal mining town founded to exploit the natural resources of Disko Island.

title: Riverton, Washington
fact: Riverton is a census-designated place (CDP) in King County, Washington, United States. The population was 6,407 at the 2010 census. Riverton was formerly part of the Riverton-Boulevard Park CDP, which was split up for the 2010 census into Riverton and Boulevard Park.

title: Al Madam
fact: Al Madam is an inland town of the Emirate of Sharjah, in the United Arab Emirates. Located at the intersection of the Dubai-Hatta (E44) and Mleiha-Shwaib (E55) roads, its development has mainly centred around these road links and the road traffic through Hatta to Oman.

title: Dyea, Alaska
fact: Dyea ( dye-EE) is a ghost town in the U.S. state of Alaska. A few people live on individual small homesteads in the valley; however, it is largely abandoned.

title: Littleport, Iowa
fact: Littleport is an unincorporated community and former city in Clayton County, Iowa, United States. After the Volga River flood of May 16, 1999, much of the town was destroyed and most residents moved away. At the 2000 Census, there were 26 residents.

title: Poliochne
fact: Poliochne, often cited under its modern name Poliochni, was an ancient settlement on the east coast of the island of Lemnos.

title: Pony, Montana
fact: Pony is an unincorporated community and census-designated place in northeastern Madison County, Montana, United States, on the eastern edge of the Tobacco Root Mountains. As of the 2020 census, it had a population of 127.

title: Sexton, Iowa
fact: Sexton is an unincorporated community and census-designated place in Irvington Township, Kossuth County, Iowa, United States. It is located at the intersection of U.S. Route 18 and Kossuth CR P60. As of the 2020 census it had a population of 46.

title: Thistle, Utah
fact: Thistle is a ghost town in Spanish Fork Canyon in southeastern Utah County, Utah, United States. During the era of steam locomotives, the town's primary industry was servicing trains for the Denver and Rio Grande Western Railroad (often shortened to D&RG, D&RGW, or Rio Grande).

title: Brewster, Florida
fact: Brewster is a ghost town in southwest Polk County, Florida, United States, ten miles south of Mulberry. It is at an elevation of 143 ft (44 m) above sea level and has been uninhabited since the early 1960s. The population is 3, according to the 2010 Census.

title: Gantts Quarry, Alabama
fact: Gantts Quarry is a quarry and ghost town in Talladega County, Alabama, United States. The population was zero at the 2000, 2010, and 2020 censuses, although it had seven residents as late as the 1998 population estimate.

title: Luckenbach, Texas
fact: Luckenbach ( LOO-kin-bahk) is an unincorporated town 13 miles (19 km) from Fredericksburg in southeastern Gillespie County, Texas, United States.

title: Cook, South Australia
fact: Cook is a former railway town in South Australia. It is 824 kilometres (512 miles) by rail from Port Augusta, 863 kilometres (536 miles) by rail from Kalgoorlie, and about 100 kilometres (62 mi) north of the Eyre Highway via an unsealed road.

title: Far West, Missouri
fact: Far West was a settlement of the Latter Day Saint movement in Caldwell County, Missouri, United States, during the late 1830s. It is recognized as a historic site by the U.S. National Register of Historic Places, added to the register in 1970.

title: Flora, Oregon
fact: Flora is an unincorporated community in Wallowa County, Oregon, United States. It is located about 35 miles north of Enterprise, just off Oregon Route 3, and is considered a ghost town. Its elevation is 4350 ft. The community includes 6 mines.

title: Glenrio, New Mexico and Texas
fact: Glenrio, formerly Rock Island, is an unincorporated community in both Deaf Smith County, Texas, and Quay County, New Mexico, United States. Located on the former U.S. Route 66, the ghost town sits on the Texas–New Mexico state line.
story_label: Wikipedia: Glenrio, New Mexico and Texas

title: Mezaine
fact: Mežaine, officially Military training area Mežaine, is a Latvian National Armed Forces military training area of the 4th Brigade of the Latvian National Guard in Raņķi Parish, Kuldīga Municipality near the town of Skrunda.

title: Palisade, Nevada
fact: Palisade (originally called Palisades) is located in Eureka County in the northeastern section of the state of Nevada, in the western United States. It is about 10 miles (16 km) south of Carlin, and about 33 miles (53 km) southwest of Elko.

title: Pithole, Pennsylvania
fact: Pithole, or Pithole City, is a ghost town in Cornplanter Township, Venango County, Pennsylvania, United States, about 6 miles (9.7 km) from Oil Creek State Park and the Drake Well Museum, the site of the first commercial oil well in the United States.

title: Praha, Texas
fact: Praha is an unincorporated community located in Fayette County, Texas, United States. The community was sometimes called "Maticka Praha," which means in Czech "Mother Prague." The city is called the "Czech capital of Texas".

title: Aurora, Nevada
fact: Aurora is a ghost town in Mineral County in the west central part of the US state of Nevada, approximately 22 mi (35 km) southwest of the town of Hawthorne, three miles from the California border. Today the townsite is much diminished, having been damaged by vandals.

title: Barkerville
fact: Barkerville was the main town of the Cariboo Gold Rush in British Columbia, Canada, and is preserved as a historic town. It is located on the north slope of the Cariboo Plateau near the Cariboo Mountains 80 kilometres (50 mi) east of Quesnel.

title: Bingham Canyon, Utah
fact: Bingham Canyon was a city formerly located in southwestern Salt Lake County, Utah, United States, in a narrow canyon on the eastern face of the Oquirrh Mountains.

title: Climax, Colorado
fact: Climax is an extinct mining company town, railroad station, and post office located in Lake County, Colorado, United States. The town site is located at an elevation of 11,341 feet (3,457 m) at Fremont Pass on the Continental Divide of the Americas.

title: Crystal Springs, Nevada
fact: Crystal Springs is a ghost town in the Pahranagat Valley region of Lincoln County, Nevada in the United States. The ghost town is located at the junction of State Route 318 and State Route 375 (Extraterrestrial Highway), just northwest of U.S. Route 93.

title: Elcor, Minnesota
fact: Elcor is a ghost town, or more properly, an extinct town, in the U.S. state of Minnesota that was inhabited between 1897 and 1956. It was built on the Mesabi Iron Range near the city of Gilbert in St. Louis County.

title: Hyampolis
fact: Hyampolis was a city in ancient Phocis, Greece. A native of this city was called a Hyampolites. Some ancient authors record that the city was also called simply Hya.

title: Ingalls, Oklahoma
fact: Ingalls is a census-designated place (CDP) in eastern Payne County, Oklahoma, about 9 miles (14 km) east of Stillwater. As of the 2020 census, Ingalls had a population of 192.

title: Lida, Nevada
fact: Lida, Nevada is a small ghost town in Esmeralda County, Nevada, near the border with California. The GNIS classifies it as a populated place. It is located on State Route 266, north of Magruder Mountain. The first white settlers at Lida arrived in 1867.

title: Ludlow, California
fact: Ludlow is an unincorporated community in the Mojave Desert on Interstate 40, located in San Bernardino County, California, United States. The older remains of the ghost town are along historic Route 66.

title: Reimerswaal (city)
fact: Reimerswaal is a lost city in the Netherlands. The present-day municipality of Reimerswaal is named after this city, which was granted city rights in 1374. The city was destroyed by repeated floods, and the last citizens left in 1632. Nothing remains.

title: Unionville, Nevada
fact: Unionville is a census-designated place in Pershing County, Nevada, located south of Interstate 80 and just west of State Route 400 on Unionville Road, with the population as of the 2020 census being 27.

title: Ballarat, California
