fact: Dam, completed 1966. The Roseires Dam is a dam on the Blue Nile at Ad Damazin, just upstream of the town of Er Roseires, in Sudan. It consists of a concrete buttress dam 1 km wide with a maximum height of 68 m, and an earth dam on either side.

title: Rubjerg Knude Lighthouse
fact: Lighthouse, first lit 1899. Rubjerg Knude Lighthouse is on the coast of the North Sea in Rubjerg, in the Jutland municipality of Hjørring in northern Denmark. It was first lit on 27 December 1900. Construction of the lighthouse began in 1899.

title: San Juan National Historic Site
fact: Fortress, built 1949. San Juan National Historic Site in the Old San Juan section of San Juan, Puerto Rico, is a National Park Service-managed historic site which preserves and interprets the Spanish colonial-era fortification system of the city of San Juan…
story_label: Wikipedia: San Juan National Historic Site

title: Sanjō Ōhashi
fact: Bridge, 74 m long, opened 1950. Sanjō Ōhashi (三条大橋) is a bridge in Kyoto, Kyoto Prefecture, Japan. It spans the Kamo River as part of Sanjō-dōri.

title: Spaç Prison
fact: Prison, opened 1968. The Spaç Prison was a political prison in Communist Albania at the village of Spaç. The former prison is listed as a second-category national monument.

title: Trepça Mines
fact: Mine, opened 1930. The Trepça Mines is a large industrial complex in Kosovo, located 9 km (5.6 mi) northeast of Mitrovica.

title: Vladimir Central Prison
fact: Prison, opened 1783. Vladimir Prison, popularly known as Vladimir Central, is a prison in Vladimir, Russia. It is the second-largest prison in Russia, with a capacity of 1,220 detainees, and is operated by the Federal Penitentiary Service as a maximum-security prison with most…

title: Arroyito Dam
fact: The Arroyito Dam is the fifth of five dams on the Limay River in northwestern Argentine Patagonia (the Comahue region), at 315 metres (1,033 ft) above mean sea level. It was inaugurated in 1979. The dam is made of compacted loose materials.

title: Bar Aqueduct
fact: Aqueduct, 3 km long. The Bar Aqueduct is a stone aqueduct located on the northern side of Stari Bar Fortress, 4 km north of the town of Bar in Montenegro.

title: Macagua Dam
fact: Dam, completed 1997. The Macagua Dam, officially known as Antonio José de Sucre, is an embankment dam with concrete gravity sections on the Caroní River in Ciudad Guayana, Bolívar State, Venezuela.

title: Taabo Dam
fact: Dam, completed 1975. The Taabo Dam is a hydroelectric power plant of the Bandama River in Côte d'Ivoire with a power generating capacity of 210 megawatts (280,000 hp), enough to power over 141,000 homes. It was formed in 1975. This dam is located downstream from Kossou Dam.

title: Adziogol Lighthouse
fact: Lighthouse, 64 m tall, first lit 1911. The Adziogol Lighthouse, also known as Stanislav–Adzhyhol Lighthouse or Stanislav Range Rear light, is one of two vertical lattice hyperboloid structures of steel bars, serving as active lighthouses in Dnieper Estuary, Ukraine.

title: Ajloun Castle
fact: Fortress, built 1184. Ajloun Castle, medieval name Qalʻat ar-Rabad, is a 12th-century Muslim castle situated in northwestern Jordan. It is placed on a hilltop in the Mount Ajloun district, also known as Jabal Auf after an Arab tribe that lived in the area in the 12th century.

title: Alcázar de Colón
fact: Fortress, built 1511. The Alcázar de Colón is the first fortified European palace built in the Americas. Located in the colonial area of Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic, it forms part of the Ciudad Colonial, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

title: Chagres and Fort San Lorenzo
fact: Fortress, built 1590. Chagres, once the chief Atlantic port on the isthmus of Panama, is now an abandoned village at the historical site of Fort San Lorenzo.
story_label: Wikipedia: Chagres and Fort San Lorenzo

title: Dez Dam
fact: The Dez Dam, formerly known as Mohammad-Reza Shah Pahlavi Dam, before the 1979 Revolution, is an arch dam on the Dez River in the southwestern province of Khuzsetan.

title: Galle Fort
fact: Galle Fort, in the Bay of Galle on the southwest coast of Sri Lanka, was built first in 1588 by the Portuguese, then extensively fortified by the Dutch during the 17th century from 1649 onwards.

title: Het Steen
fact: Prison, opened 1200. Het Steen is a medieval fortress in the old city centre of Antwerp, Belgium, one of Europe's biggest ports.

title: Kainji Dam
fact: Dam, completed 1968. Kainji Dam is a dam across the Niger River in Niger State of Central Nigeria. Construction of the dam by Impregilo began in 1964 and was completed in 1968.

title: La Navidad
fact: La Navidad ("The Nativity", i.e. Christmas) was a Spanish fort that Christopher Columbus and his crew built on the northwest coast of Hispaniola…

title: Saint Mark's Coptic Orthodox Cathedral (Alexandria)
fact: Saint Mark's Coptic Orthodox Cathedral is a Coptic church in Alexandria, Egypt. It is the historical seat of the Pope of Alexandria, the head of the Coptic Orthodox Church.
story_label: Wikipedia: Saint Mark's Coptic Orthodox Cathedral (Alexandria)

title: Sõrve Lighthouse
fact: Lighthouse, 52 m tall, first lit 1646. Sõrve Lighthouse is a lighthouse located in Saaremaa Parish, on the island of Saaremaa, in Estonia.

title: Sup'ung Dam
fact: Dam, completed 1943. The Sup'ung Dam, also referred to as the Shuifeng Dam and originally the Suihō Dam, is a gravity dam on the Yalu River between Kuandian Manchu Autonomous County, Liaoning Province in China and Sakju County, North Pyongan Province in North Korea.

title: Thridrangaviti Lighthouse
fact: Þrídrangaviti Lighthouse is an active lighthouse 7.2 kilometres (4.5 miles) off the southwest coast of Iceland, in the archipelago of Vestmannaeyjar.

title: Volga Hydroelectric Station
fact: Dam, completed 1958. The Volga Hydroelectric Station or Volga GES also known as the 22nd Congress of the CPSU Stalingrad/Volgograd Hydroelectric Power Station, is the largest hydroelectric station in Europe, and the last of the Volga-Kama Cascade of dams…

title: Westerheversand Lighthouse
fact: Lighthouse, 40 m tall, first lit 1907. The Westerheversand Lighthouse is located in Westerhever, Schleswig-Holstein, Germany. Considered to be one of the best-known lighthouses in northern Germany, it was built in 1908. Its cast iron tower is 40 metres (130 ft) high.

title: Almatti Dam
fact: Dam, 49 m tall. The Lal Bahadur Shastri Dam is also known as Almatti Dam is a hydroelectric project on the Krishna River in North Karnataka, India which was completed in July 2005. The target annual electric output of the dam is 560 MU (or GWh).

title: Birecik Dam
fact: Dam, completed 2000. The Birecik Dam, one of the 21 dams of the Southeastern Anatolia Project of Turkey, is located on the Euphrates River 60 km (37 mi) downstream of Atatürk Dam and 8 km (5.0 mi) upstream of Birecik town 80 km (50 mi) west of Province of Şanlıurfa in the…

title: Jatiluhur Dam
fact: Dam, completed 1957. The Jatiluhur Dam is a multi-purpose embankment dam on the Citarum River in West Java, Indonesia. It is located 70 km (43 mi) east of Jakarta, close to the medium-sized town of Purwakarta.

title: Tungabhadra Dam
fact: Dam, 49 m tall. The Tungabhadra Dam, also known as Pampa Sagar, is a water reservoir constructed across the Tungabhadra River in the Hosapete-Koppal confluence in Karnataka, India.

title: Bell Rock Lighthouse
fact: Lighthouse, 36 m tall, first lit 1810. The Bell Rock Lighthouse, off the coast of Angus, Scotland, is the world's oldest surviving sea-washed lighthouse.

title: Bengtskär Lighthouse
fact: Lighthouse, 46 m tall, first lit 1906. Bengtskär Lighthouse is located in the Archipelago Sea about 25 kilometers south west of Hanko, Finland. It rises 52 meters above sea level and is the highest lighthouse in the Nordic countries.

title: Ismaïlia Canal
fact: Ismailia Canal or the Al-Ismāʿīliyyah Canal, formerly known as the Sweet Water Canal or the Fresh Water Canal, is a canal which was dug by thousands of Egyptian fellahin to facilitate the construction of the Suez Canal. The canal travels east-west across Ismailia Governorate.

title: Naica Mine
fact: The Naica Mine of the Mexican state of Chihuahua, is a lead, zinc and silver mine. Located in Naica in the municipality of Saucillo, the Naica Mine is owned by Industrias Peñoles, the world's largest silver producer.

title: National Redoubt (Switzerland)
fact: The Swiss National Redoubt is a defensive plan developed by the Swiss government beginning in the 1880s to respond to foreign invasion. In the opening years of the Second World War the plan was expanded and refined to deal with a potential German invasion.

title: Operation Gold
fact: Operation Gold was a joint operation conducted by the American Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) and the British MI6 Secret Intelligence Service (SIS) in the 1950s to tap into landline communication of the Soviet Army headquarters in Berlin using a tunnel into the…

title: Salt Cathedral of Zipaquirá
fact: Mine, opened 1995. The Salt Cathedral of Zipaquirá is an underground Roman Catholic church built within the tunnels of a salt mine 200 metres (660 ft) underground in a halite mountain near the city of Zipaquirá, in Cundinamarca, Colombia.

title: Central Arizona Project
fact: Aqueduct, built 1993. The Central Arizona Project (CAP) is a 336 mi (541 km) diversion canal in Arizona in the Western United States.

title: Abashiri Prison
fact: Abashiri Prison is a prison in Abashiri, Hokkaido that opened in 1890. The northernmost prison in Japan, it is located near the Abashiri River and east of Mount Tento. It holds inmates with sentences of less than ten years.

title: Abu Salim prison
fact: Abu Salim prison is a maximum security prison in Tripoli, Libya. The prison was notorious during the rule of Muammar Gaddafi for alleged mistreatment and human rights abuses, including a massacre in 1996 in which Human Rights Watch estimated that 1,270 prisoners were killed.

title: Big Dig
fact: Tunnel, opened 2002. The Big Dig was a megaproject in Boston that rerouted the elevated Central Artery of Interstate 93 into the O'Neill Tunnel and built the Ted Williams Tunnel to extend Interstate 90 to Logan International Airport.

title: Bois du Cazier
fact: Mine, opened 1822. The Bois du Cazier was a coal mine in what was then the town of Marcinelle, near Charleroi, in Belgium which today is preserved as an industrial heritage site.

title: Carandiru Penitentiary
fact: Prison, opened 1920. Carandiru Penitentiary, officially São Paulo House of Detention was a penitentiary located in the North Zone of São Paulo, Brazil. It was inaugurated on April 21, 1920 and was built by the engineer-architect Samuel das Neves.

title: Euphrates Tunnel
fact: Tunnel, 929 m long. The Euphrates Tunnel was a legendary tunnel purportedly built under the river Euphrates to connect the two halves of the city of Babylon in Mesopotamia. The first tunnel known definitively to have been built underwater was the Thames Tunnel, completed in 1841.

title: Garuda Wisnu Kencana statue
fact: Statue, 75 m tall, unveiled 2018. Garuda Wisnu Kencana statue is a 121-meter-tall statue located in Garuda Wisnu Kencana Cultural Park, Bali, Indonesia. It was designed by Nyoman Nuarta and inaugurated in September 2018.

title: La Catedral
fact: Prison, opened 1991. La Catedral was a personal prison overlooking the city of Medellín, in Colombia. The prison was built to specifications ordered by Medellín Cartel leader Pablo Escobar…

title: La Vieille
fact: Lighthouse, 27 m tall, first lit 1882. La Vieille is a lighthouse in the département of Finistère at the commune of Plogoff, on the northwest coast of France.

title: Qincheng Prison
fact: Prison, opened 1960. The Ministry of Public Security Qincheng Prison is a maximum-security prison located in Qincheng Village, Xingshou, Changping District, Beijing in the People's Republic of China.

title: Sado mine
fact: The Sado gold mine is a generic term for gold and silver mines which were once located on the island of Sado in Niigata Prefecture, Japan. Among these mines, the Aikawa Gold and Silver Mine was the largest and was in operation until the modern era.

title: Chipiona Lighthouse
fact: Lighthouse, 62 m tall, first lit 1867. Chipiona Lighthouse, also known as Punta del Perro Light, is an active 19th-century lighthouse in Chipiona, in the province of Cádiz, Spain.

title: Les Eclaireurs Lighthouse
fact: Lighthouse, 11 m tall, first lit 1920. Les Eclaireurs Lighthouse is a slightly conical lighthouse standing on the northeasternmost island of the five or more Les Eclaireurs islands, which it takes its name from, 5 nautical miles (9 km) east of Ushuaia in the Beagle Channel…

title: Saalfeld Fairy Grottoes
fact: The Saalfeld Fairy Grottoes are caverns or grottoes of a former mine near Saalfeld, in the German state of Thuringia. They have long been famous for their countless colorful mineral formations (speleothems) formed over many years by water dripping through relatively soft rock.

title: Shabla Lighthouse
fact: Lighthouse, first lit 1857. The Shabla Lighthouse is a lighthouse located 5 kilometres east of the town of Shabla, Dobrich Province; in Bulgaria. The lighthouse was built in 1856 by the Ottoman Empire and is the oldest lighthouse in Bulgaria.

title: Berkeley Pit
fact: The Berkeley Pit is a former open pit copper mine in the western United States, located in Butte, Montana. It is one mile (1.6 km) long by one-half mile (800 m) wide, with an approximate maximum depth of 1,780 feet (540 m).

title: Bulolo
fact: Mine, opened 1930. Bulolo is a town in Bulolo Urban LLG, Morobe Province, Papua New Guinea. It was once an important gold dredging centre in the former Territory of New Guinea, situated on the Bulolo River, a tributary of the Markham River, about 32 km (20 mi) north-west of Wau.

title: Flannan Isles Lighthouse
fact: Lighthouse, 23 m tall, first lit 1899. Flannan Isles Lighthouse is a lighthouse near the highest point on Eilean Mòr, one of the Flannan Isles in the Outer Hebrides off the west coast of Scotland. In 1900, its three keepers disappeared under mysterious circumstances.

title: Fremantle Prison
fact: Prison, opened 1855. Fremantle Prison, sometimes referred to as Fremantle Gaol or Fremantle Jail, is a former Australian prison and World Heritage Site in Fremantle, Western Australia. The site includes the prison cellblocks, gatehouse, perimeter walls, cottages, and tunnels.

title: Grand-Hornu
fact: Grand-Hornu is an old industrial coal mining complex and company town in Hornu (Boussu), near Mons, in Belgium. It was built by Henri De Gorge between 1810 and 1830. It is a unique example of functional town-planning.

title: Jwaneng diamond mine
fact: Mine, opened 1982. The Jwaneng diamond mine is the richest diamond mine in the world, and also the second largest in the world. It is nicknamed "the Prince of Mines", and is located in south-central Botswana about 170 kilometers (110 mi) southwest of the city of Gaborone.

title: Kamares Aqueduct
fact: Aqueduct, built 1750. Kamares Aqueduct, also known as the Bekir Pasha Aqueduct, is an aqueduct near Larnaca, Cyprus. Located just outside the city near the old road to Limassol, it was built between 1747 and 1750 and supplied Larnaca with fresh water for nearly two centuries.

title: Lindesnes Lighthouse
fact: Lighthouse, 16 m tall, first lit 1915. Lindesnes Lighthouse is a coastal lighthouse at the southernmost tip of Norway, about 10 kilometres (6.2 mi) southwest of the village of Høllen in Lindesnes Municipality in Agder county.

title: Los Angeles Aqueduct
fact: Aqueduct, built 1913. The Los Angeles Aqueduct system, comprising the Los Angeles Aqueduct (Owens Valley aqueduct) and the Second Los Angeles Aqueduct, is a water conveyance system…

title: Miike coal mine
fact: Mine, opened 1721. Miike coal mine, also known as the Mitsui Miike Coal Mine, was the largest coal mine in Japan, located in the area of the city of Ōmuta, Fukuoka and Arao, Kumamoto, Japan.

title: Slettnes Lighthouse
fact: Lighthouse, 39 m tall, first lit 1905. Slettnes Lighthouse is the northernmost mainland lighthouse on Earth. It is located in Gamvik Municipality in Finnmark county, Norway.

title: Sotk gold mine
fact: The Sotk gold mine, known in Azerbaijan as the Zod gold mine, is the largest mine in Armenia and Azerbaijan in terms of pure gold reserves.

title: Tchintabaraden
fact: Tchintabaraden (var. Tchin-Tabaraden, Tchin Tabaraden) is a town and commune located in the Azawagh area of Niger, in the north of the Tahoua Region. It is the capital of the region's Tchintabaraden Department. It is the market center for the Iwellemmedan Tuareg.

title: Ar Men
fact: Lighthouse, 37 m tall, first lit 1867. Ar Men ("the rock" in Breton) is a lighthouse at one end of the Chaussée de l'Île de Sein, at the west end of Brittany. It shares its name with the rock on which it was erected between 1867 and 1881. It has been a listed monument since 2017.

title: Fachi
fact: Fachi is an oasis surrounded by the Ténéré desert and the dunes of the Erg of Bilma in eastern Niger, placed on the western edge of the small Agram mountain outcropping. It has a population of 2,215 people (2012).

title: Hidirlik Tower
fact: Hıdırlık Tower is a landmark tower of tawny stone in Antalya, Turkey, where Kaleiçi meets Karaalioğlu Park.

title: Långe Jan
fact: Lighthouse, 42 m tall, first lit 1784. Långe Jan ("Tall John") is a Swedish lighthouse located at the south cape of Öland in the Baltic Sea, Sweden's second largest island.

title: Nosy Alañaña Light
fact: Lighthouse, first lit 1933. Nosy Alañaña Light, also known as Île aux Prunes Light, is an active lighthouse in Île aux Prunes, Toamasina Province, Madagascar.

title: Pascua Lama
fact: Pascua-Lama is an open pit mining project of gold, silver, copper and other minerals. Pascua Lama is located in the Andes mountains, in the southern reaches of Atacama Desert…

title: Premier Mine
fact: Mine, opened 1902. The Premier Mine is an underground diamond mine owned by Petra Diamonds in the town of Cullinan, 40 kilometres (25 mi) east of Pretoria, Gauteng Province, South Africa.

title: Puquios
fact: Puquios are ancient systems of subterranean aqueducts which allow water to be transported over long distances in hot dry climates without loss of much of the water to evaporation.

title: Rosario-Victoria Bridge
fact: Bridge, 610 m long, opened 2003. Rosario-Victoria Bridge is the informal name of the physical connection between the Argentine cities of Rosario (province of Santa Fe) and Victoria. This roadlink is composed of several bridges, viaducts and earth-filled sections.

title: Shinkolobwe
fact: Shinkolobwe, or Kasolo, or Chinkolobew, or Shainkolobwe, was a radium and uranium mine in the Haut-Katanga Province of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), located 20 km (12.4 mi) west of Likasi, 20 km (12.4 mi) south of Kambove…

title: Super Pit gold mine
fact: The Fimiston Open Pit, colloquially known as the Super Pit, is an open-pit mine in Western Australia. It was Australia's largest open cut gold mine until late 2015, when it was overtaken by the Newmont Boddington gold mine, also in Western Australia.

title: Tahkuna Lighthouse
fact: Lighthouse, 43 m tall, first lit 1875. Tahkuna Lighthouse is a lighthouse located in the Tahkuna Peninsula, Hiiu Parish, on the island of Hiiumaa, in Estonia.

title: Las Raíces Tunnel
fact: Tunnel, 4.5 km long, opened 1939. Las Raíces Tunnel is a road tunnel on Route 181 in the Araucanía Region of Chile, connecting the communes of Curacautín and Lonquimay through the Cordillera de Las Raíces in the upper Biobío River basin.

title: California Lighthouse
fact: Lighthouse, 30 m tall, first lit 1914. The California Lighthouse, known by locals as Faro stands tall on a limestone plateau at Hudishibana, near Arashi Beach and Sasariwichi dunes on the northwestern tip of Aruba. It holds the distinction of being the tallest structure in Aruba.

title: Cape Hatteras Lighthouse
fact: Lighthouse, 64 m tall. Cape Hatteras Light is a lighthouse located on Hatteras Island in the Outer Banks in the town of Buxton, North Carolina originally built in 1802 and relocated twice due to coastal erosion. It is part of the Cape Hatteras National Seashore.

title: Hercílio Luz Bridge
fact: Bridge, 821 m long, opened 1926. The Hercílio Luz Bridge, located in Florianópolis, the capital city of Santa Catarina State in southern Brazil, is the first bridge constructed to link the Island of Santa Catarina to the mainland. It is the longest suspension bridge in Brazil.

title: Kihnu Lighthouse
fact: Lighthouse, 28 m tall, first lit 1865. Kihnu Lighthouse is a lighthouse located in Kihnu, an island in the northern Gulf of Riga in Pärnu County, in Estonia. The lighthouse was prefabricated in England; and assembled in 1865.

title: Klaipėda Lighthouse
fact: Lighthouse, 40 m tall, first lit 1796. Klaipėda Lighthouse is a lighthouse located in Klaipėda, on the Lithuanian coast of the Baltic Sea; located 500 metres from the coast.

title: Långe Erik
fact: Lighthouse, 32 m tall. Långe Erik ("Tall Erik"), official name Ölands norra udde, is a Swedish lighthouse built in 1845 and located on a little island, Stora Grundet, in Grankullaviken bay at the north point of Öland, the second largest island in Sweden.

title: Pilsum Lighthouse
fact: Lighthouse, 11 m tall. Pilsum Lighthouse was built in 1891 as a sector light for the Ems‌hörn channel on Germany's North Sea coast. It is located on a dyke near the village of Pilsum in the municipality of Krummhörn. It guided ships through the narrow channel until 1915.

title: Pollsmoor Prison
fact: Prison, opened 1964. Pollsmoor Prison, officially known as Pollsmoor Maximum Security Prison, is located in the Cape Town suburb of Tokai in South Africa. Pollsmoor is a maximum security penal facility that continues to hold some of South Africa's most dangerous criminals.

title: Ristna Lighthouse
fact: Lighthouse, 30 m tall, first lit 1874. The Ristna Lighthouse is a lighthouse located at Ristna Point on the Kõpu Peninsula on the island of Hiiumaa (on the coast of the Baltic Sea) in Estonia.

title: Rodsher
fact: Rodsher, is an uninhabited small Russian island and a lighthouse, situated in the Gulf of Finland. It is located 16 kilometres (9 nmi) southwest of the island of Gogland and 24 kilometres (13 nmi) northeast of the Estonian island of Vaindloo.

title: Ruhnu Lighthouse
fact: Lighthouse, 40 m tall, first lit 1877. Ruhnu Lighthouse is a lighthouse located on the island of Ruhnu (in the Gulf of Riga), in Estonia.

title: Rumeli Feneri
fact: Lighthouse, 30 m tall, first lit 1830. Rumeli Feneri, also Türkeli Feneri, a historical lighthouse still in use, is located on the European side of the Bosporus Strait's Black Sea entrance in Istanbul.

title: Vorontsov Lighthouse
fact: Lighthouse, first lit 1888. The Vorontsov Lighthouse is a red-and-white, 27.2-metre-tall (89 ft) lighthouse in the Black Sea port of Odesa, Ukraine. It is named after Prince Mikhail Semyonovich Vorontsov, one of the governors-general of the Odesa region.

title: Wisłoujście Fortress
fact: Lighthouse, first lit 1482. Wisłoujście Fortress is a historic fortress located in Gdańsk by the Martwa Wisła river, by an old estuary of the river Vistula, flowing into the Bay of Gdańsk.

title: Ahırkapı Lighthouse
fact: Lighthouse, 28 m tall, first lit 1755. The Ahırkapı Feneri, a historical lighthouse still in use, is located at the southern Seraglio Point on the Rumelian coast of Bosporus' south entrance, in Ahırkapı neighborhood of Istanbul's Fatih district, Turkey.

title: Ardnamurchan Lighthouse
fact: Lighthouse, 35 m tall, first lit 1849. Ardnamurchan Lighthouse is a listed 19th century lighthouse, located on Ardnamurchan Point in Lochaber part of the Highland council area of Scotland.

title: Hel Lighthouse
fact: Lighthouse, first lit 1942. Hel Lighthouse is an active lighthouse in the town of Hel, Pomeranian Voivodeship in Poland. It is situated at the eastern tip of the Hel Peninsula and guides ship traffic into Gdańsk Bay and the Bay of Puck.

title: Kassuende Bridge
fact: Bridge, 715 m long, opened 2014. Kassuende Bridge is a bridge in Mozambique across the Zambezi River. It is about 6 kilometres (3.7 mi) downstream from the Samora Machel Bridge.

title: Kołobrzeg Lighthouse
fact: Lighthouse, first lit 1945. Kołobrzeg Lighthouse is a lighthouse in Kołobrzeg on the Polish coast of the Baltic Sea, located in Kołobrzeg (West Pomeranian Voivodeship), in north-west Poland.

title: Kullen Lighthouse
fact: Lighthouse, 15 m tall, first lit 1899. The Kullen Lighthouse is an operational lighthouse in Scania, located by the mouth of Öresund, at the point of Kullaberg peninsula, in Höganäs, on the south-west coast of Sweden.

title: Lizard Lighthouse
fact: Lighthouse, 19 m tall, first lit 1751. The Lizard Lighthouse (Cornish: Golowji Lysardh) is a lighthouse at Lizard Point, Cornwall, England, built to guide vessels passing through the English Channel.

title: Nida Lighthouse
fact: Lighthouse, 27 m tall, first lit 1945. Nida Lighthouse is located in Nida, on the Curonian Spit in between the Curonian Lagoon (to the east) and the Baltic Sea (to the west).

title: Nividic Lighthouse
fact: Lighthouse, 36 m tall, first lit 1936. Nividic Lighthouse (Phare de Nividic; Breton: Tour-tan Nividic) is one of five major lighthouses on Ushant in Brittany. The others are the Phare du Créac'h, the Stiff lighthouse (from Breton Stiv), Kéréon and La Jument.

title: Pakri Lighthouse
fact: Lighthouse, 52 m tall, first lit 1889. Pakri Lighthouse is a lighthouse located on the Pakri Peninsula (on the coast of the Baltic Sea), Harju County, in Estonia.

title: Pervalka Lighthouse
fact: Lighthouse, 14 m tall, first lit 1900. Pervalka Lighthouse - a lighthouse located in Pervalka on the Curonian Spit, located in between the Curonian Lagoon (to the east) and the Baltic Sea (to the west); located in Lithuania.

title: Port Said Lighthouse
fact: Lighthouse, 56 m tall, first lit 1869. Port Said Lighthouse is one of the most important architectural and tourist landmarks in the city of Port Said in Egypt.

title: Red Flag Canal
fact: The Red Flag Canal is an irrigation canal located 80 km (50 mi) northwest of Anyang in the northern extremity of Henan, China.

title: Roter Sand Lighthouse
fact: Lighthouse, 28 m tall, first lit 1885. Roter Sand is a lighthouse in the North Sea, in the Weser estuary. It entered service in 1885. The light was deactivated in 1986 but the tower still serves as a day beacon.

title: Skagen Lighthouse
fact: Lighthouse, 46 m tall, first lit 1848. Skagen Lighthouse, also known as Skagen's Grey Lighthouse (Det Grå Fyr), is an active lighthouse four kilometres (2+1⁄2 miles) northeast of Skagen in the far north of Jutland, Denmark.

title: Wadi el Kuf Bridge
fact: Bridge, 477 m long, opened 1971. Wadi el Kuf Bridge, is a bridge located 20 km west of Bayda, Libya. It is the second highest bridge in Africa. It was designed by Italian civil engineer Riccardo Morandi. Construction of the bridge began in 1965 and the bridge was opened in 1972.

title: Wignacourt Aqueduct
fact: Aqueduct, built 1610. The Wignacourt Aqueduct (Maltese: L-Akwedott ta' Wignacourt) is a 17th-century aqueduct in Malta, which was built by the Order of Saint John to carry water from springs in Dingli and Rabat to the newly built capital city Valletta.

title: Acqua Felice
fact: The Acqua Felice is one of the aqueducts of Rome, completed in 1586 by Pope Sixtus V, whose birth name, which he never fully abandoned, was Felice Peretti. The first new aqueduct of early modern Rome, its source is at the springs at Pantano Borghese, off Via Casilina.

title: Aloha Tower
fact: Lighthouse, 56 m tall, first lit 1926. The Aloha Tower is a retired lighthouse that is considered one of the landmarks of the state of Hawaii in the United States. Opened on September 11, 1926, at a cost of $160,000 ($2,805,206 in 2024), the tower is at Pier 9 of Honolulu Harbor.

title: California Aqueduct
fact: The Governor Edmund G. Brown California Aqueduct is a system of canals, tunnels, and pipelines that conveys water collected from the Sierra Nevada and valleys of Northern and Central California to Southern California.

title: Giordan Lighthouse
fact: Lighthouse, 22 m tall, first lit 1853. The Giordan, Ġordan is an active lighthouse on the Maltese island of Gozo. It is located on Ġurdan hill above the village of Għasri on the northern coast of the island.

title: Île Vierge
fact: Lighthouse, 83 m tall, first lit 1902. Île Vierge (Breton language: Enez-Werc'h) is a 6-hectare (15-acre) islet lying 1.5 kilometres (3⁄4 nautical mile) off the north-west coast of Brittany, opposite the village of Lilia.

title: Jerwan
fact: Jerwan is a locality north of Mosul in the Nineveh Province of Iraq. The site is clear of vegetation and is sparsely settled.

title: Punta Carena Lighthouse
fact: Lighthouse, 28 m tall, first lit 1867. Punta Carena Lighthouse is an active lighthouse, located on the island of Capri on the head of the same name, about 3 kilometres (1.9 mi) southwest of Anacapri. The lighthouse has been active since 1867; its construction began in 1862.

title: Roquefavour Aqueduct
fact: Aqueduct, 393 m long. The Roquefavour Aqueduct is an aqueduct in the commune of Ventabren, near Aix-en-Provence, Bouches-du-Rhône, France. The aqueduct was first planned in 1565, but it was not realized until the 19th century.

title: Tora Prison
fact: Prison, opened 1908. Tora Prison is an Egyptian prison complex for criminal and political detainees, located in Tora, Egypt. The complex is situated in front of the Tora El Balad metro station.

title: Tungenes Lighthouse
fact: Lighthouse, 12 m tall, first lit 1828. Tungenes Lighthouse is a coastal lighthouse located in Randaberg Municipality in Rogaland county, Norway.

title: Reiterdenkmal
fact: The Equestrian Monument, more commonly known under its German original name Reiterdenkmal and the name Südwester Reiter (Rider of South West), was a monument in Windhoek, the capital of Namibia. It was inaugurated on 27 January 1912, the birthday of German emperor Wilhelm II.

title: Serkadji Prison
fact: Prison, opened 1857. Serkadji Prison, formerly Barberousse Prison, was a high-security prison in Algiers, Algeria; in 1995, about two-thirds of the 1,500 prisoners detained are (or were) accused or convicted of terrorism.

title: Tamagawa Aqueduct
fact: The Tamagawa Aqueduct is a historic 43‑kilometre, gravity‑fed waterway constructed in 1653–54 under the Tokugawa shogunate to transport water from the Tama River into Edo.

title: Amoreira Aqueduct
fact: The Amoreira Aqueduct (Aqueduto da Amoreira) is a 16th-century aqueduct (begun in 1537) that spans the Portuguese municipality of Elvas, bringing water into the fortified seat.

title: Aqueduct of the Gier
fact: Aqueduct, built 100 CE. The Aqueduct of the Gier is an ancient Roman aqueduct probably constructed in the 1st century AD to provide water for Lugdunum (Lyon), in what is now eastern France.

title: Pegões Aqueduct
fact: The Convent of Christ Aqueduct, also known as the Pegões Aqueduct, was built to supply water to the Convent of Christ in Tomar from four different springs. It is approximately 6 km long.

title: Raúl Uranga – Carlos Sylvestre Begnis Subfluvial Tunnel
fact: Tunnel, opened 1969. The Raúl Uranga – Carlos Sylvestre Begnis Subfluvial Tunnel, formerly known as the Hernandarias Subfluvial Tunnel, is an underwater road tunnel that connects the provinces of Entre Ríos and Santa Fe in Argentina…

title: Surco River
fact: The Surco River, also known as the Surco Canal, is a pre-Columbian irrigation canal in Lima, Peru.

title: Bezymianny
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,882 m in Russia. Last erupted 2025. The modern Bezymianny, much smaller than its massive neighbors Kamen and Kliuchevskoi on the Kamchatka Peninsula…

title: Llaima
fact: Stratovolcano, 3,125 m in Chile. Last erupted 2009. Llaima, one of Chile's largest and most active volcanoes, contains two main historically active craters, one at the summit and the other, Pichillaima, to the SE.

title: La Palma
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,426 m in Spain. Last erupted 2021. The 47-km-long wedge-shaped island of La Palma, the NW-most of the Canary Islands, is composed of two large volcanic centers.

title: Barren Island
fact: Stratovolcano, 354 m in India. Last erupted 2026. Barren Island, a possession of India in the Andaman Sea about 135 km NE of Port Blair in the Andaman Islands, is the only historically active volcano along the N-S volcanic arc extending between Sumatra and Burma (Myanmar).

title: Izu-Oshima
fact: Stratovolcano, 758 m in Japan. Last erupted 1990. Izu-Oshima volcano in Sagami Bay, east of the Izu Peninsula, is the northernmost of the Izu Islands. The broad, low stratovolcano forms an 11 x 13 km island constructed over the remnants of three older dissected stratovolcanoes.

title: Anatahan
fact: Stratovolcano, 790 m in United States. Last erupted 2008. The elongate, 9-km-long island of Anatahan in the central Mariana Islands consists of a large stratovolcano with a 2.3 x 5 km compound summit caldera.

title: Redoubt
fact: Stratovolcano, 3,108 m in United States. Last erupted 2009. Redoubt is a glacier-covered stratovolcano with a breached summit crater in Lake Clark National Park about 170 km SW of Anchorage.

title: Krafla
fact: Caldera, 800 m in Iceland. Last erupted 1984. The Krafla volcanic system in the Northern Volcanic Zone (NVZ) of Iceland is about 100 km long, consisting of a fissure swarm and a central volcano with a 7 x 9 km caldera formed about 110,000 years ago that deposited a rhyolitic…

title: Alaid
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,285 m in Russia. Last erupted 2022. The highest and northernmost volcano of the Kuril Islands, Alaid is a symmetrical stratovolcano when viewed from the north, but has a 1.5-km-wide summit crater that is breached open to the south.

title: Ischia
fact: Complex volcano, 789 m in Italy. Last erupted 1302. The Ischia volcanic complex forms a rectangular, 6 x 9 km island immediately SW of the Campi Flegrei area at the western side of the Bay of Naples.

title: Slamet
fact: Stratovolcano, 3,428 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 2014. Slamet is one of Java's most active volcanoes. It has a cluster of about three dozen cinder cones on its lower SE-NE flanks and a single cinder cone on the W flank.

title: Santiago
fact: Shield volcano, 920 m in Ecuador. Last erupted 1906. The elongated shield volcano of Santiago Island, also known as San Salvador Island or James Island, has numerous scattered Holocene pyroclastic cones. Fresh-looking lava flows from these cones cover the flanks.

title: Raung
fact: Stratovolcano, 3,260 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 2025. Raung, one of Java's most active volcanoes, is a massive stratovolcano in easternmost Java that was constructed SW of the rim of Ijen caldera.

title: Batur
fact: Caldera, 1,711 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 2000. The historically active Batur is located at the center of two concentric calderas NW of Agung volcano.

title: Cleveland
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,730 m in United States. Last erupted 2020. The symmetrical Mount Cleveland stratovolcano is situated at the western end of the uninhabited Chuginadak Island.

title: Tacana
fact: Stratovolcano, 4,064 m in Mexico-Guatemala. Last erupted 1986. Tacaná is a 4064-m-high composite stratovolcano that straddles the México/Guatemala border at the NW end of the Central American volcanic belt.

title: Concepcion
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,700 m in Nicaragua. Last erupted 2024. Volcán Concepción is a symmetrical basaltic-to-dacitic stratovolcano that forms the NW half of the dumbbell-shaped island of Ometepe in Lake Nicaragua and is connected to neighboring Madera volcano by a narrow isthmus.

title: Guallatiri
fact: Stratovolcano, 6,071 m in Chile. Last erupted 1960. One of northern Chile's most active volcanoes, Volcán Guallatiri is a symmetrical ice-clad stratovolcano at the SW end of the Nevados de Quimsachata volcano group.

title: Soufriere Guadeloupe
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,467 m in France. Last erupted 1977. La Soufrière de la Guadeloupe volcano occupies the southern end of Basse-Terre, the western half of the island of Guadeloupe.

title: Zavodovski
fact: Stratovolcano, 551 m in United Kingdom. Last erupted 2016. The 5-km-wide Zavodovski Island, the northernmost of the South Sandwich Islands, consists of a single basaltic stratovolcano with two cones on the east side.

title: Orizaba, Pico de
fact: Stratovolcano, 5,564 m in Mexico. Last erupted 1846. Pico de Orizaba, México's highest peak and North America's highest volcano, lies at the southern end of a volcanic chain extending north to Cofre de Perote volcano, east of the Serdan-Oriental Basin.

title: Niuafo'ou
fact: Shield volcano, 260 m in Tonga. Last erupted 1946. Niuafo'ou ("Tin Can Island") is a low 8-km-wide island that forms the summit of a largely submerged basaltic shield volcano in the north central Lau Basin about 170 km W of the northern end of the Tofua volcanic arc.

title: Ekarma
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,170 m in Russia. Last erupted 2010. The small 5 x 7.5 km island of Ekarma lies 8.5 km N of Shiashkotan Island along an E-W-trending volcanic chain extending westward from the central part of the main Kuril Island arc.

title: Shishaldin
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,857 m in United States. Last erupted 2023. The symmetrical glacier-covered Shishaldin in the Aleutian Islands is the westernmost of three large stratovolcanoes in the eastern half of Unimak Island.

title: Katmai
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,047 m in United States. Last erupted 1912. Katmai was initially considered to be the source of the Valley of Ten Thousand Smokes ash flow in 1912.

title: Izalco
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,950 m in El Salvador. Last erupted 1966. Volcán de Izalco began growing in 1770 CE on the southern flank of Santa Ana volcano, eventually building a steep 650-m-high stratovolcano truncated by a 250-m-wide summit crater.

title: Tolima, Nevado del
fact: Stratovolcano, 5,215 m in Colombia. Last erupted 1943. The steep-sided, glacier-covered Nevado del Tolima volcano contrasts with the broad profile of Nevado del Ruiz to the north.

title: Gaua
fact: Stratovolcano, 729 m in Vanuatu. Last erupted 2022. The roughly 20-km-diameter Gaua Island, also known as Santa Maria, consists of a basaltic-to-andesitic stratovolcano with an 6 x 9 km summit caldera.

title: Dempo
fact: Stratovolcano, 3,142 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 2025. Dempo is a stratovolcano that rises above the Pasumah Plain of SE Sumatra. The andesitic complex has two main peaks, Gunung Dempo and Gunung Marapi, constructed near the SE rim of a 3-km-wide amphitheater open to the north.

title: Colo
fact: Stratovolcano, 404 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 1983. Colo volcano forms the isolated small island of Una Una in the middle of the Gulf of Tomini in northern Sulawesi. The broad, low volcano contains a 2-km-wide caldera with a small central cone.

title: Miyakejima
fact: Stratovolcano, 775 m in Japan. Last erupted 2010. The circular, 8-km-wide island of Miyakejima forms a low-angle stratovolcano that rises about 1,100 m from the sea floor in the northern Izu Islands about 200 km SSW of Tokyo.

title: Asuncion
fact: Stratovolcano, 857 m in United States. Last erupted 1906. A single large asymmetrical stratovolcano forms 3-km-wide Asuncion Island. The steeper NE flank terminates in high sea cliffs, while the gentler SW flanks have low-angle slopes bounded by sea cliffs only a few meters high.

title: Agrigan
fact: Stratovolcano, 965 m in United States. Last erupted 1917. The highest of the Marianas arc volcanoes, Agrigan contains a 500-m-deep, flat-floored caldera. The elliptical island is 8 km long; its summit is the top of a massive 4000-m-high submarine volcano.

title: Spurr
fact: Stratovolcano, 3,374 m in United States. Last erupted 1992. Mount Spurr is the closest volcano to Anchorage, Alaska (130 km W) and just NE of Chakachamna Lake.

title: San Miguel
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,130 m in El Salvador. Last erupted 2023. The symmetrical cone of San Miguel, one of the most active volcanoes in El Salvador, rises from near sea level to form one of the country's most prominent landmarks.

title: Maipo
fact: Caldera, 5,323 m in Chile-Argentina. Last erupted 1912. Maipo, a conical stratovolcano that straddles the Chile-Argentina border SE of Santiago, partially fills the 16 x 20 km Pleistocene Diamante caldera…

title: Lipari
fact: Stratovolcano, 590 m in Italy. Last erupted 1230. Lipari, the largest of the Aeolian Islands, is located immediately north of Vulcano Island. The irregular-shaped island contains numerous small stratovolcanoes, craters, and lava domes on a basement of submarine volcanic deposits.

title: Basile, Pico
fact: Shield volcano, 2,999 m in Equatorial Guinea. Last erupted 1923. Pico Basilé is the largest and highest of three basaltic shield volcanoes forming Bioko Island.

title: East Epi
fact: Stratovolcano, 833 m in Vanuatu. Last erupted 2023. The submarine East Epi group of basaltic and dacitic cones are located within a possible 10-km-diameter caldera off the NE coast of southern Epi Island in Vanuatu.

title: Salak
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,218 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 1938. The forested Salak volcano was constructed at the NE end of an eroded volcanic range. Satellitic cones occur on the SW flank and at the northern foot, and two large breached craters truncate the summit.

title: Chirinkotan
fact: Stratovolcano, 724 m in Russia. Last erupted 2022. The small, mostly unvegetated 3-km-wide island of Chirinkotan occupies the far end of an E-W volcanic chain that extends nearly 50 km W of the central part of the main Kuril Islands arc.

title: Kamaehuakanaloa
fact: Shield volcano, -975 m in United States. Last erupted 1996. The Kama`ehuakanaloa seamount, previously known as Lo`ihi, lies about 35 km off the SE coast of the island of Hawaii.

title: San Cristobal
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,745 m in Nicaragua. Last erupted 2024. The San Cristóbal volcanic complex, consisting of five principal volcanic edifices, forms the NW end of the Marrabios Range.

title: Ubinas
fact: Stratovolcano, 5,608 m in Peru. Last erupted 2024. The truncated appearance of Ubinas, Perú's most active volcano, is a result of a 1.4-km-wide crater at the summit.

title: Vulcano
fact: Stratovolcano, 500 m in Italy. Last erupted 1890. The word volcano is derived from Vulcano stratovolcano in Italy's Aeolian Islands. Vulcano was constructed during six stages over the past 136,000 years.

title: Kasatochi
fact: Stratovolcano, 314 m in United States. Last erupted 2008. Located at the northern end of a shallow submarine ridge trending perpendicular to the Aleutian arc, Kasatochi is small 2.7 x 3.3 km island volcano with a 750-m-wide summit crater lake.

title: Fernandina
fact: Shield volcano, 1,476 m in Ecuador. Last erupted 2024. Fernandina, the most active of Galápagos volcanoes and the one closest to the Galápagos mantle plume, is a basaltic shield volcano with a deep 5 x 6.5 km summit caldera.

title: Gamalama
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,714 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 2018. Gamalama is a near-conical stratovolcano that comprises the entire island of Ternate off the western coast of Halmahera, and is one of Indonesia's most active volcanoes.

title: Kirishimayama
fact: Shield volcano, 1,700 m in Japan. Last erupted 2025. Kirishimayama is a large group of more than 20 Quaternary volcanoes located north of Kagoshima Bay.

title: Turrialba
fact: Stratovolcano, 3,340 m in Costa Rica. Last erupted 2022. Turrialba, the easternmost of Costa Rica's Holocene volcanoes, is a large vegetated basaltic-to-dacitic stratovolcano located across a broad saddle NE of Irazú volcano overlooking the city of Cartago.

title: Llullaillaco
fact: Stratovolcano, 6,739 m in Chile-Argentina. Last erupted 1877. The world's highest historically active volcano, Llullaillaco sits astride the Chile-Argentina border. The summit is formed by a smaller well-preserved cone that was constructed on an older Pleistocene edifice.

title: Papandayan
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,643 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 2002. Papandayan is a complex stratovolcano at the S end of a curved volcanic massif with Kendang volcano ~9 km away at the N end, Gunung Puntang ~3.5 km NNE, and Gunung Jaya ~6 km NNE.

title: Dieng Volcanic Complex
fact: Complex volcano, 2,565 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 2025. The Dieng plateau in the highlands of central Java is renowned both for the variety of its volcanic scenery and as a sacred area housing Java's oldest Hindu temples, dating back to the 9th century CE.

title: Lokon-Empung
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,580 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 2015. The Lokong-Empung volcanic complex, rising above the plain of Tondano in North Sulawesi, includes four peaks and an active crater. Lokon, the highest peak, has a flat craterless top.

title: Funka Asane
fact: Stratovolcano, -20 m in Japan. Last erupted 2022. Eruptions have been recorded since the 18th century from Funka Asane, a submarine edifice ~4 km NW of Kita-Ioto, the northernmost of the Kazan Retto (Volcano Islands), in the southern Ogasawara Volcanic Arc.

title: Toya
fact: Stratovolcano, 733 m in Japan. Last erupted 2001. Usuzan, one of Hokkaido's most well-known volcanoes, is a small stratovolcano located astride the southern topographic rim of the 110,000-year-old Toya caldera.

title: Karymsky
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,513 m in Russia. Last erupted 2025. Karymsky is a symmetrical stratovolcano constructed within a 5-km-wide caldera that formed during the early Holocene.

title: St. Paul
fact: Stratovolcano, 268 m in France. Last erupted 1793. The uninhabited triangular island of St. Paul is located near the axis of the East Indian Ocean Ridge, 80 km S of Amsterdam Island.

title: Fukutoku-Oka-no-Ba
fact: Pyroclastic cone, -29 m in Japan. Last erupted 2021. Fukutoku-Oka-no-ba is a submarine volcano located 5 km NE of the island of Minami-Ioto. Water discoloration is frequently observed, and several ephemeral islands have formed in the 20th century.

title: Tangkuban Parahu
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,084 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 2019. Gunung Tangkuban Parahu is a broad stratovolcano overlooking Indonesia's former capital city of Bandung. The volcano was constructed within the 6 x 8 km Pleistocene Sunda caldera, which formed about 190,000 years ago.

title: Adatarayama
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,728 m in Japan. Last erupted 1996. The broad forested massif of Adatarayama volcano is located E of Bandai volcano, about 15 km SW of Fukushima city.

title: Farallon de Pajaros
fact: Stratovolcano, 337 m in United States. Last erupted 1953. The small 2-km-wide island of Farallon de Pajaros is the northernmost and most active volcano of the Mariana Islands.

title: Tokachidake
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,077 m in Japan. Last erupted 2004. Tokachidake volcano consists of a group of dominantly andesitic stratovolcanoes and lava domes arranged on a NE-SW line above a plateau of welded Pleistocene tuffs in central Hokkaido.

title: Ketoi
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,172 m in Russia. Last erupted 1960. The circular 10-km-wide Ketoi island, which rises across the 19-km-wide Diana Strait from Simushir Island, hosts of one of the most complex volcanic structures of the Kuril Islands.

title: Raikoke
fact: Stratovolcano, 551 m in Russia. Last erupted 2019. A low truncated volcano forms the small barren Raikoke Island, which lies 16 km across the Golovnin Strait from Matua Island in the central Kuriles.

title: Kharimkotan
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,145 m in Russia. Last erupted 1933. The 8 x 12 km island of Kharimkotan in the northern Kuriles consists of a stratovolcano cut by two breached depressions on the east and NW sides.

title: Rincon de la Vieja
fact: Complex volcano, 1,729 m in Costa Rica. Last erupted 2024. Rincón de la Vieja is a volcanic complex in the Guanacaste Range of NW Costa Rica. Sometimes referred to as the Rincon de la Vieja-Santa María Volcanic Complex…
story_label: Wikipedia: Rincón de la Vieja Volcano

title: Marchena
fact: Shield volcano, 343 m in Ecuador. Last erupted 1991. The low shield volcano forming Marchena Island contains one of the largest calderas of the Galápagos Islands.

title: Kverkfjoll
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,930 m in Iceland. Last erupted 1968. Kverkfjöll is a large subglacial volcano at the NE end of the Vatnajökull icecap. Two elliptical ice-filled calderas, each about 8 x 5 km in size, have been identified.

title: Nightingale Island
fact: Stratovolcano, 365 m in United Kingdom. Last erupted 2004. Nightingale Island, along with the adjacent smaller Middle (or Alex) and Stoltenhoff Islands and associated small islets, are the southernmost of the Tristan da Cunha island group.

title: Gede-Pangrango
fact: Stratovolcano, 3,026 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 1957. The two peaks of the Gede-Pangrango volcanic complex overlook the major cities of Cianjur, Sukabumi, and Bogor, situated to the E, S, and NW, respectively.

title: Soputan
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,785 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 2020. The Soputan stratovolcano on the southern rim of the Quaternary Tondano caldera on the northern arm of Sulawesi Island is one of Sulawesi's most active volcanoes.

title: Karangetang
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,797 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 2023. Karangetang (Api Siau) volcano lies at the northern end of the island of Siau, about 125 km NNE of the NE-most point of Sulawesi. The stratovolcano contains five summit craters along a N-S line.

title: Gamkonora
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,635 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 2007. The shifting of eruption centers on Gamkonora, the highest peak of Halmahera, has produced an elongated series of summit craters along a N-S trending rift.

title: Myojinsho
fact: Caldera, 11 m in Japan. Last erupted 1970. Beyonesu Rocks are part of the barely exposed rim of the largely submarine Myojinsho caldera.

title: Izu-Torishima
fact: Stratovolcano, 394 m in Japan. Last erupted 2002. The circular, 2.7-km-wide island of Izu-Torishima in the southern Izu Islands is capped by an unvegetated summit cone formed during an eruption in 1939.

title: Pavlof
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,493 m in United States. Last erupted 2022. The most active volcano of the Aleutian arc, Pavlof is a Holocene stratovolcano that was constructed along a line of vents extending NE from the Emmons Lake caldera.

title: Wrangell
fact: Shield volcano, 4,278 m in United States. Last erupted 1912. Mount Wrangell is one of the world's largest continental-margin volcanoes, with a diameter of 30 km at 2,000 m elevation.

title: Irruputuncu
fact: Stratovolcano, 5,163 m in Chile-Bolivia. Last erupted 1995. Irruputuncu is a small stratovolcano that straddles the Chile/Bolivia border. It is the youngest and most southerly of a NE-SW-trending chain of volcanoes.

title: Azul, Cerro
fact: Stratovolcano, 3,788 m in Chile. Last erupted 1967. The Cerro Azul stratovolcano is at the southern end of the Descabezado Grande-Cerro Azul eruptive system. It is a steep-sided edifice with a 500-m-wide summit crater open to the north.

title: Tristan da Cunha
fact: Shield volcano, 2,060 m in United Kingdom. Last erupted 1962. Tristan da Cunha is a 13-km-wide island volcano lying about 500 km E of the crest of the Mid-Atlantic Ridge just south of the latitudes of Buenos Aires and Cape Town.

title: Tair, Jebel at
fact: Stratovolcano, 244 m in Yemen. Last erupted 2008. The basaltic Jebel at Tair volcano rises from 1,200 m depth in the south-central Red Sea, forming an oval-shaped island about 3 km long.

title: Arjuno-Welirang
fact: Stratovolcano, 3,343 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 1952. The Arjuno and Welirang volcanoes anchor the SE and NW ends, respectively, of a 6-km-long line of volcanic cones and craters.

title: Kuchinoerabujima
fact: Stratovolcano, 657 m in Japan. Last erupted 2020. A group of young stratovolcanoes forms the eastern end of the irregularly shaped island of Kuchinoerabujima in the northern Ryukyu Islands, 15 km W of Yakushima.

title: Iwatesan
fact: Complex volcano, 2,038 m in Japan. Last erupted 1919. Viewed from the east, Iwatesan volcano has a symmetrical profile that invites comparison with Fuji, but on the west an older cone is visible containing an oval-shaped, 1.8 x 3 km caldera.

title: Shikotsu
fact: Caldera, 1,320 m in Japan. Last erupted 1981. The 13 x 15 km Shikotsu caldera, largely filled by the waters of Lake Shikotsu, was formed during one of Hokkaido's largest Quaternary eruptions about 31-34,000 years ago.

title: Rasshua
fact: Stratovolcano, 956 m in Russia. Last erupted 1957. The elongated 6 x 13 km island of Rasshua in the central Kuriles contains three overlapping central cones within a 6 km caldera whose eastern margin is beyond the shoreline.

title: Ebeko
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,103 m in Russia. Last erupted 2024. The flat-topped summit of the central cone of Ebeko volcano, one of the most active in the Kuril Islands, occupies the northern end of Paramushir Island.

title: Telica
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,036 m in Nicaragua. Last erupted 2025. Telica, one of Nicaragua's most active volcanoes, has erupted frequently since the beginning of the Spanish era. This volcano group consists of several interlocking cones and vents with a general NW alignment.

title: Negro, Cerro
fact: Pyroclastic cone, 728 m in Nicaragua. Last erupted 1999. Nicaragua's youngest volcano, Cerro Negro, was created following an eruption that began in April 1850 about 2 km NW of the summit of Las Pilas volcano.

title: Cumbal
fact: Stratovolcano, 4,764 m in Colombia. Last erupted 1926. Many youthful lava flows extend from the glacier-capped Cumbal volcano, the southernmost historically active volcano of Colombia.

title: Montagu Island
fact: Shield volcano, 1,370 m in United Kingdom. Last erupted 2007. The largest of the South Sandwich Islands, Montagu consists of a massive shield volcano cut by a 6-km-wide ice-filled summit caldera.

title: Talang
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,575 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 2007. Talang is part of a large volcanic edifice just NW of Dibawah Lake. An older volcanic peak, Pasar Arbaao, is ~1.5 km W. The steep-sided Talang cone exhibits fumarolic activity but has no crater…

title: Mutnovsky
fact: Complex volcano, 2,288 m in Russia. Last erupted 2000. Massive Mutnovsky, one of the most active volcanoes of southern Kamchatka, is formed of four coalescing stratovolcanoes of predominantly basaltic composition. Multiple summit craters cap the volcanic complex.

title: Kizimen
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,334 m in Russia. Last erupted 2013. Kizimen is an isolated, conical stratovolcano that is morphologically similar to St. Helens prior to its 1980 eruption.

title: Alcedo
fact: Shield volcano, 1,130 m in Ecuador. Last erupted 1993. Alcedo is one of the lowest and smallest of six shield volcanoes on Isabela Island. Much of the flanks and summit caldera are vegetated, but young lava flows are prominent on the N flank near the saddle with Darwin volcano.

title: Tupungatito
fact: Stratovolcano, 5,660 m in Chile-Argentina. Last erupted 1987. Tupungatito volcano, the northernmost historically active volcano of the central Chilean Andes, is located along the Chile-Argentina border about 90 km E of Santiago and immediately SW of the Pleistocene Tupungato…

title: Southern Thule
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,075 m in United Kingdom. Last erupted 1975. The Southern Thule island group, at the southern end of the South Sandwich island arc bordering the Scotia Sea, consist of three stratovolcanoes constructed along an E-W line.

title: Halla
fact: Shield volcano, 1,919 m in South Korea. Last erupted 1007. The massive Halla shield volcano forms much of the 40 x 80 km Cheju (Jeju) Island, which lies 90 km S of the Korean Peninsula.

title: Ascension
fact: Stratovolcano, 822 m in United Kingdom. Last erupted 1508. Ascensión Island, just west of the Mid-Atlantic Ridge ~2,250 km E of the eastern-most point of Brazil, is the 12-km-diameter emergent summit of a stratovolcano that rises ~3,000 m above the seafloor.

title: Ciremai
fact: Stratovolcano, 3,039 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 1951. The symmetrical Ciremai stratovolcano is located closer to the northern coast than other central Java volcanoes.

title: Paluweh
fact: Stratovolcano, 875 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 2013. Paluweh, also known as Rokatenda, forms the 8-km-wide island of Palu'e north of the volcanic arc that cuts across Flores Island.

title: Camiguin
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,552 m in Philippines. Last erupted 1953. The 20-km-long Camiguin Island just off the coast of north-central Mindanao Island consists of four overlapping stratovolcanoes overlying older buried edifices.

title: Kusatsu-Shiranesan
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,165 m in Japan. Last erupted 2018. The Kusatsu-Shiranesan complex, located immediately north of Asama volcano, consists of a series of overlapping pyroclastic cones and three crater lakes.

title: Chokaisan
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,236 m in Japan. Last erupted 1974. Chokaisan is composed of two overlapping stratovolcanoes with a conical profile that inspired the local names of Akita-Fuji or Dewa-Fuji.

title: Kanaga
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,307 m in United States. Last erupted 2023. Symmetrical Kanaga stratovolcano is situated within the Kanaton caldera at the northern tip of Kanaga Island.

title: Bogoslof
fact: Stratovolcano, 150 m in United States. Last erupted 2017. Bogoslof is the emergent summit of a submarine volcano that lies 40 km N of the main Aleutian arc. It rises 1,500 m above the Bering Sea floor.

title: Akutan
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,303 m in United States. Last erupted 1992. Akutan contains a 2-km-wide caldera with a large cinder cone in the NE part of the caldera that has been the source of frequent explosive eruptions and occasional lava effusion that covers the caldera floor.

title: Miravalles
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,028 m in Costa Rica. Last erupted 1946. Miravalles is an andesitic stratovolcano that is one of five post-caldera cones along a NE-trending line within the broad 15 x 20 km Guayabo (Miravalles) caldera.

title: Isluga
fact: Stratovolcano, 5,550 m in Chile. Last erupted 1913. The broad Isluga volcano lies 7 km W of the Chile/Bolivia border at the W end of a group of volcanoes extending to Tata Sabaya volcano in Bolivia.

title: Bristol Island
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,100 m in United Kingdom. Last erupted 2016. The 9 x 10 km Bristol Island near the southern end of the South Sandwich arc lies across Fortser's Passage from the Southern Thule Islands and forms one of the largest islands of the chain.

title: Candlemas Island
fact: Stratovolcano, 550 m in United Kingdom. Last erupted 1911. The southern end of Candlemas Island consists of an eroded, glacier-covered basaltic stratovolcano cut by steep cliffs on the east.

title: Kie Matubu
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,713 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 1210. The conical Kie Matubu volcano on the south end of Tidore Island is the highest peak of the North Maluku island chain west of Halmahera. Faral et al. (2022) identified deposits from two eruptions within the past 3,000 years.

title: Oraefajokull
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,010 m in Iceland. Last erupted 1728. Öræfajökull, Iceland's highest peak, is a broad glacier-clad central volcano at the SE end of the Vatnajökull icecap. A 4 x 5 km subglacial caldera truncates the summit of the dominantly basaltic and rhyolitic volcano.

title: Fagradalsfjall
fact: Fissure vent, 250 m in Iceland. Last erupted 2023. Although the Fagradalsfjall fissure swarm has previously been considered a split or secondary swarm of the Krýsuvík–Trölladyngja volcanic system…

title: Eldey
fact: Fissure vent, 70 m in Iceland. Last erupted 1926. The Eldey volcanic system is located on the northernmost part of the Reykjanes Ridge and is submarine with the exception of Eldey Island and the skerries (small rocky islands) Eldeyjardrangur, Geirfugladrangur, and Geirfuglasker.

title: Raoul Island
fact: Stratovolcano, 516 m in New Zealand. Last erupted 2006. Anvil-shaped Raoul Island is the largest and northernmost of the Kermadec Islands. During the past several thousand years volcanism has been dominated by dacitic explosive eruptions.

title: Karkar
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,839 m in Papua New Guinea. Last erupted 1979. Karkar is a 19 x 25 km forest-covered island that is truncated by two nested summit calderas. The 5.5 km outer caldera was formed during one or more eruptions, the last of which occurred 9,000 years ago.

title: Izu-Tobu
fact: Pyroclastic cone, 580 m in Japan. Last erupted 1989. The Izu-Tobu (or Higashi-Izu) volcano group is scattered over a broad, plateau-like area of more than 400 km2 on the E side of the Izu Peninsula.

title: Zaozan [Zaosan]
fact: Complex volcano, 1,841 m in Japan. Last erupted 1940. The Zaozan (or Zaosan) volcano group consists of a complex cluster of stratovolcanoes in north-central Honshu about 40 km W of Sendai Bay.

title: Semisopochnoi
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,221 m in United States. Last erupted 2023. Semisopochnoi, the largest subaerial volcano of the western Aleutians, is 20 km wide at sea level and contains an 8-km-wide caldera.

title: Azul, Cerro
fact: Shield volcano, 1,640 m in Ecuador. Last erupted 2008. Located at the SW tip of the J-shaped Isabela Island, Cerro Azul contains a steep-walled 4 x 5 km nested summit caldera complex that is one of the smallest diameter, but at 650 m one of the deepest in the Galápagos Islands.

title: Tinguiririca
fact: Stratovolcano, 4,280 m in Chile. Last erupted 1917. Tinguiririca is composed of at least seven Holocene scoria cones W of the Chile-Argentina border constructed along a NNE-SSW fissure over an eroded Pleistocene stratovolcano.

title: Descabezado Grande
fact: Stratovolcano, 3,953 m in Chile. Last erupted 1933. Volcán Descabezado Grande is a late-Pleistocene to Holocene andesitic-to-rhyodacitic stratovolcano with a 1.4-km-wide ice-filled summit crater.

title: Kazbek
fact: Stratovolcano, 5,004 m in Georgia. Last erupted 750 BCE. The glacier-covered Kazbek stratovolcano in the Caucasus Mountains of Georgia, just south of the border with Russia, has produced long lava flows down flank valleys.

title: Haleakala
fact: Shield volcano, 3,053 m in United States. Last erupted 1750. The massive Haleakala shield volcano forms the eastern portion of the island of Maui. The summit is at the NW end of a volcanic ridge and at the head of a large scarp that opens to the ENE…

title: Pico
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,351 m in Portugal. Last erupted 1720. The conical Pico stratovolcano occupies the western end of Pico Island and is the highest volcano in the Azores.

title: Tinakula
fact: Stratovolcano, 796 m in Solomon Islands. Last erupted 2024. The small 3.5-km-wide island of Tinakula is the exposed summit of a massive stratovolcano at the NW end of the Santa Cruz islands. It has a breached summit crater that extends from the summit to below sea level.

title: Sundoro
fact: Stratovolcano, 3,149 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 1971. Gunung Sundoro, in central Java, is located between the Dieng complex to the NW and Sumbing volcano to the SE. The large Kembang cone is about 2.5 km from the summit on the SW flank.

title: Akan
fact: Caldera, 1,499 m in Japan. Last erupted 2026. Akan is a 13 x 24 km caldera located immediately SW of Kussharo caldera in eastern Hokkaido.

title: Ksudach
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,007 m in Russia. Last erupted 1907. Ksudach is unique among Kamchatka volcanoes in its morphology and geologic history. It is a large, low-angle stratovolcano, constructed of alternating basaltic-andesitic lavas and dacitic pyroclastics…

title: Zhupanovsky
fact: Compound volcano, 2,899 m in Russia. Last erupted 2016. The Zhupanovsky volcanic massif consists of four overlapping stratovolcanoes along a WNW-trending ridge.

title: Tanaga
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,806 m in United States. Last erupted 1914. Tanaga volcano, the second largest volcanic center of the central Aleutians, is the central and highest of three youthful stratovolcanoes oriented along a roughly E-W line at the NW tip of Tanaga Island.

title: Veniaminof
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,507 m in United States. Last erupted 2021. Veniaminof, on the Alaska Peninsula, is truncated by a steep-walled, 8 x 11 km, glacier-filled caldera that formed around 3,700 years ago.

title: Penguin Island
fact: Stratovolcano, 180 m in Antarctica. Last erupted 1905. The 1.4 x 1.7 km Penguin Island is located off the SE coast of King George Island in Antarctica's South Shetland Islands, west of the axis of the Bransfield Rift.

title: Long Island
fact: Complex volcano, 1,263 m in Papua New Guinea. Last erupted 1993. The broad profile of Long Island is dominated by two steep-sided stratovolcanoes, Mount Reaumur in the north and Cerisy Peak in the south.

title: Lamington
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,680 m in Papua New Guinea. Last erupted 1956. Lamington is an andesitic stratovolcano with a 1.3-km-wide breached summit crater containing a lava dome that rises above the coastal plain of the Papuan Peninsula of New Guinea north of the Owen Stanley Range.

title: Kavachi
fact: Stratovolcano, -20 m in Solomon Islands. Last erupted 2014. Named for a sea-god of the Gatokae and Vangunu peoples, Kavachi is located in the Solomon Islands south of Vangunu Island.

title: Telong, Bur ni
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,617 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 1937. The conical Bur ni Telong volcano was constructed at the southern base of the massive Bur ni Geureudong volcanic complex, one of the largest in northern Sumatra.

title: Tandikat-Singgalang
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,879 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 1924. This volcanic complex is dominated by the Singgalang stratovolcano and the smaller Tandikat edifice ~4.5 km SSW. They are located ~15 km WSW across the Bukittinggi plain from Marapi volcano.

title: Tara, Batu
fact: Stratovolcano, 633 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 2015. The small isolated island of Batu Tara is located in the Flores Sea ~50 km N of Lembata Island and the main volcanic arc.

title: Hakoneyama
fact: Complex volcano, 1,438 m in Japan. Last erupted 2015. Hakoneyama volcano is truncated by two overlapping calderas, the largest of which is 10 x 11 km wide. The calderas were formed as a result of two major explosive eruptions about 180,000 and 49,000-60,000 years ago.

title: Hokkaido-Komagatake
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,131 m in Japan. Last erupted 2000. Much of the truncated Hokkaido-Komagatake andesitic volcano on the Oshima Peninsula of southern Hokkaido is Pleistocene in age.

title: Etorofu-Atosanupuri [Atosanupuri]
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,209 m in Japan - administered by Russia. Last erupted 1932. The conical Etorofu-Atosanupuri stratovolcano forms a peninsula joined to the SW side of Iturup (Etorofu) Island by an isthmus 30 m high.

title: Maly Semyachik
fact: Caldera, 1,527 m in Russia. Last erupted 1952. Maly Semyachik is a compound stratovolcano located in a 10-km-wide caldera within the 15 x 20 km mid-Pleistocene Stena-Soboliny caldera.

title: Aniakchak
fact: Caldera, 1,341 m in United States. Last erupted 1931. One of the most dramatic calderas of the Aleutian arc, the 10-km-wide Aniakchak caldera formed around 3,400 years ago during a voluminous eruption in which pyroclastic flows traveled more than 50 km N to the Bering Sea and…

title: Fourpeaked
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,105 m in United States. Last erupted 2006. Poorly known Fourpeaked volcano in NE Katmai National Park consists of isolated outcrops surrounded by the Fourpeaked Glacier, which descends eastward almost to the Shelikof Strait.

title: San Jose
fact: Stratovolcano, 6,070 m in Chile-Argentina. Last erupted 1960. Volcán San José lies along the Chile-Argentina border at the southern end of a volcano group that includes the Pleistocene volcanoes of Marmolejo and Espíritu Santo.

title: Callaqui
fact: Stratovolcano, 3,099 m in Chile. Last erupted 1980. The late-Pleistocene to Holocene Callaqui stratovolcano has a profile of an overturned canoe, due to its construction along an 11-km-long, SW-NE fissure above a 1.2-0.3 million year old Pleistocene edifice.

title: Lonquimay
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,832 m in Chile. Last erupted 1990. Lonquimay is a small, flat-topped, symmetrical stratovolcano of late-Pleistocene to dominantly Holocene age immediately SE of Tolguaca volcano. A glacier fills its summit crater and flows down the S flank.

title: Osorno
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,659 m in Chile. Last erupted 1869. The symmetrical, glaciated, Osorno volcano towers above Todos los Santos and Llanquihué lakes.

title: Baru
fact: Stratovolcano, 3,474 m in Panama. Last erupted 1550. The westernmost volcano in Panamá, Barú, is a complex dominantly andesitic stratovolcano in the Talamanca Range near the Costa Rica border.

title: Cayambe
fact: Compound volcano, 5,790 m in Ecuador. Last erupted 1786. The massive compound andesitic-dacitic Cayambe stratovolcano is located on the western edge of the Cordillera Real, east of the Inter-Andean Valley.

title: Dabbahu
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,401 m in Ethiopia. Last erupted 2005. Dabbahu is a Pleistocene-to-Holocene volcanic massif forming an axial range of the Afar depression SSW of the Alayta massif.

title: Kadovar
fact: Stratovolcano, 365 m in Papua New Guinea. Last erupted 2023. The 2-km-wide island of Kadovar is the emergent summit of a Bismarck Sea stratovolcano of Holocene age.

title: Sorikmarapi
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,145 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 1986. Sorikmarapi is a forested stratovolcano with a 600-m-wide summit crater containing a lake and substantial sulfur deposits.

title: Nakanoshima
fact: Stratovolcano, 979 m in Japan. Last erupted 1914. The 9 x 5 km island of Nakanoshima is surrounded by coral reefs. A flat plateau separates the older dissected Sakiwaridake volcano on the south from the active andesitic cone of Ontake, which forms the northern half of the island.

title: Azumayama
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,949 m in Japan. Last erupted 1977. The Azumayama volcanic group consists of a cluster of stratovolcanoes, shield volcanoes, lava domes, and pyroclastic cones.

title: Kambalny
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,116 m in Russia. Last erupted 2017. The southernmost major stratovolcano on the Kamchatka peninsula, Kambalny has a summit crater that is breached to the SE. Five Holocene cinder cones on the W and SE flanks have produced fresh-looking lava flows.

title: Gorely
fact: Caldera, 1,799 m in Russia. Last erupted 2010. Gorely volcano consists of five small overlapping stratovolcanoes constructed along a WNW-ESE line within a large 9 x 13 km caldera.

title: Chiles-Cerro Negro
fact: Stratovolcano, 4,698 m in Colombia-Ecuador. Last erupted 1936. The Chiles-Cerro Negro volcanic complex includes both the Pleistocene Chiles and the Cerro Negro de Mayasquer stratovolcanoes astride the Colombia-Ecuador border.

title: Burney, Monte
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,758 m in Chile. Last erupted 1910. Monte Burney, a large ice-covered volcano in the Patagonian region of Chile, lies about 200 km NW of the town of Punta Arenas.

title: Kick 'em Jenny
fact: Complex volcano, -185 m in Grenada. Last erupted 2017. Kick 'em Jenny, an active submarine volcano 8 km off the N shore of Grenada, rises 1,300 m from the sea floor.

title: Huaynaputina
fact: Stratovolcano, 4,679 m in Peru. Last erupted 1600. Huaynaputina (whose name means "new volcano") was the source of the largest historical eruption of South America in 1600 CE.

title: Ardoukoba
fact: Fissure vent, 298 m in Djibouti. Last erupted 1978. The Ardoukôba (Asal) Rift in Djibouti, trending NW from the Red Sea, contains a broad area of youthful fissure vents between Lake Asal and the Ghoubbat al Kharab gulf.

title: Kuwae
fact: Caldera, -2 m in Vanuatu. Last erupted 1974. The largely submarine Kuwae caldera occupies the area between Epi and Tongoa islands. The 6 x 12 km caldera contains two basins that cut the NW end of Tongoa Island and the flank of the Tavani Ruru volcano on the SE peninsula of Epi…

title: Matthew Island
fact: Stratovolcano, 177 m in France - claimed by Vanuatu. Last erupted 1956. Matthew Island is composed of two low andesitic-to-dacitic cones separated by a narrow isthmus. The Matthew name originates from an English mariner who sighted the island in 1788.
