title: Ebulobo
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,096 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 1969. Ebulobo, also referred to as Amburombu or Keo Peak, is a steep-sided symmetrical stratovolcano in central Flores Island.

title: Iya
fact: Stratovolcano, 618 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 1969. Gunung Iya is the southernmost of a group of three volcanoes comprising a small peninsula south of the city of Ende on central Flores Island.

title: Banda Api
fact: Caldera, 596 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 1988. The 3-km-wide island of Banda Api is the northern-most volcano in the Banda arc and has a long period of recorded observation because of its key location in the Portuguese and Dutch spice trade.

title: Kie Besi
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,357 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 1988. Kie Besi volcano, forming the 10-km-wide Makian island off the west coast of Halmahera, has been the source of infrequent, but strong eruptions that have devastated villages on the island.

title: Nikko-Shiranesan
fact: Shield volcano, 2,578 m in Japan. Last erupted 1952. Nikko-Shiranesan is a relatively small, 2578-m-high andesitic volcano consisting of a group of four lava domes resting on a shield volcano that rises to the NW of scenic Lake Chuzenji in Nikko National Park.

title: Akita-Komagatake
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,637 m in Japan. Last erupted 1971. Two calderas partially filled by basaltic cones cut the summit of Akita-Komagatake volcano.

title: Yunaska
fact: Shield volcano, 550 m in United States. Last erupted 1937. The elongated 9 x 23 km Yunaska in the Islands of the Four Mountains group of the Aleutian Islands is comprised of two distinct volcanic centers.

title: San Salvador
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,893 m in El Salvador. Last erupted 1917. The massive compound San Salvador volcano dominates the landscape W of El Salvador's capital city of San Salvador.

title: Dona Juana
fact: Stratovolcano, 4,137 m in Colombia. Last erupted 1906. The forested Doña Juana stratovolcano contains two calderas, breached to the NE and SW. The summit of the andesitic-dacitic volcano is comprised of a series of post-caldera lava domes.

title: Aragats
fact: Stratovolcano, 4,095 m in Armenia. No eruption in recorded history. Aragats is a large andesitic-to-dacitic stratovolcano in NW Armenia about 40 km NW of the capital city of Yerevan. The main edifice is dissected by glaciers and is of Pliocene-to-Pleistocene age.

title: Nemrut Dagi
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,948 m in Turkiye. Last erupted 1650. Nemrut Dagi is the westernmost of a group of volcanoes near Lake Van in eastern Anatolia and the only one that has erupted in historical time.

title: Bandaisan
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,816 m in Japan. Last erupted 1888. One of Japan's most noted volcanoes, Bandaisan rises above the north shore of Lake Inawashiro. This complex is formed of several overlapping andesitic stratovolcanoes, the largest of which is Obandai.

title: Hachijojima
fact: Stratovolcano, 854 m in Japan. Last erupted 1606. Hachijojima, in the central Izu Islands about 300 km S of Tokyo, consists of two small Quaternary dominantly basaltic stratovolcanoes forming an elongated NW-SE-trending island.

title: Alu-Dalafilla
fact: Fissure vent, 578 m in Ethiopia. Last erupted 2008. The summit region of Alu, ~5 km NW of the Dalafilla stratovolcano, is an ellipsoidal volcanic horst, elongated NNW-SSE, and formed primarily of older basaltic lava flows.

title: Alayta
fact: Shield volcano, 1,496 m in Ethiopia. Last erupted 1915. The massive Alayta shield volcano covers an area of 2700 km2 in the western Danakil depression SW of Lake Afrera. A series of very recent craters is aligned along the NNW-trending axis of the basaltic-to-trachytic shield.

title: Fonualei
fact: Stratovolcano, 188 m in Tonga. Last erupted 1957. The small island of Fonualei (~2 km diameter) contains a fumarolically active crater breached to the SE with a fresh lava flow extending to the sea and forming a rugged shoreline.

title: Ritter Island
fact: Stratovolcano, 75 m in Papua New Guinea. Last erupted 2007. Prior to 1888, Ritter Island was a steep-sided, nearly circular island about 780 m high between Umboi and Sakar Islands.

title: Lopevi
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,413 m in Vanuatu. Last erupted 2007. The small 7-km-wide conical island of Lopevi, known locally as Vanei Vollohulu, is one of Vanuatu's most active volcanoes.

title: Egon
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,661 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 2008. Gunung Egon, also known as Namang, sits within the narrow section of eastern Flores Island. The barren, sparsely vegetated summit region has a 350-m-wide, 200-m-deep crater that sometimes contains a lake.

title: Sirung
fact: Complex volcano, 1,347 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 2021. Sirung is located at the NE end of a volcanic massif with multiple centers that extends 14 km NE from the southern end of Pantar Island.

title: Ambang
fact: Complex volcano, 1,795 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 2005. The compound Ambang volcano is the westernmost of the active volcanoes on the northern arm of Sulawesi. The stratovolcano rises 750 m above lake Danau.

title: Babuyan Claro
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,064 m in Philippines. Last erupted 1924. Multiple Quaternary volcanic centers occupy Babuyan de Claro Island north of Luzon. The largest edifice is Babuyan Claro (Mount Pangasun) at the center of the island…

title: Kujusan
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,791 m in Japan. Last erupted 1996. Kujusan is a complex of stratovolcanoes and lava domes lying NE of Aso caldera in north-central Kyushu. The group consists of 16 andesitic lava domes, five andesitic stratovolcanoes, and one basaltic cone.

title: Nasudake
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,915 m in Japan. Last erupted 1963. The Nasudake volcanic group consists of a N-S-trending cluster of stratovolcanoes and lava domes at the north end of the Kanto Plain. Volcanic activity dates back about 500,000 years.

title: Nemo Peak
fact: Caldera, 994 m in Russia. Last erupted 1938. Nemo Peak volcano at the northern end of Onekotan Island in the northern Kuriles is truncated by two preglacial nested calderas, the largest of which is 10 km in diameter and extends to the northern coast.

title: Iliinsky
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,555 m in Russia. Last erupted 1901. The conical Iliinsky volcano, rising dramatically to 1555 m above the NE shore of Kurile Lake, was constructed beginning about 7600 radiocarbon years ago at the NE margin of Kurile Lake caldera.

title: Zheltovsky
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,926 m in Russia. Last erupted 1923. Zheltovsky volcano was constructed during the last 8000 years within a 4 x 5 km caldera truncating an earlier Pleistocene edifice.

title: Atka Volcanic Complex
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,518 m in United States. Last erupted 2025. The Atka Volcanic Complex consists of a central shield and Pleistocene caldera and four notable volcanic cones.

title: Seguam
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,054 m in United States. Last erupted 1993. The 11.5 x 24 km island of Seguam, between Amlia and Amukta Islands in the central Aleutians, contains two calderas with Holocene post-caldera cones.

title: Makushin
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,800 m in United States. Last erupted 1995. The ice-covered Makushin volcano on northern Unalaska Island is capped by a 2.5 km caldera. Its broad, dome-like structure contrasts with the steep-sided profiles of most other Aleutian stratovolcanoes.

title: Negra, Sierra
fact: Shield volcano, 1,124 m in Ecuador. Last erupted 2018. The broad shield volcano of Sierra Negra at the southern end of Isabela Island contains a shallow 7 x 10.5 km caldera that is the largest in the Galápagos Islands.

title: Lautaro
fact: Stratovolcano, 3,542 m in Chile. Last erupted 1979. Lautaro is the northernmost volcano of the Austral Volcanic Zone (AVZ) in the southernmost Chilean Andes, and is the closest volcano to the Chile Triple Junction plate boundary.

title: Watt, Morne
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,224 m in Dominica. Last erupted 1997. Morne Watt (Watt Mountain) volcano lies SE of the Trois Piton/Micotrin lava-dome complex in SE Dominica, E of the capital city of Roseau.

title: Erciyes Volcanic Complex
fact: Stratovolcano, 3,864 m in Turkiye. Last erupted 6,880 BCE. The Erciyes Volcanic Complex at the northern end of the Sultansazligi Basin in central Anatolia is dominated by the massive eroded Erciyes Dagi stratovolcano at the approximate center of a radial monogenetic volcanic…

title: Campi Flegrei del Mar di Sicilia
fact: Volcanic field, -8 m in Italy. Last erupted 1867. Campi Flegrei del Mar di Sicilia (Phlegraean Fields of the Sicily Sea) is composed of a group of submarine volcanoes SW of Sicily.

title: Hakusan
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,702 m in Japan. Last erupted 1659. Hakusan is a complex andesitic-dacitic stratovolcano near the western coast of central Honshu.

title: Saba
fact: Stratovolcano, 887 m in Netherlands. Last erupted 1640. Saba, the northernmost active volcano of the West Indies, is a 5-km-diameter island forming the upper half of a large stratovolcano that rises 1,500 m above the sea floor.

title: Tutuila
fact: Tuff cone, 653 m in United States. Last erupted 440 CE. The elongated, extensively eroded Tutuila Island in the center of the Samoan Islands consists of five Pliocene-to-Pleistocene volcanoes constructed along two or three rifts trending SSW-NNE.

title: Amsterdam Island
fact: Stratovolcano, 881 m in France. No eruption in recorded history. The elliptical 7 x 10 km Amsterdam Island is the northernmost subaerial volcano on the Antarctic Plate. The basaltic volcano is located near the axis of the East Indian Ocean Ridge adjacent to the Indian Plate.

title: Upolu
fact: Shield volcano, 1,100 m in Samoa. No eruption in recorded history. The massive, basaltic shield volcano forming 75-km-long Upolu Island in Samoa is elongated in an E-W direction and was constructed during two periods of extensive eruptions during the Pliocene and Pleistocene.

title: Snaefellsjokull
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,446 m in Iceland. Last erupted 200 CE. Ice-clad Snaefellsjökull volcano anchors the western tip of the isolated Snaefellsnes Peninsula in western Iceland.

title: Madeira
fact: Shield volcano, 1,862 m in Portugal. Last erupted 4,500 BCE. Madeira Island is the emergent top of a massive shield volcano that rises about 6 km from the floor of the Atlantic Ocean and forms the largest island of the 90-km-long Madeira Archipelago.

title: Antisana
fact: Stratovolcano, 5,753 m in Ecuador. Last erupted 1802. Antisana is a massive, glacier-covered stratovolcano NE of Cotopaxi, along the western margin of the Eastern Cordillera, 50 km SE of Quito.

title: Fonuafo'ou
fact: Stratovolcano, -17 m in Tonga. Last erupted 1936. The ephemeral Fonuafo'ou island in the central part of the Tonga Islands is also known as Falcon Island, named after the British vessel H.M.S. Falcon, which reported a shoal in 1865.

title: Simbo
fact: Stratovolcano, 335 m in Solomon Islands. Last erupted 1910. Simbo is a small island in the western Solomons with three truncated andesitic volcanic centers.

title: Yakedake
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,455 m in Japan. Last erupted 1995. Yakedake rises above the popular resort of Kamikochi in the Northern Japan Alps. The small dominantly andesitic stratovolcano, one of several Japanese volcanoes named Yakedake or Yakeyama…

title: Sumisujima
fact: Caldera, 136 m in Japan. Last erupted 1916. Sumisujima is a steep-sided basaltic pinnacle that forms part of the outer southern flank of a 8-9 km submarine caldera that truncates a 20-km-wide seamount. The caldera was formed between about 60,000 and 30,000 years ago.

title: Sashiusudake [Baransky]
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,128 m in Japan - administered by Russia. Last erupted 1951. The Sashiusudake volcanic complex along the Pacific coast in the central part of Iturup Island consists of a Holocene stratovolcano built over an eroded Pleistocene edifice.

title: Moyorodake [Medvezhia]
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,124 m in Japan - administered by Russia. Last erupted 1999. The Moyorodake volcanic complex occupies the NE end of Iturup (Etorofu) Island. Two overlapping calderas, 14 x 18 and 10 x 12 km in diameter, were formed during the Pleistocene.

title: Amukta
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,066 m in United States. Last erupted 1996. The symmetrical Amukta stratovolcano lies in the central Aleutians SW of Chagulak Island and is the westernmost of the Islands of the Four Mountains group.

title: Kagamil
fact: Stratovolcano, 893 m in United States. Last erupted 1929. Kagamil Island lies near the NE end of the Islands of the Four Mountains archipelago in the central Aleutians, between Chuginadak and Uliaga Islands.

title: Chiginagak
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,221 m in United States. Last erupted 1998. The symmetrical, glaciated Chiginagak stratovolcano located on the Alaska Peninsula ~15 km NW of Chiginagak Bay contains a small summit crater, which is breached to the south, and one or more summit lava domes.

title: Barcena
fact: Pyroclastic cone, 332 m in Mexico. Last erupted 1953. Volcán Bárcena, formed by eruptions during 1952-53, is the most prominent feature of the 4.5-km-long Isla San Benedicto, the NE-most of the Revillagigedo Islands, 350 km S of the tip of Baja California.

title: Planchon-Peteroa
fact: Stratovolcano, 3,977 m in Chile. Last erupted 2025. Planchón-Peteroa is an elongated complex volcano along the Chile-Argentina border with several overlapping calderas.

title: Longonot
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,776 m in Kenya. Last erupted 1863. The trachytic Longonot stratovolcano SE of Lake Naivasha in the Gregory Rift valley contains a 8 x 12 km caldera. Formation of the caldera accompanied large explosive eruptions about 21,000 years ago.

title: Merbabu
fact: Stratovolcano, 3,118 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 1797. Gunung Merbabu is a massive forested volcano north of Merapi in central Java. Three prominent radial valleys extend from the summit toward the NW, NNE, and ESE.

title: Quilotoa
fact: Caldera, 3,914 m in Ecuador. Last erupted 1280. Quilotoa is a truncated, dacitic cone in the Western Cordillera of Ecuador, 35 km WNW of the city of Latacunga, that contains a 3-km-wide caldera with steep-sided walls that rise 400 m above the surface of 240-m-deep caldera lake.

title: Aogashima
fact: Stratovolcano, 423 m in Japan. Last erupted 1785. The small 2.5 x 3.5 km dominantly basaltic island of Aogashima is surrounded by steep cliffs and contains a small 1.7 x 1.5-km-wide caldera.

title: Barrier, The
fact: Shield volcano, 1,032 m in Kenya. Last erupted 1921. The Barrier volcanic complex separates Lake Turkana from the broad Suguta Trough to the S, the site of a former lake.

title: Lateiki
fact: Stratovolcano, 43 m in Tonga. Last erupted 2019. Lateiki, previously known as Metis Shoal, is a submarine volcano midway between the islands of Kao and Late that has produced a series of ephemeral islands since the first confirmed activity in the mid-19th century.

title: Witori
fact: Caldera, 724 m in Papua New Guinea. Last erupted 2012. The active Pago cone has grown within the Witori caldera (5.5 x 7.5 km) on the northern coast of central New Britain contains the active Pago cone.

title: Ranakah
fact: Lava dome, 2,288 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 1991. The Anak Ranakah (Child of Ranakah) lava dome was formed in 1987 in an area without previous recorded eruptions at the base of the large older lava dome of Gunung Ranakah.

title: Inielika
fact: Complex volcano, 1,559 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 2001. Inielika is a broad, low volcano in central Flores Island that was constructed within the Lobobutu caldera.

title: Iliwerung
fact: Complex volcano, 583 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 2021. Constructed on the southern rim of the Lerek caldera, Iliwerung forms a prominent south-facing peninsula on Lembata Island.

title: Ragang
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,790 m in Philippines. Last erupted 1916. The large Ragang stratovolcano, also called Piapayungan, is SE of Lake Lanao in central Mindanao.

title: Chillan, Nevados de
fact: Stratovolcano, 3,180 m in Chile. Last erupted 2022. The compound volcano of Nevados de Chillán is one of the most active of the Central Andes.

title: Savo
fact: Stratovolcano, 455 m in Solomon Islands. Last erupted 1847. The 6 x 7 km island of Savo, off the NE coast of Guadalcanal Island, consists of a forested andesitic-to-dacitic stratovolcano with a shallow, elliptical 1 x 1.5 km summit crater.

title: Ilopango
fact: Caldera, 450 m in El Salvador. Last erupted 1880. The 8 x 11 km Ilopango caldera, filled by one of El Salvador's largest lakes, has a scalloped 150-500 m high rim.

title: Furnas
fact: Stratovolcano, 805 m in Portugal. Last erupted 1630. Furnas volcano lies at the eastern end of Sao Miguel Island, immediately west of the older Nordeste shield volcano and its Povoaçao caldera.

title: Melbourne
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,732 m in Antarctica. Last erupted 1892. Mount Melbourne is a large undissected stratovolcano along the western coast of the Ross Sea in Antarctica's northern Victoria Land.

title: Chaine des Puys
fact: Lava dome, 1,464 m in France. Last erupted 4,040 BCE. The Chaîne des Puys, prominent in the history of volcanology, form a N-S-trending chain of basaltic and trachytic cinder cones, basaltic maars…

title: Karisimbi
fact: Stratovolcano, 4,490 m in DR Congo-Rwanda. Last erupted 8,050 BCE. Karisimbi is a complex basanitic-to-trachytic volcano with a symmetrical sharp-peaked summit. The 2-km-wide Branca caldera, located SE of the summit, is filled by viscous lava flows and two explosion craters.

title: Parinacota
fact: Stratovolcano, 6,336 m in Chile-Bolivia. Last erupted 290 CE. The symmetrical Volcán Parinacota is the southernmost and youngest of a pair of volcanoes forming the Nevados de Payachata group along the Chile-Bolivia border.

title: Zubair Group
fact: Shield volcano, 191 m in Yemen. Last erupted 2013. The 5-km-long Jebel Zubair Island is the largest of a group of small islands and submerged shoals that rise from a shallow platform in the Red Sea rift.

title: Flores
fact: Stratovolcano, 914 m in Portugal. Last erupted 950 BCE. Flores Island and Corvo Island to its north are located over 200 km W of the other Azores islands, west of the Mid-Atlantic Ridge.

title: Kao
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,009 m in Tonga. Last erupted 1847. The symmetrical Kao rises steeply from the ocean about 6 km N of Tofua Island in Tonga. It is elongated NNE-SSW and, with the exception of a small flat area on the SSW coast, rises at angles exceeding 35° to the summit…

title: Ofu-Olosega
fact: Shield volcano, 639 m in United States. Last erupted 1866. The two triangle-shaped islands of Ofu and Olosega in eastern Samoa, with a combined length of 6 km, are separated by a narrow strait.

title: Ichinsky
fact: Stratovolcano, 3,596 m in Russia. Last erupted 1740. Ichinsky, by far the highest peak in the Sredinny Range, is a massive, 450 km3 edifice. The andesitic Pleistocene-to-Holocene stratovolcano, also known as Icha…

title: Atitlan
fact: Stratovolcano, 3,535 m in Guatemala. Last erupted 1853. Volcán Atitlán is one of several conical stratovolcanoes in the Guatemalan highlands. Along with Tolimán to the north, it forms a dramatic backdrop to Lake Atitlán.

title: Manda-Inakir
fact: Fissure vent, 600 m in Ethiopia-Djibouti. Last erupted 1928. Manda-Inakir consists of a series of NW-trending fissure vents and pyroclastic cones along the Ethiopia-Djibouti border.

title: Kaba
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,962 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 2000. The Kaba volcanic massif is ~8 km long, elongated WSW-ENE, with a summit area that includes multiple large craters.

title: Sangeang Api
fact: Complex volcano, 1,912 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 2022. Sangeang Api volcano, one of the most active in the Lesser Sunda Islands, forms a small 13-km-wide island off the NE coast of Sumbawa Island.

title: Zavaritzki Caldera
fact: Caldera, 612 m in Russia. Last erupted 1957. The Zavaritzki volcano on Simushir Island in the central Kuril Islands contains three nested calderas 10, 8, and 3 km in diameter.

title: Westdahl
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,563 m in United States. Last erupted 1992. Westdahl is a broad glacier-covered volcano occupying the SW end of Unimak Island. Two peaks protrude from the summit plateau, and a new crater formed in 1978 cuts the summit icecap.

title: Mocho-Choshuenco
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,422 m in Chile. Last erupted 1937. The compound Mocho-Choshuenco volcano is composed of two glacier-covered stratovolcanoes, located east of Lago Rinihué and SE of Lago Panguipulli and post-dating a 4-km-wide basaltic caldera.

title: Kussharo
fact: Caldera, 574 m in Japan. Last erupted 1320. The 20 x 26 km Kussharo caldera, is the largest of a cluster of calderas in NE Hokkaido. The caldera was formed in a series of major eruptions between about 340,000 and 30,000 years ago.

title: Banua Wuhu
fact: Complex volcano, -5 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 1919. The submarine Banua Wuhu volcanic cone lies ~600 m off the western coast of Mahengatang Island, the emergent summit of a large submarine edifice, in the Sangihe Islands.

title: Ulleungdo
fact: Stratovolcano, 984 m in South Korea. Last erupted 2,990 BCE. Ulleungdo, also known as Ulreungdo, is a 10-km-wide island about 100 km E of the central Korean Peninsula. The trachyandesitic stratovolcano is truncated by the Nari caldera.

title: Graciosa
fact: Stratovolcano, 402 m in Portugal. Last erupted 1,950 BCE. The SE end of Graciosa, the northernmost of the central Azorean islands, contains a 0.9 x 1.6 km caldera with active fumaroles. The SE caldera rim is the high point of the 7 x 12 km island.

title: Guguan
fact: Stratovolcano, 232 m in United States. Last erupted 1883. The island of Guguan, ~2.8 km in diameter, is composed of an eroded volcano on the south, a caldera with a post-caldera cone, and a northern volcano.

title: Taisetsuzan
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,291 m in Japan. Last erupted 1739. The Taisetsuzan volcano group lies at the northern end of the Taisetsu-Tokachi graben in central Hokkaido. It consists of a complex of stratovolcanoes and lava domes associated with a 2-km-wide caldera.

title: Cosiguina
fact: Stratovolcano, 872 m in Nicaragua. Last erupted 1859. Cosigüina is a low basaltic-to-andesitic composite volcano that is isolated from other eruptive centers in the Nicaraguan volcanic chain.

title: Manda Hararo
fact: Shield volcano, 600 m in Ethiopia. Last erupted 2009. As the southernmost axial range of western Afar, the Manda Hararo complex is located in the Kalo plain, SSE of Dabbahu volcano.

title: Didicas
fact: Compound volcano, 228 m in Philippines. Last erupted 1978. Didicas, 22 km NE of Camiguin Island in the Babuyanes Islands north of Luzon, was a submarine volcano prior to 1952, when a permanent island was formed.

title: Kikai
fact: Caldera, 704 m in Japan. Last erupted 2025. Multiple eruption centers have exhibited recent activity at Kikai, a mostly submerged, 19-km-wide caldera near the northern end of the Ryukyu Islands south of Kyushu.

title: Akita-Yakeyama
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,366 m in Japan. Last erupted 1997. One of several Japanese volcanoes named Yakeyama ("Burning Mountain"), Akita-Yakeyama is the most recently active of a group of coalescing edifices in NW Honshu immediately west of Hachimantai volcano.
